For example, we show that a blend of MOGREPS-UK with either AIFS-CRPS or the physics-based Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) is better than a blend of IFS and AIFS-CRPS which are not very diverse. This has implications for the importance of weather model diversity and may lend weight to different model development approaches being pursued in tandem. We also demonstrate that calibrating AIFS-CRPS forecasts yields an increase in forecast skill comparable to calibrated ensemble physics-based forecasts, and calibrating the source forecasts before blending and the blended forecast after blending improves the overall forecast accuracy.

papers.title: Fewer Heads, Fewer Memories: Pruning Redundant Attention Heads Suppresses Verbatim Memorisation
papers.abstract: Large language models have been shown to memorise and reproduce verbatim sequences from their training data, raising concerns about privacy leakage, intellectual property exposure, and the limits of generalisation. Recent theoretical work suggests that attention heads may contribute to this behaviour by functioning as associative memory mechanisms, with memorisation capacity scaling with the number of heads. At the same time, empirical work has shown that many attention heads are redundant and can be pruned with limited impact on downstream performance. Despite these parallel findings, the effect of pruning redundant heads on memorised-sequence reproduction remains unexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that zeroing out a substantial fraction of attention heads prior to inference can significantly suppress verbatim memorisation while preserving, or even improving, language modelling performance on the benchmark used to identify redundant heads. Evaluating GPT-2-XL(1.5B) on known memorised sequences, we find that pruning 729 task-redundant heads reduces the memorisation count by 91.5%, while improving WikiText-103 perplexity by 0.92. These findings suggest that attention-head redundancy can be exploited to mitigate memorisation at inference time, without retraining or modifying the training data.

papers.title: MOSAIC: Addressing Disproportionate Task-Modality Dependencies via Modality-Partitioned Gradient Routing
papers.abstract: In multi-task settings, combining multiple modalities allows task representations to draw on signals that a single modality alone would not capture. However, individual tasks may depend disproportionately on particular modalities, a structure that conventional fusion-based architectures do not model explicitly, instead enforcing a unified representation space. Consequently, a task's gradients can affect parameters tied to modalities it barely relies on, leaving features that compromise between competing demands. Although prior work has explored task-weighting and loss-balancing strategies, their effectiveness is limited by the absence of explicit modality separation, preventing models from optimising each modality according to its task-specific importance. To address these limitations, we propose MOSAIC (MOdality-Separated Architecture with Inter-modal Cross-attention), which preserves unimodal representations while enabling controlled interaction between them, and uses modality-specific losses to route gradients to their corresponding partitions. On the Corpus of Everyday Japanese Conversation (CEJC), MOSAIC improves average macro-F1 by 7.4 points across four tasks with a 72% reduction in backbone parameters relative to a fusion-based baseline. Our results demonstrate that modality partitioning yields consistent gains across tasks while requiring far fewer backbone parameters than a fusion-based design.

papers.title: ARK: Avoiding Routing Collisions for KV Cache Transfer in Disaggregated LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Disaggregated LLM inference separates the prefill and decode phases across GPU pools, generating massive KV-cache transfers. Because these transfers last hundreds of milliseconds to seconds, they behave as mega elephant flows that dominate link bandwidth utilization. In this regime, stateless ECMP can perform poorly: hash collisions may overload one spine link while leaving others idle, stretching transfer times by seconds. Yet this same persistence makes coordination practical. Since these flows are long-lived, even lightweight one-to-all coordination can be amortized over their lifetime. We present ARK, a distributed elephant-flow path reservation mechanism. ARK coordinates senders to choose source ports whose hashes map concurrent flows onto distinct spines, without requiring switch changes or receiver-side packet reordering. Packet-level RDMA simulations show that ARK reduces mean and P95 FCT by up to 27.3% and 34.0% under moderate load, and further reduces mean TTFT by up to 12.9%.

papers.title: Focusing through coupled multimode fibers for miniaturized single-atom tweezer arrays
papers.abstract: Real-world deployment of quantum technologies requires systems in low SWaP-C packages. Quantum platforms based on ultracold atoms typically trap and control atoms with optical tweezers using light focused through bulky objective lenses, which are costly and sensitive to misalignment. Multimode fibers (MMFs) offer a compact route to focusing light, but their use in forming optical tweezers for cold atoms has been limited to a single fiber. Here we use a 2x1 MMF fused coupler to obtain two independent control paths sharing a common distal facet. We form near-diffraction-limited tweezers through each channel, suppress interference by applying a small frequency offset between the channels, and demonstrate that the tweezer separation is insensitive to misalignment of the input coupling. This work provides a route to reconfigurable single-atom arrays in low SWaP-C environments.

papers.title: Spectral Convergence of the Discrete Steklov Problem
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Schur complement $\textbf{S}$ of the graph Laplacian, defined on vertices sampled from a domain with $C^2$ boundary. We use a thin boundary layer to approximate the continuum boundary as the number of vertices increases and rely on transportation theory to justify the consistency of a discrete Steklov problem. In particular, $\textbf{S}$ acts on vectors defined over the shrinking boundary layer but behaves asymptotically like a known operator. In this paper, we use a variational argument to determine conditions for which the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of $\textbf{S}$ converge to the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a Dirichlet-to-Neumann map, and we provide evidence of this spectral convergence through a numerical example.

papers.title: Beyond CLIP: Calibrated (Few-Shot) Defect Detection With System One Decision Models
papers.abstract: Cameras and vision sensors are widely used for product and process inspection in manufacturing environments. Traditionally, this process required thousands of images of both nominal and defective products to train such models. Recent research shows that vision transformer (ViT) models, such as CLIP, can reduce this requirement to 50-100 images per nominal and defective class. However, collecting even 50 defective images can be difficult in high-yield or low-volume manufacturing processes. In this paper, we examine the utility of two recently proposed structured decision models (Jev and Clef-Flash) in applications using as few as k=2 reference images per class at inference. In the process, we provide three main contributions: (a) a framework for k-shot learning of these models for image classification/inspection applications; (b) an agentic approach for automatically refining the text descriptions that guide image classification in these decision models; and (c) an approach to calibrate the resulting defect probabilities to improve their reliability for inspection decisions. We test these contributions in five manufacturing case studies. Using two reference images per class, both Jev and Clef-Flash outperform CLIP's test accuracies with the same references (0.75-1.00 [Jev] and 0.71-0.99 [Clef-Flash] vs 0.67-0.84 [CLIP]). Furthermore, we show that our agentic refinement of text descriptions significantly improves accuracy across 6 of 8 model-application combinations, and our calibration approach reduces the Brier score in 13 of the 15 model-application configurations. To support the reproducibility of our work, we provide our replication code and have created the R "decisions" package for evaluating additional models. We also provide a publicly available web app that allows practitioners to inspect their own images with no code.

papers.title: Disconnectedness of stability manifolds and their geometric loci, and separation of braid orbits of semiorthogonal decompositions
papers.abstract: This paper proves that the Bridgeland stability manifold $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ has infinitely many connected components for general quintic threefolds, other general complete intersection Calabi--Yau threefolds, certain odd-dimensional Calabi--Yau varieties, and certain rational weak Fano varieties. Moreover, we show that the geometric locus $\mathrm{Stab}^{\mathrm{geo}}(X)$ meets distinct connected components of $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ for general quintic threefolds and their products with varieties with finite Albanese morphisms, which gives examples in any dimension at least three. For the weak Fano examples, we also construct semiorthogonal decompositions in infinitely many braid group orbits. The proof is an extension of Nordskova's argument to families, using semilinear autoequivalences and absolute Galois actions on geometric generic fibers to permute mutually orthogonal spherical objects. Then, we specialize the separation to closed fibers. In our examples, the spherical objects are constructed from rigid rational curves or spinor bundles on quadrics.

papers.title: Suspense and surprise in matroid bingo
papers.abstract: We present the game of Matroid Bingo and prove that it gets more suspenseful the longer the game goes on.

papers.title: Dreams Are Cheaper Than Flights: Curated World-Model Data Improves Aerial Detection
papers.abstract: Robot perception is increasingly data driven, yet field data is slow, costly, and sometimes disruptive to collect. Video world models offer a cheaper source: seeded with real frames, they extend a recorded scene into new footage with the deployment's sensor, altitude, and environment. We ask whether such synthetic data matches the utility of real field data and whether detectors trained with it perform in the field. Seeding a 7B-parameter world model with wildlife drone video, we more than double the training set with curated frames. On held-out videos from the same drones, mAP@50--95 rises 4.3\% when these frames are added to real data and 10.3\% when they replace it, and up to 33.5\% on an urban benchmark. Although an expert rejects an estimated 87.5\% of generated clips, the data costs about \$1,100 of GPU time, against more than \$3,200 of field labor alone for a less useful real training set. Synthetic data thus shifts data costs from fieldwork to compute.

papers.title: On the factorization graph of finite groups
papers.abstract: Given a finite group $G$, the factorization graph $\Gamma(G)$ has as vertices the nontrivial proper subgroups of $G$, with two distinct vertices $H$ and $K$ adjacent if and only if $HK = G$. In this paper, we study structural and combinatorial properties of $\Gamma(G)$ for three families of groups: cyclic groups of square-free order, generalized quaternion groups, and dicyclic groups. For cyclic groups $C_{p_1\cdots p_r}$, we describe the global structure of $\Gamma(G)$ and determine its order, degree sequence, center, girth, and diameter. We also characterize completely when $\Gamma(G)$ is claw-free, show that it is non-planar for $r \geq 4$, and prove that after removing all pendant vertices, the resulting induced subgraph is 2-connected; we further compute its exact circumference for small $r$, showing it is Hamiltonian precisely when $r=4, 5$. For generalized quaternion groups, we classify all isolated vertices and prove that the reduced factorization graph has diameter two and a unique central vertex. Moreover, we show that it is planar, has chromatic number~$3$, is Eulerian, and non-Hamiltonian, and that it contains maximal induced stars and triangular book subgraphs. Finally, we analyze the dicyclic case and show that the reduced factorization graph is a complete bipartite graph, from which all main invariants follow directly. An explicit SageMath algorithm for constructing $\Gamma(G)$ is included.

authors.name: Yesneri Zuleta y E. J. Garcia-Claro

papers.title: Robust Opinion Maximization
papers.abstract: Opinion-formation models are fundamental for analyzing social behavior and understanding social dynamics. The Friedkin-Johnsen (FJ) model is the most commonly used model in this line of research. In FJ, the expressed opinion of an individual evolves over time as the combination of the opinions of their peers and a fixed inner opinion, weighted by their stubbornness. A problem that has received considerable attention is the problem of Opinion Maximization, where the goal is to adjust the parameters of the FJ model, such as stubbornness, or inner opinions, to maximize the average expressed opinion, i.e., the public opinion. Most existing work assumes full knowledge of the parameters of the model, which is unrealistic. In this paper, we introduce the problem of Robust Opinion Maximization, where we assume uncertainty for the inner opinions of the nodes, and we maximize the public opinion under worst-case assumptions on this uncertainty. Using tools from Robust Optimization, we formulate our problem as a max-min problem, and we develop an optimal two-step solution that is both highly intuitive and efficient. Experiments on several real-world networks demonstrate that our approach can achieve robust solutions for million-node graphs in minutes, and reveal that our robust strategies can significantly mitigate the impact of noise compared to standard baselines.

papers.title: Not Everyone Has a Voice, or an Ear, on Social Media: The Poster-Observer Model of Opinion Dynamics
papers.abstract: Classic modeling of opinion dynamics via the Friedkin-Johnsen (FJ) model relies on the unrealistic assumption of synchronous communication among network users. Social media, however, exhibit extreme participation asymmetries: a vast majority of users silently observe, while a tiny minority creates and broadcasts most of the content. To capture this reality, we introduce the Poster-Observer FJ (PO-FJ) model, which decouples user communication into distinct posting and observing behaviors. This formulation fundamentally alters network dynamics by preventing convergence to a static equilibrium, driving opinions into perpetual oscillations. We establish closed-form expressions for these new dynamics and generalize classic metrics of public opinion, polarization, and disagreement under the PO-FJ model. By leveraging the novel Poster-Observer dynamics, we introduce a realistic and scalable intervention algorithm for conflict mitigation. Through experiments on synthetic and real-world networks, we demonstrate the efficacy and efficiency of our approach in reducing social-network conflict.

papers.title: Cutting out the middleman? Elon Musk and the rhetoric of citizen journalism in platform-mediated communication
papers.abstract: This article examines how Elon Musk constructed discourse about journalism and the media on X between the 2024 United States presidential election and Donald Trump's presidential inauguration. It investigates how references to journalism, media organisations, and platform-based communication were articulated within Musk's posts, and how users responded to these narratives during a period of intense political polarisation. The study combines computational classification, qualitative thematic coding, and inferential statistical analysis. A corpus of 2,906 posts published by Musk between 5 November 2024 and 20 January 2025 was compiled. From this corpus, 500 posts referring to journalism, media organisations, platforms, or media-related discourse were identified through AI-assisted filtering and subsequent manual review. In addition, 42,066 user responses were analysed from a stratified sample drawn from 3,233,112 interactions. The analysis examined patterns of agreement and disagreement with Musk's stance and their relationship with thematic, gender, and professional variables inferred from publicly available profile information. The findings show that Musk's discourse is organised around three recurrent dynamics: criticism of institutional journalism, the association of media organisations with political and ideological agendas, and the presentation of X as an alternative communicative space. Journalism is predominantly framed through accusations of bias, disinformation, propaganda, and electoral manipulation, whereas X is more often linked to participation, innovation, and direct communication. User responses largely converged with Musk's position, although disagreement remained visible. While thematic orientation and professional background showed statistically significant associations with agreement patterns, effect sizes were limited.

papers.title: Advancing Clinical Trial Outcome Prediction with Domain-Specific Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Clinical trial failures are a major barrier to efficient drug development, incurring substantial costs and delaying patient access to effective therapies. Structured approaches such as the Hierarchical Interaction Network (HINT) predict trial outcomes by explicitly modelling interactions between drugs, diseases and protocols, but make limited use of the free text in trial registrations. We evaluate two domain-specific language models, BioBERT (108M parameters) and BioMistral (7B parameters), for phase-level outcome prediction on the TOP benchmark (12,477 trials), representing each trial as text built from ten ClinicalTrials.gov fields. We compare fine-tuning (full fine-tuning for BioBERT, low-rank adaptation for BioMistral) with probing, in which the pretrained model is frozen and only a lightweight classifier is trained on its embeddings. On the held-out test set of each phase, all four language-model variants achieved higher ROC-AUC (0.613--0.772) and PR-AUC (0.649--0.901) than the published HINT results, corresponding to relative PR-AUC gains of 10--20\%. F1 differences were small and mixed, and no model, including HINT, clearly exceeded the F1 of a trivial classifier that predicts success for every trial. Under the configurations tested, probing performed comparably to fine-tuning: fine-tuned models scored highest on ROC-AUC and PR-AUC in Phases I and II, and frozen BioMistral embeddings in Phase III (ROC-AUC 0.772; PR-AUC 0.901), although most differences between variants were below 0.03 and were not tested for significance. These results suggest that pretrained biomedical representations already encode signal relevant to trial outcome, and that probing is a computationally cheaper alternative to fine-tuning for this task.

papers.title: CAMEL: Cross-Architecture Masked Embedding Learning for Ultra-Lightweight Retinal Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Recent progress in deep learning has substantially advanced automated grading of ophthalmologic pathologies, supported by large annotated datasets and improved representation learning. However, a significant gap remains between state-of-the-art performance and clinical scalability. In particular, foundation models have reshaped image-based medical screening and diagnosis. These large-scale architectures trained on extensive datasets learn rich, generalizable feature representations that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks. In ophthalmology, RETFound, one of the most relevant foundation models for retinal images, performs strongly across classification, segmentation, and risk prediction tasks. Despite their effectiveness, foundation models are often computationally prohibitive, hindering their deployment in real-world clinical environments where hardware constraints and latency are critical. To bridge this gap, we introduce CAMEL (Cross-Architecture Masked Embedding Learning), a novel cross-architecture distillation framework that uses an asymmetric masking strategy during embedding learning to effectively transfer knowledge from massive teacher foundation models to compact, lightweight student models. Our experimental evaluation across four datasets shows that CAMEL preserves accuracy while drastically reducing computational complexity, enabling lightweight yet highly accurate models suitable for resource-limited clinical settings.

authors.name: Giovani Decico Lucafo
authors.institution: Institute of Mathematics and Computer Science

papers.title: Ultraviolet Raman spectroscopy using multimode aluminum oxide waveguides
papers.abstract: Waveguide-based Raman spectroscopy offers a route toward compact and integrated photonic sensors. While most waveguide Raman platforms operate in the near-infrared, extending excitation toward the visible and ultraviolet is attractive because shorter excitation wavelengths can provide substantially stronger Raman scattering and access to resonance-enhanced molecular responses. This transition, however, places greater demands on the photonic material because of optical loss, absorption and waveguide-generated spectral background. Here, we investigate aluminum oxide ($Al_2O_3$) waveguides as a low-background platform for Raman spectroscopy at 532 nm and 325 nm using a back-collected excitation and detection geometry. At 532 nm, after normalization to the incident excitation power-time product, the measured $Al_2O_3$ background was more than two orders of magnitude lower than that of $Si_3N_4$. Under 325 nm excitation, the waveguides maintained a weak and reproducible spectral background across the investigated widths. Using immersion oil as a model analyte deposited over the waveguide surface, we demonstrate that analyte-specific Raman fingerprints can be recovered above the waveguide background at both wavelengths. Signal-to-background ratio and spectral contrast were used to quantify analyte visibility relative to the waveguide background, and both metrics consistently confirmed clear detection of the analyte bands. These results demonstrate that $Al_2O_3$ combines low measured spectral background with operation from the visible into the ultraviolet, providing a promising route toward integrated Raman spectroscopy at shorter excitation wavelengths.

authors.name: Roman Zakoldaev
authors.institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

authors.name: Nikhil Jayakumar
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

authors.name: Jean-Claude Tinguely
authors.institution: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

papers.title: Higher-Order Kinematic Derivatives for Aspect-Preserving Real-Time Numerical Inverse Kinematics
papers.abstract: This paper leverages the higher-order kinematic derivatives of serial robots to achieve efficient, aspect-preserving real-time inverse kinematics. First, a family of higher-order solvers is derived, with a necessary orientation-error correction map, yielding the QuIK4 and QuIK5 methods with fourth- and fifth-order convergence. Second, an aspect-preserving step limiter extrapolates the Jacobian determinant along the step to predict and avoid singularities, shortening steps only when they head toward a singularity rather than when the current iterate is ill-conditioned. Third, a Hermite-interpolation certifier verifies the aspect of each answer, and a certified restart algorithm recovers failures from proven same-aspect seeds. The proposed methods are shown to outperform prior methods, reducing failures by up to four orders of magnitude and nearly eliminating aspect switching at tracking-level errors. A C++ library is released with ROS 2 integration.

papers.title: The full shadow of a polynomial II. Vanishing root masses and holes
papers.abstract: For a complex polynomial $P$, its full shadow is the closure of the set of zeros of all derivatives of all powers $P^n$, and its limiting core is the Hausdorff limit, as $n\to\infty$, of the set of zeros of all derivatives of $P^n$. These sets retain geometric information that weak limits of root-counting measures discard. We determine complete zero-set limits for arrays of polynomials whose roots approach finitely many locations. A cluster containing $o(D)$ roots of a degree-$D$ polynomial can survive outside the limiting support of the derivative zeros, which depends only on the positive limiting masses: under repeated differentiation, the zeros it produces follow a straight path, selected by an explicit min--max condition, and preserve the cluster's exact multiplicity. When such a location instead carries a small positive mass $\varepsilon$, the support of the limiting zero distribution at a fixed ratio of derivative order to degree develops an arc on the $\sqrt{\varepsilon}$ scale with a universal local semicircle profile. We use these mechanisms to prove that polynomial shadows can have robust and arbitrarily complicated topology. For every $k\ge2$, there are polynomials with $k+2$ distinct root locations whose limiting cores and full shadows have at least $\binom{k}{2}$ holes; this persists under coefficient perturbations and among square-free polynomials without a reflection axis. In a four-location family, the core and full-shadow areas tend to zero while one hole has area tending to $8/1221$.

papers.title: Coarse-Graining Optimal Transport for Rollout-Free Post-Training of Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Flow matching depends critically on the coupling used to pair source and target samples. Optimal transport (OT) couplings can reduce velocity conflict and straighten trajectories; but, in practice, challenges remain: the source comes from a continuous distribution, only a finite number of target samples data are accessible, and the neural network has finite capacity. For these reasons, making the coupling more OT-like may not consistently improve sampling quality, in particular in the low number-of-function-evaluation (NFE) regime. Motivated by this, we introduce ReCouple, a controllable framework that constructs coarse-grained OT couplings, to better understand rollout-free OT-based post-training. We also consider extensions of this basic framework: ReCouple+ extends this toward the continuous-source setting by increasing source resolution, converging to semi-discrete OT in the appropriate limit; and ReCouple++ further adds spatial regularization, motivated by the observation that straight trajectories need not correspond to spatially simple velocity fields. Empirical validation demonstrates the effectiveness of these methods, and it reveals an NFE-dependent interplay between coupling optimality, neural realizability, and generation quality.

papers.title: RadioTraj3D: Height-Aware Adaptive Sampling for 3D Radio-Map Reconstruction from Ultra-Sparse Trajectories
papers.abstract: Aerial networks require radio propagation information at unvisited positions and heights to plan routes, select links, and allocate wireless resources. A three-dimensional radio map (3D RM) represents propagation conditions over the service area, enabling these decisions before flight. However, constructing such a map from autonomous aerial vehicle (AAV) measurements is challenging, since radio measurements are available only along the trajectory, whereas the target covers the 3D service volume. Existing methods use fixed AAV trajectories that ignore how building distributions and heights affect electromagnetic propagation, missing the heights most informative for RM reconstruction. To address these issues, we propose RadioTraj3D, which uses building-height information to coordinate measurement selection and layer-wise reconstruction. Building-height variations reveal propagation-sensitive layers that guide height-adaptive sampling. We therefore propose G-METS to select geometry-sensitive heights and allocate an exact budget across edge, corridor, and open regions before channel acquisition. A dual-view reconstructor then integrates local three-dimensional boundaries with full-height context through one bounded coefficient per layer. Simulated outdoor and indoor maps demonstrate state-of-the-art reconstruction across environments and vertical grids. On real-world AAV measurements from the LACN dataset, RadioTraj3D improves peak signal-to-noise ratio by 0.84 dB and reduces normalized mean squared error by 17.5% over Completion AE.

authors.name: Xiucheng Wang
authors.institution: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

authors.name: Conghao Zhou
authors.institution: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

papers.title: ID2Pattern: Pretraining Generalizable Identity Behavior Patterns for Transaction Risk Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Large-scale behavioral pretraining offers a promising route to generalizable representations in online payment systems. However, high-cardinality identity fields such as card, device, and account IDs, though rich in behavioral signals, remain underexploited. Their continually growing vocabularies and limited semantic meaning make existing vocabulary-based and semantics-based encodings ill-suited. Their generalizable signal lies not in specific values, but in the identity behavior patterns they exhibit across a transaction sequence. Building on this insight, we propose ID2Pattern, a pretraining framework that brings these patterns into transaction foundation models. ID2Pattern first encodes identity fields with a Local Anonymous ID (LAID) tokenizer, which captures how each identity appears and recurs within the sequence, independent of its specific value. It then pretrains a multi-scale pattern codebook on unlabeled sequences, which abstracts LAID sequences into discrete behavior patterns for downstream prediction. Experiments on an industrial dataset with over 100M sequences and six public datasets show that ID2Pattern consistently outperforms strong baselines, improving industrial by 4.13% and public datasets by 8.83% on average. Notably, ID2Pattern remains equally effective even when all identity values are unseen during training, highlighting its potential to generalize to new users and markets.

authors.name: Ze Zhao
authors.institution: Inner Mongolia University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Generation and spectroscopic characterization of continuous-wave 148.4-nm light in strontium tetraborate
papers.abstract: Continuous-wave (CW) radiation at 148.4~nm is required to drive the $^{229}$Th isomeric transition of a solid-state nuclear clock, and frequency doubling of 296.8-nm light is its most direct source. We generate CW 148.4-nm light by random quasi-phase matching in strontium tetraborate and characterize it with a compact prism spectrometer built for the purpose. The spectrometer separates the harmonic from the pump on a CaF$_2$ prism, reads the wavelength from the rotation angle of a solar-blind photomultiplier, resolves the two lines with $\delta\lambda \approx 0.6~nm$, and yields an absolute power calibration. At room temperature the source delivers $1.9~nW$ at 148.4~nm, rising to 5.7 nW at the optimum crystal temperature. The conversion efficiency is also strongly structured in temperature: between 30 degree and 50 degree it shows several pronounced maxima, with neighbouring extrema only a few degrees apart, so that a small temperature excursion moves the output from a maximum to a minimum. These results provide practical guidance for optimizing and stabilizing 148.4-nm sources for solid-state $^{229}$Th nuclear clocks.

authors.name: Xiaojun Liu
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Advanced Microstructures

papers.title: Inviscid limit for the hyperbolic Keller--Segel equations in $B_{\infty,1}^{1}$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the inviscid limit for the hyperbolic Keller--Segel equations with logistic sensitivity $1-u$. We establish a common existence time and a priori estimates uniform with respect to the diffusion coefficient in the critical Besov spaces $B_{p,1}^{1+d/p}(R^d)$ with $1\le p\le\infty$. For $1<p<\infty$, we obtain explicit convergence rates in $B_{p,1}^{0}$, and we also give estimates for the case $p=1$. For initial data in $B_{\infty,1}^{1}$, we prove convergence at rate $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$ in $L^\infty$, a bound of order $O(\varepsilon^{1/2}\log(e/\varepsilon))$ in $B_{\infty,1}^{0}$, and strong convergence in $L^\infty(0,T;B_{\infty,1}^{1})$. Additional regularity of the initial data yields improved convergence rates. We construct a fixed initial datum showing that the exponent $1/2$ in $L^\infty$ is optimal.

papers.title: WASABI: Wasserstein Sampling via Bridge Interpolants
papers.abstract: Sampling from Boltzmann distributions is a fundamental problem in physics, chemistry, and biology. We introduce WAsserstein SAmpling via Bridge Interpolants (WASABI), a method that trains a diffusion model to generate samples from a target Boltzmann distribution given access only to the energy function. WASABI minimizes the KL divergence between the distribution generated by its diffusion model and the Boltzmann target using Wasserstein gradient flows. This approach builds on a principle underlying classical sampling methods such as Langevin dynamics. However, applying Wasserstein gradient flows to diffusion models is challenging because the updates require the gradient of the model's own log density, which is generally intractable. We derive a practical training algorithm that avoids computing this gradient. Once trained, WASABI can generate new samples without further evaluations of the energy or its gradient. On alanine dipeptide, WASABI outperforms the best reported baselines using an estimated 3.3 times fewer energy evaluations. It also achieves competitive performance on interacting particle system benchmarks.

papers.title: The Dynamical Mass Profiles of Galaxy Groups - Application to IllustrisTNG-300
papers.abstract: We present a new rescaling and stacking method to test cold dark matter predictions through the dynamical modelling of galaxy groups using the Jeans equation. We test the viability of this method on idealised, line-of-sight group data at $z=0$ in the IllustrisTNG-300 simulation, using subhalos and satellite galaxies as tracers. Dynamical mass profiles are measured using the code `Gravsphere' for seven distinct quality cuts, three on the dark matter substructure and four on the `visible' satellite galaxies. When using the dark matter substructure, we find that selecting subhalos by their infall time onto the group provides the best recovery of the true mass profile. When using satellite galaxies we instead find that selecting quenched satellites provides the best recovery. In both cases the mass profile is recovered within $<1\sigma$ of the true value up to $\sim 1.5$ times the median host virial radius. However, we also find the recovered velocity anisotropy to be biased towards negative values for all seven of our subhalo samples beyond the median host virial radius. This suggests dynamical systematics may still be present in the data, which will need to be quantified in future work before application to surveys.

papers.title: AuditFL: A Contract-Backed Clearing Layer for Open Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) keeps raw data local, but most deployments still rely on a trusted coordinator for client admission, checkpoint distribution, update collection, aggregation, and rewards. This paper presents AuditFL, a contract-backed clearing layer for auditable FL in open settings. AuditFL keeps training and aggregation off chain, stores model artifacts in an assumed reliable off-chain artifact store, and records only content identifiers and economic state on chain. Clients reserve update tickets with deposits, publish update identifiers, and later claim refunds or rewards; the task coordinator publishes global checkpoints and finalizes rounds through deterministic settlement rules. The design does not remove the aggregator, but makes its on-chain round decisions attributable, replayable, auditable, and economically constrained. We implement AuditFL as both a deterministic state-machine prototype and a Solidity contract on a local Ethereum-compatible Anvil chain. On full MNIST with Dirichlet non-IID splits, 12 rounds, and up to 200 clients, AuditFL preserves the Plain FL learning trajectory while its overhead follows closed-form control-plane models. At 200 clients, the contract run issues 5,026 transactions, stores 2,413 off-chain artifacts (144.9 MiB), and consumes 829.7M EVM gas, dominated by per-client reserve and publish calls. Controlled dropout, invalid-update, and artifact-unavailability stress tests reduce inclusion nearly linearly but still finalize rounds, with final-accuracy changes remaining within a few tenths of an accuracy percentage point even under high injected failure rates.

papers.title: On the Origin and Evolution of Training-Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: On-policy reinforcement learning for large language models assumes that training responses are sampled from the current policy. In practice, an inference engine samples the responses and a separate trainer computes the gradients, and the \textbf{training-inference mismatch} between the two makes the training data off-policy. The mismatch has two sources, the numerics of the engine and the stale weights of asynchronous sampling, and a correction that stabilizes training under one source can fail under the other. \textit{We ask which property of a mismatch source decides the correction it needs.} Evaluating the trainer at the sampler's weights splits each sampled-token error exactly into a \textit{numerical discrepancy} of the engine and a \textit{policy lag} of the trainer, and we follow both through training. The numerical discrepancy stays approximately constant, so it biases the updates by a nearly fixed amount, and centering the score at each prefix removes its leading bias. The policy lag is produced by the trainer's own updates: the bias it leaves enters the next update, which enlarges the next lag and closes a feedback loop. Importance weighting cuts this loop only while the lag ratio stays concentrated, and on Qwen3-1.7B it fails at the step where the effective sample size of the ratio falls below one half. From this account we derive the \textbf{discrepancy-lag correction} (DLC), which centers the numerical discrepancy, clips the lag ratio against the sampler's weights and resynchronizes the sampler when this effective sample size falls below one half. Under a stale sampler, DLC keeps the KL divergence from on-policy training within twice the KL between two independent on-policy trainings on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B, and its resynchronization prevents collapses that the per-token corrections leave and that a KL measured on the sampler's prefixes does not detect.

papers.title: On the geometry of asymptotically conical Ricci shrinkers (II): strong uniqueness
papers.abstract: We prove strong uniqueness of tangent flows at the first singular time of a closed Ricci flow when one tangent flow is generated by a complete smooth asymptotically conical Ricci shrinker. The modified flow converges to this shrinker in a fixed gauge, with quantitative estimates on expanding domains. The main ingredients are a {\L}ojasiewicz-Simon inequality for Perelman's entropy, based on the global weighted divergence-free gauge constructed in the preceding paper, and estimates controlling the geometric radius under Ricci flow.

papers.title: Clique-factors in randomly perturbed hypergraphs
papers.abstract: In this paper we establish the following result for clique-factors in randomly perturbed hypergraphs when the cliques are large enough. For integers $k \geq 3$ and $t\geq t_0(k)$, we show that for every $\alpha> 0$, there exists $C>0$ such that for sufficiently large $n\in(t+1)\mathbb{N}$, the union of a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with minimum codegree at least $\alpha n$ and a binomial random $k$-uniform hypergraph $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with $p\geq Cn^{-{t/\binom{t+1}{k}}}$ on the same vertex set contains a $K_{t+1}^{(k)}$-factor asymptotically almost surely. The bound on $p$ is asymptotically best possible and extends the graph case, resolved by Balogh, Treglown and Wagner. In particular, we have $t_0(3)=3$, which implies that our result applies to every $t\ge 3$ for $3$-uniform hypergraphs. Together with the previously established result for perfect matchings, this covers all possible clique sizes for $3$-uniform hypergraphs.

authors.name: Jie Han
authors.institution: Research Institute of Petroleum Exploration and Development

papers.title: Numerical analysis of linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze the standard and the mass-lumped linear finite element methods for the Gross--Pitaevskii eigenvalue problem. For the standard method, we give a new proof of the uniqueness of the discrete ground state up to sign for sufficiently small mesh sizes, which only requires the $H^1$-convergence of the discrete ground states. For both methods, we establish optimal convergence rates in the $L^p$- and $W^{1,p}$-norms for $1 \le p < \infty$. Under additional regularity assumptions on the potential, we further obtain an optimal convergence rate in the $W^{1,\infty}$-norm and an almost optimal convergence rate, up to a logarithmic factor, in the $L^\infty$-norm. Moreover, we prove that the discrete ground states superconverge to the Ritz projection of the exact ground state in the $W^{1,p}$-seminorm. The analysis is based on a perturbation argument. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

papers.title: Equation informed time reparametrization for physics informed neural networks
papers.abstract: Physics Informed Neural Networks offer a mesh-free approach to solving differential equations, but their application to time-dependent problems remains challenging, particularly when the governing dynamics involve widely different time scales. With collocation points spread uniformly in time, short intervals of rapid change are under resolved. This work introduces an equation informed time reparameterization framework that modifies the temporal coordinate used during PINN training based on the local dynamics of the governing equation. The proposed method follows a two stage procedure. First, a pilot PINN training provides an approximate solution, which is used to linearize the governing differential operator and estimate its local response to small perturbations. These responses are combined into a time-dependent rate function, large where the dynamics are fast, that defines a strictly increasing transformation from physical time to a new computational time coordinate. A second PINN is then trained on the transformed governing equation, with uniformly sampled collocation points in the new coordinate producing a nonuniform distribution in physical time. Different combination rules and spatial reduction strategies are considered. With the cost of the pilot training included, the method reduces the error by a factor of 4 to 29 relative to the best alternative method on the Kachanov Rabotnov creep-damage model near rupture, and by a factor of 5 to 16 relative to every alternative method on the Frank-Kamenetskii equation near blow up.

papers.title: Trainable Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Vector Quantization (VQ) is a rapidly evolving technique for compressing Large Language Model (LLM) weights, reducing memory usage, and speeding up inference. However, extreme compression deteriorates model performance, which is challenging to recover due to the discrete nature of VQ parameters. Existing methods employ training-free approaches that are limited to layer-wise reconstruction loss minimization. To address this limitation, we propose TVQ, a novel method that leverages straight-through estimation to enable gradient descent-based optimization of vector-quantized LLMs. By reformulating VQ LLM optimization with trainable latent weights, TVQ enables arbitrary objective minimization. We constitute our approach by applying TVQ in a block-wise knowledge distillation paradigm, which balances quality and training efficiency, and propose several practical solutions to accelerate training. In experiments on modern LLMs, we demonstrate that TVQ is compatible with modern VQ schemes. As a result, TVQ achieves state-of-the-art quality in low-bit post-training quantization settings with a modest training budget and straightforward PyTorch implementation. For instance, TVQ achieves near-lossless 2-bit quantization for LLaMA2-70B with only 1% accuracy drop on popular Question-Answering benchmarks.

authors.name: Alina Bogdanova
authors.institution: V.I. Vernadsky Institute of General and Inorganic Chemistry of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine

authors.name: Ilia Zharikov
authors.institution: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

papers.title: SEAMLESS Survey: A Closer Look at Seven Local Volume Dwarf Galaxies in Diverse Environments
papers.abstract: We present Hubble Space Telescope (HST) imaging of six Local Volume dwarf galaxies identified by the SEAMLESS survey - Cetus B, Hydrus A, Ursa Major C, Hydra B, Grapes, and M83-dw14 - along with Centaurus C (Cen C), discovered serendipitously in the M83-dw14 field. We report the discovery of M83-dw14 and Cen C for the first time. Our HST imaging resolves each system into individual stars, enabling measurements of tip of the red giant branch (TRGB) distances (3.6-6.5 Mpc), structural parameters, and star formation histories (SFHs). We complement these data with new HI observations from the Very Large Array for Ursa Major C, Hydra B, and M83-dw14 (also covering Cen C), and from the Green Bank Telescope for Grapes, together with existing HI limits for Cetus B and Hydrus A. With accurate TRGB distances, we place each target in its environmental context, ranging from a confirmed satellite (M83-dw14) to isolated systems (Hydrus A, Hydra B, Grapes, Cen C). Cen C ($M_V=-7.96$) is among the faintest isolated dwarfs known. It matches the size and luminosity of Leo T, the lowest mass gas-rich galaxy currently known, yet unlike Leo T it shows neither detected HI ($\log(M_{\rm HI}/M_{\odot})<5.3$) nor recent star formation. Ursa Major C shows strongly asymmetric, spatially offset HI, suggesting that feedback may efficiently displace gas in such low-mass systems. Overall, our sample exhibits a broad range of SFHs and quenching states that does not track simply with present-day environment. This diversity is consistent with recent evidence that similarly varied SFHs occur even among isolated low-mass dwarfs, pointing to the important roles of inhomogeneous reionization, stochastic mass assembly, and internal feedback alongside environmental effects.

papers.title: Heat trace and Riesz means with a large Robin parameter
papers.abstract: We consider the Laplacian with Robin boundary conditions on a smooth Riemannian manifold with boundary and investigate the behavior of various spectral quantities as the Robin parameter approaches infinity. Although the spectrum, heat trace, and Riesz means converge pointwise to their Dirichlet analogues, the asymptotics of these quantities as the spectral parameter approaches infinity, or as time approaches zero, do not. The remainders in the usual asymptotic expansions are not bounded as the Robin parameter approaches infinity. Our main result is a two-term asymptotic expansion for the Robin heat trace that depends jointly on the time variable and the Robin parameter, with a remainder that satisfies a uniform bound independent of the Robin parameter. We apply this result to obtain a similar two-term asymptotic expansion for Riesz means of order at least one, again with a remainder bound independent of the Robin parameter.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Transformer Encoders for Audio-Image-Symbolic Music Retrieval
papers.abstract: Score-based multimodal music retrieval requires representations that are both discriminative within each modality and compatible across audio recordings, sheet music images, and symbolic scores. This paper investigates the effectiveness of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) for adapting pretrained music encoders and examines whether modality-specific improvements translate into better multimodal representations. We compare full fine-tuning, LoRA, and QLoRA across nine pretrained audio, image, and symbolic score encoders on TriScore and the Musical Theme Dataset. Encoders are first evaluated and selected through supervised unimodal classification, using frozen-encoder linear probing as a reference. We then introduce a controlled 2x2 design crossing encoder adaptation with task-specific shared projection, comparing frozen and adapted representations before and after projection. LoRA or QLoRA is selected in 14 of 18 modality-target combinations, frequently matching or outperforming full fine-tuning while optimizing substantially fewer parameters. However, these unimodal gains do not transfer uniformly to multimodal classification. Adaptation and projection are complementary for composer classification on TriScore, largely redundant for TriScore instrument and the Musical Theme Dataset instrument and ensemble tasks, and partially interfering for composer classification on the Musical Theme Dataset. The final adapted-and-projected title representation on TriScore supports piece-level retrieval, reaching average Top-5 and Top-10 accuracies of 55.32 and 64.68, respectively. Cross-modal exclusion and neighborhood analyses further reveal strong modality-specific local structure in the projected spaces. Overall, PEFT provides an effective and computationally efficient alternative to full fine-tuning, but improved unimodal discrimination alone does not guarantee better multimodal organization.

papers.title: Truncated Dirichlet estimates for Bloch functions
papers.abstract:
We study the truncated Dirichlet functional
  \[
  \Phi_n (f) = \sum_{k = 1}^n k |a_k|^2, \quad f(z) = \sum_{k = 0}^\infty a_k z^k,
  \]
  when $f$ belongs to the Bloch space. If $n \geq 27$, we find a normalized Bloch function $f_n$ such that
  \[
  \Phi_n (f_n) > n B_n^2,
  \]
  where $B_n = \max \{ |a_n| : \| f \|_{\mathcal{B}} = 1 \}$, thus proving that an inequality by Kayumov and Wirths cannot be extended to large values of $n$. Nevertheless, we show that the inequality $\Phi_n(f) \leq n B_n^2$ holds for all normalized functions when $n \leq 9$.

papers.title: FGSM Attack Transferability from Simulation to Quantum Hardware in Network Intrusion Detection
papers.abstract: Quantum computers are now available through cloud platforms, and recent work has proposed using them to detect network intrusions. It is not yet clear how easily such systems can be attacked. We train a hybrid variational quantum classifier (VQC) on the Friday DDoS subset of CICIDS2017 and test it against two attacks: label flipping during training and FGSM evasion at prediction time. We run the tests in simulation and on IBM hardware, the Fez superconducting processor (Heron r2). We find that two models with similar accuracy can differ greatly in how easily they are attacked. A model that decides with little confidence loses half its detections to a very small change in the input, while a model trained to decide with more confidence needs a much larger change before it fails. Attacks built in simulation against the more confident model also work on real hardware, and the device classifies every unaltered attack sample correctly. Simulated device noise does not reduce accuracy, but it does reduce the model's confidence and makes attacks easier, so accuracy alone does not show how exposed a model is. Label flipping has no measurable effect until 15% of attack labels are changed. These results show that device noise should not be treated as a defense and that reported weaknesses in these classifiers depend partly on how they were trained.

papers.title: Dilation systems with two generators and the optimal Riesz bounds of a basis of ReLU networks
papers.abstract: For two $1$-periodic functions $\psi_1,\psi_2\in L^2(0,1)$ with mean zero we characterize when $\{1\}\cup\{\psi_1(\alpha\cdot x),\psi_2(\alpha\cdot x)\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}^d,\,\alpha\succ0}$ is a Riesz basis of $L^2([0,1]^d)$, in terms of a $2\times2$ matrix of Dirichlet series, and we compute its optimal bounds. The tool is a $2\times2$ matrix version of the theorem of Hedenmalm, Lindqvist and Seip for systems of dilations with two generators, proved through the reproducing kernel of the Hardy space of the infinite polydisk. In particular, we get the optimal bounds $2/3$ and $3/2$ for $\psi_1,\psi_2$ the triangle waves considered by Daubechies, DeVore, Foucart, Hanin and Petrova in $L^2(0,1)$, and the extended version in $L^2([0,1]^d)$ defined by Schneider and Vyb\'iral.

authors.name: Daniel Carando
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

authors.name: Tomas Fernandez Vidal
authors.institution: Universidad Nacional de Educación a Distancia

papers.title: A lower bound for the stability constant in the Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality
Elliptic Fekete points: separation, Riesz energies, and polynomial conditioning
papers.abstract: Elliptic Fekete configurations minimize logarithmic energy on the sphere. They also provide a natural source of complex polynomials with controlled Shub--Smale condition number. The link between these two problems is the product of the distances from each point to all the other points: logarithmic energy controls the geometric mean of these products, whereas local conditioning depends on each product separately. This paper studies the passage from global information to uniform estimates at individual nodes, exploring its connections with quantitative equidistribution, Riesz energies, and polynomial conditioning. We improve separation bounds for elliptic Fekete configurations and obtain quantitative Riesz-energy estimates for both these configurations and spherical roots of polynomials with optimal-order global conditioning. For $0<s<2$, these estimates also improve explicit upper bounds for the minimal Riesz $s$-energy.

papers.title: Coxeter Rigidity and ADE Classification of Fibonacci-Generated Tensor Categories
papers.abstract: We propose a program to classify tensor categories generated by prescribed seed tensor categories. We carry out this program for finitely many marked copies of the positive Fibonacci category with pairwise nonisomorphic generating simple objects, in the setting of split locally finite semisimple rigid $\CC$-linear tensor categories with simple unit. We show that the Fibonacci fusion relation forces the fusion rules to be those of a specialized Coxeter--Hecke ring. The systems admitting categorification have Coxeter exponents $2,3,\infty$. For every such system we construct a tensor category and prove uniqueness up to marked tensor equivalence. Its simple objects are indexed by the Coxeter group, which may be infinite. Finite rank occurs precisely for disjoint unions of finite ADE diagrams, giving the ADE classification of Fibonacci-generated fusion categories. These categories are unitarizable, with no unitary structure assumed on the candidate. In finite ADE type, allowing Yang--Lee seeds gives one independent tensor-branch choice on each connected component.

papers.title: Finite Composites of the Fibonacci Category with Pointed Fusion Categories
papers.abstract: We classify finite composites of the positive Fibonacci category with arbitrary pointed fusion categories, retaining the entire source functor and making no unitarity assumption on the target. Formal codegrees, dimension fields, and algebraic integrality exclude all dihedral Fibonacci rings $R_n$ with $n\ge4$ from categorification. Together with an independent graphical uniqueness argument, this gives the finite two-Fibonacci classification. For several marked Fibonacci generators, a geometric height-and-polygon argument identifies the based ring with a standard-basis Coxeter--Hecke ring. Transitive conjugation by the pointed image forces the noncommutation graph to be empty or a perfect matching. We then obtain a crossed-product classification in terms of a quotient group, a stabilizer, labelled Fibonacci or rank-six $\TT$ blocks, and compatible cocycle and categorical action data. This includes the Fibonacci--$\Z/3\Z$ composite problem without target unitarity. We also establish the corresponding forms and marked descent statements over characteristic-zero fields admitting the chosen Fibonacci-type input.

papers.title: HIPC: Humanoid Iterative Planning and Control via Goal-Conditioned Motion Closure
papers.abstract: Recent generative models are widely used to provide whole-body motion for humanoid tracking. Current methods combine motion generators with controllers in an open-loop paradigm, which leads to critical issues: tracking errors can accumulate into spatial drift, and the planner cannot adapt to unexpected physical disturbances without feedback from physical execution. However, directly feeding realized states back to the planner in a closed loop can cause discontinuities, resulting in physical jitter and even falls, since such states are out of distribution during training. To bridge this gap, we propose HIPC, a real-time Humanoid Iterative Planning and Control framework that couples a generative model with motion tracking into a unified planning-and-control paradigm. HIPC introduces a goal-conditioned motion planning trained with a canonical motion representation that avoids gimbal-lock singularities under extreme orientations and supports motion generation on diverse geometric and semantic conditions. Then, HIPC adopts two strategies, deviation-decayed recovery and history re-anchoring, to mitigate the out-of-distribution shift caused by realized-state feedback. Finally, HIPC operates a real-time asynchronous planning-and-control system, with latency compensation to reduce temporal mismatch for inference delay. Extensive experiments confirm the effectiveness of HIPC under switching and composition of diverse conditions. Results show that HIPC achieves state-of-the-art goal-reaching accuracy among existing methods while simultaneously demonstrating robustness to physical perturbations and the ability to recover from falls.

authors.name: Hesheng Wang
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

authors.name: Renjing Xu
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Probability-Layer Clustering for Bound-and-Budget Calibration in Multi-Bound Robust Bidding of Renewable-Based Virtual Power Plants
papers.abstract: RVPPs that aggregate dispatchable and non-dispatchable renewable energy sources, storage, and flexible demand that bid in the day-ahead and secondary reserve markets must cope with uncertainties in market prices, renewable generation, and demand. MBRO is well suited to this setting because it hedges adverse realizations through several deviation layers while keeping the final bidding problem as a tractable, scenario-free MILP. Its performance, however, depends on how the deviation bounds and uncertainty budgets are calibrated. Existing MBRO implementations commonly rely on fixed percentile-based bounds and externally specified budget vectors, usually examined through sensitivity analysis. This paper proposes PL-MBRO, that constructs parameter-specific deviation bounds from historical data conditional on selected risk-attitude quantiles and automatically derives the corresponding uncertainty budgets from empirical cluster probabilities. For each uncertain parameter, k-medians clustering partitions the historical daily profiles into representative probability layers; the cluster median defines the balanced representative, while favorable and adverse within-cluster percentiles define the optimistic and pessimistic representatives. The empirical cluster probabilities are mapped to integer full-horizon uncertainty budgets over the 96 quarter-hourly periods, while the robust inner problem determines the periods in which the corresponding deviation layers are most adverse to the schedule. Compared with a percentilebased MBRO benchmark, in-sample and out-of-sample tests on an RVPP bidding in both markets show that PL-MBRO consistently achieves better realized economic outcomes across the optimistic, balanced, and pessimistic strategies, with improvements of up to 92.7% in-sample and 57.3% out-of-sample, measured relative to the absolute value of the corresponding benchmark realized profit.

papers.title: When Is a Game a Markov Decision Process? Correspondences Between Game Theory and Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning and game theory describe the same object from two sides. Game theory says what a rational outcome of a strategic interaction is; reinforcement learning says how an agent could reach one through experience. The two literatures nevertheless keep separate vocabularies for identical structures, and the treatments that bridge them present the correspondence as analogy rather than theorem. This monograph supplies the theorems. A game is a Markov decision process in three distinct senses, and every table entry is labelled with the one that applies: a definitional identity, an exact reduction carried by a value- and solution-preserving map, or a structural analogy that fails under identifiable conditions. We take every standard class of game, from normal-form through repeated, stochastic, partially observable, extensive-form with imperfect information, Bayesian, graphical, Stackelberg, potential, coalitional, mean-field and evolutionary games, and identify for each the decision-theoretic model that reinforcement learning already studies under another name. The same treatment is applied to solution concepts: Nash equilibrium and the fixed point of the Bellman optimality operator, quantal response equilibrium and the soft Bellman operator, the Shapley value and credit assignment, Blackwell approachability and no-regret learning. We map each model class onto the training procedures sound for it and record the complexity of the associated solution problems. A final part collects the correspondences that do not hold: the non-stationarity that invalidates the independent-learner reduction, the impossibility results that forbid uncoupled convergence to Nash equilibrium, and the gap between the coarse correlated equilibria that no-regret self-play reaches and the correlated equilibria it is credited with.

papers.title: Kupershmidt--Nijenhuis structures on pre-Leibniz algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first construct the dual of a representation of a pre-Leibniz algebra and study infinitesimal deformations of a pre-Leibniz algebra with a representation, which lead to Nijenhuis pairs, characterizing trivial deformations, and to dual-Nijenhuis pairs. Building on these notions, we introduce Kupershmidt-(dual-)Nijenhuis structures and show that they give rise to hierarchies of pairwise compatible Kupershmidt operators, the converse holding under an invertibility condition. Finally, we show that Rota--Baxter--Nijenhuis structures, $r$-$n$ structures and BN-structures all arise as particular cases, and that the first two correspond to each other on quadratic pre-Leibniz algebras.

papers.title: Nedimo: An Evidence-Grounded Multilingual Pipeline for AI-Generated Sleep Stories
papers.abstract: Generative audio systems can produce large libraries of personalized bedtime content, but ordinary media objectives (retention, completion, and novelty) are poorly aligned with the goal of supporting a transition toward sleep. Direct evidence for narrated bedtime audio in adults is mixed, and a recent active-controlled trial did not support such audio as a standalone treatment for sleep disturbance. We translate this uncertain evidence into conservative engineering requirements and present a multilingual pipeline for generating and narrating low-arousal sleep stories. The implemented prototype separates deterministic planning from large language model generation, represents content and delivery parameters explicitly, shapes each script through a four-phase attention taper, validates structural and lexical constraints, performs a bounded error-aware retry, and quarantines unresolved outputs. Provider-agnostic text-to-speech synthesis is followed by paragraph-aware joining, two-pass loudness normalization, and a publication gate that re-measures the saved, encoded file against fixed loudness, loudness-range, and true-peak limits. The product data model records stop position, replay, early abandonment, and completion while treating these events as ambiguous behavioral proxies rather than clinical outcomes. We contribute an evidence-to-requirement mapping, a traceable guardrail architecture with explicit acceptance thresholds, technical evaluation criteria, and a prospective protocol for testing sleep-onset effects. No clinical efficacy is claimed; the system is positioned as a relaxation and attentional-support tool whose benefit and possible reliance must be evaluated empirically.

papers.title: Metadevices that compute: mathematical foundations and experimental implementations for neuromorphic nanophotonics
papers.abstract: Wave-based analog computing has re-emerged as a compelling alternative to digital electronics for specific linear-algebraic and machine-learning workloads, promising massively parallel, high-bandwidth, and energy-efficient information processing. Metamaterials, metasurfaces, and integrated metastructures (collectively, metadevices) now perform mathematical operations, solve integral and differential equations, multiply matrices, and implement trainable photonic neural networks directly in the wave domain. This focused review consolidates the mathematical foundations that underpin such devices, i.e., the mapping between linear operators and wave scattering, the feedback architectures that realize equation inversion, and the inverse-design and scientific machine-learning toolchains that make their synthesis and training tractable, and connects them to the rapidly growing body of experimental demonstrations, from free-space diffractive processors to reconfigurable guided-wave metastructures. We conclude with open problems and opportunities for this emerging neuromorphic nanophotonics ecosystem.

papers.title: Web application for retrospective geomagnetic storm detection, main phase analysis and identification of solar wind influence on storm intensity
papers.abstract: This work presents a web application for retrospective detection and analysis of geomagnetic storms using hourly Dst and solar wind data from OMNIWeb. The application detects storm events, identifies their main phases, computes solar wind derived parameters during the main phase, and examines their relationship with storm intensity. Its detection and main phase identification parameters are user-adjustable, allowing different assumptions to be tested interactively rather than imposed through a single fixed parameter set. The analysis covers the period from 1964 through May 2026. Using the default parameter set, 1796 storms with Dst_min <= -50 nT were detected, including 1422 moderate storms (-100 < Dst_min <= -50 nT), 347 intense storms (-250 < Dst_min <= -100 nT), and 27 super-storms (Dst_min <= -250 nT). After filtering for reliable main phase identification, 1643 storms were retained. The average main phase duration per class was 9.25 hours for moderate storms, 11.30 hours for intense storms and 13.75 hours for super-storms. After also requiring OMNIWeb solar wind data availability, 990 storms remained for examining the relationship between storm intensity and solar wind derived parameters over the main phase. The strongest correlations with |Dst_min| were obtained for peak dawn-dusk electric field (Eyp: R = 0.836), peak southward IMF (Bzp: R = -0.811), and integrated electric field (Eyi: R = 0.759). These results are consistent with the importance of the solar wind electric field and southward interplanetary magnetic field in geomagnetic storm development. All outputs are downloadable for further user-defined analysis.

authors.name: Daniil Papakonstantinou
authors.institution: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

papers.title: Scalable Audio-LLM System for Speech MOS Evaluation: A Diagnostic Case Study and Adaptation Roadmap
papers.abstract: The continuous deployment of enterprise voice systems creates a critical operational bottleneck: evaluating the acoustic quality of synthetic speech across high-volume production updates. While human Mean Opinion Score (MOS) remains the quality gold standard, it introduces severe operational costs and turn-around delays that make continuous integration infeasible. In this work, we present a system design case study for a scalable, low-cost and offline evaluation pipeline capable of scoring large batches of synthetic speech at marginal cost. First, we use Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct in a zero-shot setting for granular MOS estimation, noticing perceptual blind spots and inherent biases. Then, we analyze SOMOS dataset and construct a diagnostic benchmark that operationalizes two prosodic dimensions associated with human naturalness ratings. Finally, we adapt Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct through a parameter-efficient finetuning (LoRA) on the task of MOS evaluation, observing improvements over base model and widely used neural baselines like UTMOS and establishing a practical blueprint for enterprise-grade speech quality assurance.

authors.name: Dimitrios Kokkinis
authors.institution: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

authors.name: Panagiotis Kakoulidis
authors.institution: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

papers.title: ReX-GG: a LLM Ensemble Pipeline for Relation-extraction and Graph Generation
papers.abstract: Current LLM ensemble frameworks focus on multi-step setups with additional modules for answer ranking, often opting for token and span analysis rather than structured outputs, leading to heavyweight architectures with potential fail states along the pipeline. Faster, lighter solutions are more vulnerable to hallucination propagation and can lack output control in more complex pipelines. This paper proposes a customisable, lightweight ensemble workflow of coordinated Large Language Models that leverages JSON-structured outputs and anonymous peer-review ranking to mitigate hallucinatory outputs and single-model failure points. The pipeline is demonstrated on a relation extraction task applied to popular science articles in English, targeting four ontologically-grounded relation types (strong causation, weak causation, contrastive, and compositional), with semantic node canonicalisation and interactive, colour-coded HTML causal graphs as the final output. Performance is evaluated through an anonymous user study, achieving an average perceived accuracy of 0.778 against a human-annotated gold standard. The modular architecture supports flexible deployment across both API-based and in-house LLM setups, and the full framework is released under an open license to foster reproducibility and collaborative research.

papers.title: Homotopy in enriched functor categories: Frobenius exact structures and weak Serre functors
papers.abstract: Let $(\V, \otimes, I,[-,-])$ be a closed symmetric monoidal category with finite (co)limits. Assume that $\V$ is weakly idempotent complete and additive. For a given small $\V$-category $\A$, we investigate sufficient conditions on $\A$ under which the ordinary category $[\A, \V]_0$ of $\V$-functors from $\A$ to $\V$, equipped with the exact structure $\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}}$, is a Frobenius exact category,and hence, induces a triangulated stable category. The exact structure $\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}}$ encompasses the degre-wise trivial exact structure on categories of $N$-chain complexes and $m$-periodic chain complexes, with terms in a variety of settings, including left $R$-modules, quasi-coherent sheaves on a scheme, and Banach spaces. We subsequently address the question of describing abstract left and right homotopy relations in $([\A, \V]_0;\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}})$ in terms of families of morphisms defined objectwise, as in the cases of chain-homotopy and relative homotopy relations. To this end, we introduce the notion of left/right-weak Serre $\V$-functors on $\A$, and investigate their relationships with the classical Serre functor relative to a commutative ring $k$.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Object-Centric Representation for Multi-Task Audio Analysis
papers.abstract: This paper studies the capability of an object-centric audio representation to support multiple downstream tasks within a unified framework. The object-centric model is trained in a self-supervised setup using slot attention by reconstructing Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) patch embeddings from a set of latent slots. It is trained on synthetic audio mixtures, which provides controlled multi-source audio scenes. These slot representations are evaluated for the classification, detection, and separation of sound events by training task specific output layers. On the classification task, the model achieves an F1-score of 0.8, comparable to clip-level AST embeddings which achieve 0.7. For sound event detection, it reaches a macro F1-score of 0.7, outperforming clip-level AST embeddings at 0.4 and matching AST patch embeddings at 0.7, which encode finer time-frequency information. In source separation, it achieves an SI-SDR improvement (SI-SDRi) of 18.4 dB. Furthermore, in a zero-shot source separation setting, the model achieves an SI-SDRi of 14.5 dB. These results demonstrate that slot-based representations capture transferable and compositional structure in audio scenes, enabling generalization across tasks and datasets.

papers.title: Fluid Antenna Systems for ISAC Design: A Survey
papers.abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) introduce dynamic positional degrees of freedom (DoFs), extending the spatial domain from a static and discrete resource to a quasi-continuous and reconfigurable design space. This spatial flexibility provides an effective means of alleviating the geometric rigidity and functional conflicts that constrain integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. Against this backdrop, we provide a comprehensive overview of FAS-enabled ISAC, tracing the evolution from theoretical performance limits to practical transceiver architectures. To illustrate the surveyed design evolution, we further propose the fluid antenna multi-mode modulation (FA-MM) framework as a representative case study of multidimensional physical-layer design for FAS-ISAC. Finally, several open challenges are discussed, with emphasis on predictive sensing, adaptive coordination, and secure spatial-state management in future FAS-ISAC systems.

authors.name: Hong Niu
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Shuaixin Yang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yue Xiao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: TurnTurk-GPT: Text-Based Turn-Taking Prediction for Turkish
papers.abstract: This paper presents TurnTurk-GPT, a text-based turn-taking predictor for Turkish obtained by fine-tuning a Turkish GPT-2 model with the TurnGPT objective on synthetic and real dialogue, and evaluates it on real Turkish conversation against rule baselines, a zero-shot Turkish language model and a widely used multilingual end-of-turn detector. Evaluation uses word-level decision points on unpunctuated, lower-cased text approximating the output of streaming speech recognisers, recording-disjoint and speaker-disjoint folds, nested threshold selection and paired cluster bootstrap tests. TurnTurk-GPT outperforms the multilingual detector under both recording-disjoint and speaker-disjoint evaluation. It outperforms the zero-shot language model only when the test speakers occur in training; on unseen speakers the two are statistically indistinguishable. Removing the suffixes of the turn-final word reduces AP by up to 44%, against 2% for a sentence-internal word, locating the Turkish end-of-turn cue in verb-final morphology. Synthetic dialogue alone yields the weakest trained model, and when a speaker pauses the zero-shot and multilingual baselines remain close to chance. The model and the evaluation protocol are publicly released.

papers.title: IGDA-ICMH: an Importance Guided Feature and Network Dual Adaptation Framework towards Image Compression for Machine and Human Vision
papers.abstract: With the surge of machine vision applications, image compression for both machine and human vision (ICMH) has become an important research area. Existing studies mainly focus on task-specific adaptation or multi-task joint optimization, yet they often overlook the unequal contributions of different features and network layers to downstream machine vision tasks. To address this issue, we first quantitatively investigate the impact of different feature and network layers on machine vision performance, providing a principled understanding of their importance. Based on this analysis, an Importance Guided feature and network Dual Adaptation (IGDA) framework is developed for ICMH. It adopts implicit neural representation as the basic architecture and designs an efficient adaptation structure with both feature and network weight adaptation. An Importance-Guided Network Adaptation (IGNA) module is developed with a low-rank adaptation strategy to selectively adjust key network layers according to their importance in different tasks. An Importance-Guided Feature Adaptation (IGFA) module is developed with a low-rank and Kronecker product-based transform to explore the non-local property of the features in order to reduce the number of adaptation parameters. Extensive experiments on representative machine vision tasks, including image classification and object detection, demonstrate that our IGDA-ICMH framework achieves significantly better performance than the existing implicit neural representation-based methods for ICMH.
