papers.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for End-to-End Self-Driving
papers.abstract: End-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving models achieve strong planning performance but remain largely opaque, limiting observability and trust. We apply mechanistic interpretability to E2E driving by training Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) on the internal activations of a simple, single-camera end-to-end path planning model. Unsupervised clustering of SAE latents reveals interpretable structure aligned with route intent, vehicle speed, and braking behavior, recovering route intent with 98.3% accuracy without supervision. Through paired counterfactual image edits, we further show that specific SAE features are visually grounded and systematically respond to scene changes such as traffic light state and stop sign presence. Steering individual SAE latents produces predictable, monotonic changes in planner outputs including lateral displacement, curvature, and braking. Finally, we demonstrate a practical application of these representations: we build a lightweight adapter trained on SAE latents that reduces trajectory selection error by 3.44%, outperforming an equivalent adapter that omits SAE latents, confirming that the sparse representation captures useful information for interpretability. Code and visualizations are available at https://mgagvani.github.io/mechanistic-interpretability-for-e2e-driving/

authors.name: Sivamurugan Velmurugan
authors.institution: North Carolina School of Science and Mathematics

papers.title: A Large Eddy Simulation Study of Turbine Pitch Motion Effects on Power Generation in Fully Developed Floating Wind Turbine Arrays
papers.abstract: Interactions between floating wind turbines and the marine atmospheric boundary layer affect turbine wakes and power output. This study examines the impact of turbine representations and platform pitching motion on power predictions for aligned floating wind turbine arrays. Large-eddy simulations (LES) are performed for a fully developed wind turbine array boundary layer with periodic streamwise and spanwise boundary conditions and moving surface drag (MOSD) at the bottom surface. A proposed power-curve-aware extension of the conventional actuator disk model (PCADM) is compared with the traditional constant coefficient actuator disk model (CCADM), which is valid in principle only during Region 2 operation. Harmonic pitching motion matched to a representative ocean wave frequency is prescribed for IEA 15MW turbines mounted on the UMaine VolturnUS-S platform. Results demonstrate that the CCADM produces unphysical power overshoot when relative velocities induced by harmonic pitching periodically exceed rated speed, while the PCADM eliminates these unrealistic excursions from the actual turbine operating range. Various wind-wave conditions and relative pitching motions for an aligned farm with PCADM turbines are analyzed, including in-phase, opposite-phase, and incommensurate-phase row-to-row relative turbine motion. Results reveal that, depending on operational regions, turbine pitching motion can either increase or decrease mean turbine power output. Among the relative phases considered, in-phase motions produce larger fluctuations at the farm scale due to stronger turbine-turbine correlations. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for turbine motion and associated changes in operational regions when modeling turbine and wind farm power production in LES of offshore floating wind farms using actuator disk representations.

papers.title: Queryable Gaussian View Index: Text Retrieval and Selective Camera Localization
papers.abstract: We present Queryable Gaussian View Index (QGVI) for querying existing Gaussian scene assets and their associated calibrated reference data. Text-view retrieval and selective RGB camera localization return poses in the asset's coordinate frame. QGVI-T turns Gaussian-rendered views into a language-searchable index of scene locations, binding structured captions to known camera poses and place identifiers. Semantic and lexical retrieval select views from distinct places without online rendering, VLM calls, or a scene-specific pose network. The image route, QGVI-I, filters LoGS-based geometric estimates using distinct inlier query keypoints. It omits photometric refinement and preserves accepted pose coordinates. On nine development scenes, QGVI-T achieves 58.3% Top-1 and 78.3% Top-5 joint relevance-and-validity success, compared with 26.1% and 34.6% for our CityLoC reimplementation with refinement. QGVI-I achieves 97.3% scene-mean pose success at 1 m/2 degrees, with pooled false-acceptance and false-rejection rates of 0.707% and 1.142%. A paired cached evaluation retains all 1,775 initializer poses correct at this threshold. Recorded median text query latency is 0.020 s. Matched controls show competitive BM25 retrieval and slightly lower false acceptance for thresholded full LoGS; grid augmentation suggests modest gains on novel-view-derived descriptions. We report model-judged semantic success separately from source-camera recovery, with source-verified or estimated scales for geometric evaluation.

authors.name: Tianyu Xiong
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Oncology in South China

papers.title: Berenstein-Zelevinsky polytopes for type $\mathrm{G}_{2}$
papers.abstract: In 2001, Berenstein and Zelevinsky presented a polyhedral model for the problem of computing tensor-product multiplicities for semi\-simple Lie algebras. We provide explicit linear equations and inequalities for Berenstein--Zelevinsky (BZ) polytopes of type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ Lie algebras. We prove that the denominator of a type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ BZ~polytope divides $180$, and that this bound is sharp, while the quasi-period of the Ehrhart quasipolynomial of such a polytope is always a divisor of $6$. We also show that BZ~polytopes of type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ Lie algebras can fail to satisfy Ehrhart positivity, in contrast to a conjectured property of BZ~polytopes for all classical types.

papers.title: Immersed Boundary Electrodiffusion in the Wasserstein Gradient Flow Formalism: Global Well-Posedness, Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics, and Singular Asymptotics
papers.abstract: We introduce a unified optimal transport framework for the Immersed Boundary (IB) electrodiffusion active pump model. By representing membrane chemical potential barriers and active pump potentials via smoothed Eulerian kernels ($\Psi_w, \mathcal{H}_w$), we formulate the passive dynamics as an $L^2$-Wasserstein ($W_2$) gradient flow coupled to non-conservative active pushing fields representing ATP-driven $3:2$ $\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+$ exchangers. We establish global weak existence of solutions to the continuous Poisson--Nernst--Planck--IB system via a split-step Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational scheme, backed by Calder\'on--Zygmund bounds for non-local Poisson drift and $H^3(\mathbb{S}^1)$ interface regularity under Stokes flow. We prove the continuous Rayleighian energy balance and establish exponential $W_2$-stability of Non-Equilibrium Steady States (NESS) under a quantitative Bakry--\'Emery curvature threshold. Furthermore, we analyze the dual singular limits of kernel smoothing width $w \to 0$ and dimensionless Debye length $g = \lambda_D / L \to 0$. We establish the precise asymptotic regime connecting regularized and sharp models, prove the $\Gamma$-convergence of regularized energy functionals, derive distributional interface flux jump conditions, and resolve $O(\lambda_D)$ Debye space-charge boundary layers to confirm bulk electroneutrality.

papers.title: Know When the Equation Is Wrong: Structural Uncertainty for LLM-Guided Symbolic Regression under Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can help discover mathematical equations from data, but most LLM-guided symbolic regression methods focus on a single best equation without quantifying uncertainty over alternative functional forms. This is challenging because distinct equations can fit the observed data similarly while producing substantially different extrapolations. Our experiments on the LLM-SRBench dataset show that standard conformal intervals achieve nominal in-distribution coverage but frequently fail under extrapolation. To tackle this challenge, we introduce LLM-SR-UQ, a framework that retains competing equation structures and uses their disagreement to characterize uncertainty about the underlying functional form. We extend the standard fixed-width conformal approach to quantify structural intervals, which measure disagreement among candidate equations and identify where prediction intervals should widen. Extensive experiments show our framework substantially improves coverage attainment by incorporating structural disagreement while preserving in-distribution coverage. Our approach also shows good generalizability when it is applied to other symbolic-regression methods.

papers.title: When Safety Checks Become Privacy Risks: A Privacy-Preserving Paradigm for LLM Agent Safety Auditing
papers.abstract: Large language model agents interact with online services through tool calls that may access private data or perform sensitive actions. Specialized providers can supply and maintain pre-execution safety auditing capabilities for agent operators. However, sending task descriptions, call arguments, and interaction histories to an external auditor may expose sensitive user information. In this work, we propose a paradigm for privacy-preserving safety auditing that separates delegated audit computation from plaintext access and execution authority. Grounded in a three-domain auditing model, the paradigm connects trusted representation construction, encrypted audit computation, and trusted decision and execution through explicit interfaces. These interfaces accommodate alternative representations and scorers, while encrypted computation protects audit inputs from a semi-honest auditor. We instantiate this paradigm in SealCall, a framework combining learned audit representations, CKKS-based encrypted similarity computation, and execution control bound to audited tool calls. Evaluated on 1,252 public binary candidates, SealCall achieves a mean F1 score of 0.840 under grouped nested evaluation, while preserving plaintext audit decisions in all measured cases. A representative configuration completes each encrypted scoring operation in 0.176 s.

authors.name: Jian Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: MemX: Memory-Aware Automatic Parallelism for Cross-Vendor Heterogeneous GPU Training
papers.abstract: Cross-vendor heterogeneous GPU clusters are increasingly used for large-scale model training. However, their GPUs differ substantially in compute power, memory capacity, and interconnect characteristics. Existing automatic parallelism training systems usually minimize iteration time while treating memory as a hard constraint, almost failing in resolving the compute--memory asymmetry of cross-vendor clusters regardless correlation between memory and throughput. In this paper, we present MemX, a new memory-aware automatic parallelism system that jointly optimizes iteration time, peak memory usage, and cross-GPU memory balance. MemX consists of a weighted-product objective function, heterogeneous recomputation strategies, a minimal-set profiler, interpolation-based data augmentation, a dual-output XGBoost predictor, and a hash-signature prediction cache, in order to accelerate search of large-scale auto-parallel best configurations at lower cost. We implement MemX on Megatron-LM and evaluate it against four automatic parallelism baselines on two heterogeneous clusters. MemX achieves the lowest prediction Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 12.17% and is the only method that identifies the real Top-1 configuration under both time-based and memory-balance rankings. In terms of search cost and search space, MemX searches 31,240 configurations in 26.5 seconds, while an end-to-end profiling baseline is extrapolated to require about 17 days at the same scale. The simulation study that extends the measured 20-GPU data to 40-GPU and 60-GPU clusters further illustrates the effectiveness of MemX at larger scales.

papers.title: Improved estimation of differential entropy of a multivariate Gaussian distribution
papers.abstract: We consider estimation of entropy of a multivariate variate normal distribution with unknown mean vector and unknown covariance matrix. Using a decision-theoretic approach, we study the problem under a general location-invariant loss function that is strictly convex and minimized at zero. We first characterize the class of affine equivariant estimators and obtain the best affine equivariant estimator. We further show that the best affine equivariant estimator is inadmissible under the general loss. Exploiting information in the sample mean, we derive Stein-type improved estimators, including an extension to the case of a mean matrix. Under the linex loss, we obtain a smooth Brewster--Zidek-type estimator that dominates the best affine equivariant estimator, and we show that this estimator is generalized Bayes under a suitable non-informative prior.

authors.name: Somnath Mondal
authors.institution: Calcutta Institute of Pharmaceutical Technology & Allied Health Sciences

papers.title: Anisotropic Boltzmann transport in a tight-binding superlattice: Exact results for power-law energy-dependent scattering
papers.abstract: We develop a complete Boltzmann transport theory for the in-plane ($\sigma_{xx}$) and out-of-plane ($\sigma_{zz}$) conductivities of an electronic superlattice consisting of a periodic stack of two-dimensional (2D) parabolic-band layers coupled along the superlattice axis by nearest-neighbor tunneling $t$, in the physically relevant regime $t\ll E_F$ where the Fermi surface is an open, corrugated cylinder. Within the relaxation-time approximation with a power-law energy-dependent scattering time $\tau(E)\propto E^{p}$, we study the seven models $p=0,\pm1,\pm3/2,\pm2$ as functions of the 2D electron density $n$ per layer and temperature $T$. For $p=-2$ (in plane) and $p\le -1$ (out of plane), long-lived carriers at the miniband bottom can dominate transport at finite temperature. For $p=-2$, these carriers produce a pronounced peak in $\sigma_{zz}(T)$ at $T\sim E_F$. We find that the temperature dependence of the anisotropic metallic dc conductivity can be highly counterintuitive depending on $t$, $T$, and $p$, with no generic increase or decrease with temperature. The Lorenz ratio is determined by the energy variance of the current-carrying electrons; the Wiedemann-Franz (WF) law is exact as $T\to0$ for all models at fixed $t$, with anisotropic corrections at finite temperature. Band-edge carriers first enhance the interlayer Lorenz ratio up to several times its low-temperature value through thermal occupation of separated energy ranges within the same electron band and then suppress it at high temperature by energy filtering. Strong violations of the Wiedemann-Franz law can therefore arise from miniband structure and energy-dependent elastic scattering alone.

papers.title: What Should LLMs Forget: Reinforcement Unlearning of Knowledge Associations
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) acquire extensive factual knowledge during pre-training, which may include sensitive, private, or copyrighted information, motivating the development of unlearning methods that selectively remove specific knowledge while preserving general capabilities. However, existing approaches typically optimize entire responses without explicitly identifying the knowledge to be forgotten, resulting in coarse and uncontrolled forgetting. To address this, we revisit the forgetting target of LLM unlearning and introduce Knowledge Association (KA), which characterizes the association between a query context and its target knowledge and is instantiated by the corresponding conditional predictive distribution, as the fundamental target of forgetting. Based on KA, we propose Knowledge Association Reinforcement Unlearning (KARU), a unified reinforcement learning framework that suppresses forgotten knowledge associations while preserving retained ones. Specifically, KARU derives complementary mechanisms from the KA-based formulation: token-level reward construction for finer-grained forgetting supervision, distribution-level regularization for precise knowledge suppression, and proximity-aware retain sampling to mitigate collateral degradation. Experiments across diverse LLMs on representative benchmarks demonstrate that KARU consistently improves forgetting effectiveness over existing baselines while maintaining comparable retention performance and general utility.

authors.name: Haiyan Feng
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology

papers.title: Characteristics of VHF and UHF band detection using Stark shifting in Rydberg-atom sensors
papers.abstract: We present a characterization of the sensitivity of broadband electric field measurements in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands using AC stark shifting of Rydberg states. The dependence of the sensitivity and dynamic range of the field measurements using nD5/2 states of cesium for principal quantum numbers n= 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 is presented, detailing the intricacies involved. The frequencies considered for the measurement range from 50 MHz to 900 MHz for which a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell is used to excite the Rydberg atoms with the RF fields. The corresponding sensitivities achieved are in the $(\mu V/m)/\sqrt{Hz}$ range. A general trend of better sensitivity for higher principal quantum numbers is observed. This work paves the way for a better understanding of the AC Stark dependent field measurements using Rydberg sensors.

authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

papers.title: Electron Scattering with ASTRA: Helium and Molecular Hydrogen
papers.abstract: We present an implementation of electron-impact scattering in ASTRA, a close-coupling method based on transition density matrices previously applied to molecular photoionization. The scattering states are obtained with a pole-free Galerkin method with variational surface matching, which yields the scattering matrix and the channel-resolved amplitudes for elastic and electronically inelastic integral cross sections and molecular-frame differential cross sections. For helium, ASTRA reproduces elastic and inelastic cross sections over a broad energy range, resolves the He$^-$(1s2s$^2$ $^2$S$^e$) Feshbach resonance in both energy and angle, and captures the principal interference structures in the n=2 excitation angular distributions, in selected channels matching measured differential-cross-section ratios more closely than available benchmark calculations. For molecular hydrogen, target polarization and interchannel coupling are represented through additional close-coupling channels, without a fitted polarization potential or a separately constructed (N+1)-electron correlation space. Compared with the restricted-channel description, the expanded calculations substantially improve agreement with UKRmol+ for elastic and inelastic cross sections. We further report fully orientation-resolved three-dimensional molecular-frame angular distributions for state-resolved electron-impact excitation. These reveal pronounced stereodynamic effects that vanish upon orientational averaging: at 15 eV, excitation of the b$^3\Sigma_u^+$ state is more than eight times stronger for incident momentum parallel rather than perpendicular to the molecular axis. These results connect conventional scattering benchmarks with orientation-resolved collision dynamics and open the way to larger molecular targets.

authors.name: Thomas C. Allison
authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

papers.title: Toward Low-Burden Image-Based Dietary Assessment Through Human-AI Collaborative Correction
papers.abstract: Image-based dietary assessment can automate initial food logging, but meal photographs often leave food identity, hidden ingredients, preparation, and portion uncertain, making correction a recurring part of use. We introduce Human-AI Collaborative Correction, which reframes correction as communicate intent $\rightarrow$ regenerate $\rightarrow$ verify: users express what should change through text, voice, or guided clarification, the AI regenerates the linked dietary record, and users verify the result. In a within-participant study with 30 participants, compared with conventional Manual Search-and-Edit Correction, collaborative correction was associated with lower workload (Raw TLX: 35.83 vs. 55.00; p < .001), 21.0% lower recorded usage time, 51.1% fewer recorded clicks, and more favorable user-experience ratings; 90.0% preferred it overall. An exploratory nutrient analysis also found lower energy MAE. These findings support intent-driven regeneration as a promising interaction pattern for reducing correction burden while preserving user verification and making image-based dietary tracking easier to sustain.

authors.name: Xiao Hu
authors.institution: Institute of Optics and Electronics, Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: From prediction error to sparse events: Biologically inspired signed-dyadic coding for Mandarin keyword spotting
papers.abstract: In continuous spiking keyword spotting, temporally correlated acoustic frames can repeatedly trigger memory access and neural computation at a dense input interface, even when hidden activity is sparse. Predictive processing and sensory adaptation suggest retaining predictable input locally and responding selectively to deviations. Inspired by this mechanism, we propose Predictive Signed-Dyadic Coding (PG). PG maintains a local prediction for each input channel and transmits an event only when the residual exceeds a learned threshold. Each event carries a sign and a finite power-of-two magnitude, and the receiver reconstructs it with fixed-point shifts and additions. In Mandarin keyword spotting, INPUT-PG reaches 90.00% accuracy while reducing mean SRAM reads by 33.87% and inference cycles by 32.77%. PG provides a hardware interface for research on low-power continuous speech processing and event-based sensory systems.

authors.name: Zijian Zhou
authors.institution: National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering

papers.title: Pair density waves via interband pairing --- a perspective from superfluid weight
papers.abstract: Pair density waves (PDW) are superconducting states that exhibit a spatially modulated pairing order parameter, corresponding to Cooper pairs carrying finite center-of-mass momentum. While some recent studies have emphasized the role of quantum geometry in stabilizing PDW order in certain multiband systems, we here present a systematic investigation of an alternative, geometry-independent mechanism: PDW order driven purely by interband Cooper pairing. Using the superfluid weight (SW) as a diagnostic, we study two canonical models. The first is the classic Fulde-Ferrell model of an $s$-wave superconductor subject to a Zeeman splitting field, which realizes pure interband pairing between two rigidly shifted bands; the second is a spinless honeycomb-lattice model with nearest-neighbor $f$-wave pairing, a modified version of which was recently found to exhibit PDW instability in density-matrix renormalization-group simulations. In both models the SW receives no quantum geometric contribution at the mean-field level, yet it can be greatly suppressed or even turn negative, signaling a tendency toward pairing with spatial phase modulations. For the first model, we establish that the SW is increasingly suppressed as the Zeeman field grows, drastically turning negative upon the emergence of extensive gapless excitations, i.e., the Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces. For the honeycomb $f$-wave model, we demonstrate, both analytically and numerically, vanishing quantum-geometric SW and an invariably negative total SW. Our results thus establish the SW as a qualitative indicator of the tendency toward PDW order, and provide a microscopic rationale for the interband-pairing-driven PDW instability.

authors.name: Yi-Fan Jiang
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Falcons: Pushing the Speed-Ratio Limits of Lossy Compression for Parallel Scientific Applications
papers.abstract: The extreme volume of scientific data has become a critical challenge for modern exa-scale scientific computing applications, and error-bounded lossy compression remains indispensable for scientific data management due to its high data reduction rate and controllable data fidelity. However, to ensure sufficient data reduction, existing compressors incur prohibitive computational overheads in real-world parallel scientific computing applications. To overcome the performance bottlenecks of error-bounded lossy compression, we present \textbf{Falcons}, a broadly deployable error-bounded lossy compressor that simultaneously achieves \textbf{high compression ratios with ultra-fast throughput, minimizing the overhead in parallel scientific applications}. Falcons integrates three key designs: memory-regularized interpolation with SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data) vectorization, distribution-adaptive lossless coding, and application-oriented optimizations for multiple parallelization schemes. Across our evaluations on cutting-edge supercomputers, Falcons clearly outperforms state-of-the-art compressors, simultaneously achieving up to 29\% compression ratio improvement and 255\% throughput improvement. In case studies of real-world applications, Falcons accelerates large-scale parallel data I/O and remote transfer by up to 44.6\% and 51.5\%, and provides 1.55$\times$ end-to-end speedup for the full WRF (Weather Research \& Forecasting) application workflow.

authors.name: Bing Lu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Quantong Fu
authors.institution: Yanshan College Shandong University of Finance and Economics

authors.name: Zedong Liu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Nereus: A Large-Scale Underwater Dataset for Fine-Grained Attribute Understanding and Grounded Counting Perception
papers.abstract: Underwater imagery records rich ecological information and supports applications such as science communication, fishery monitoring, ecological conservation, and oceanographic research. Beyond general scene understanding, these applications require models to recognize fine-grained biological traits and reason over spatially grounded evidence. However, existing underwater datasets often provide coarse category labels, generic captions, or total-count supervision, which limits their use for organism-level analysis and ecological reasoning. We introduce Nereus, a large-scale dataset for Underwater Fine-grained Perception that jointly supports Fine-Grained Object Attribute Understanding and Grounded Counting Perception. Nereus contains 88K images and 2.68M question-answer pairs, including annotations for 136K marine organism objects across 2,690 species and 1,515 genera, as well as 65K point annotations and 67K grounded counting QA pairs. Experiments with representative multimodal models show that Nereus improves downstream adaptation over existing underwater-domain data and provides a foundation for future research on fine-grained marine perception.

authors.name: Zihao Jin
authors.institution: North China University of Water Resources and Electric Power

papers.title: KITE: Retrieval as a Decision Procedure for Long-Term Conversational Memory
papers.abstract: Many long-term memory systems for LLM agents are built around embedding-based retrieval. Al- though effective for semantic matching, similarity ranking alone does not establish whether re- trieved memories satisfy the conditions implied by a question. In this paper, we introduce KITE (Knowledge-Indexed Temporal Evidence), a vector-free framework that formulates memory re- trieval as an explicit decision procedure. KITE organizes multi-session conversations as structured knowledge indexed by a governed topic vocabulary, which evolves through controlled expansion and consolidation. At query time, questions are compiled into inspectable retrieval plans over the same knowledge index that guides memory construction. The plans are then executed through fixed lookup and ranking operations, while sparse lexical retrieval recovers surface details omitted from the structured representation. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S show that KITE achieves 93.5% and 86.0% accuracy while using only about 1.6k reader-context tokens per ques- tion. These results demonstrate that conversational memory can move beyond similarity ranking by unifying memory construction and query compilation around a governed index, turning retrieval into an inspectable decision procedure for determining which evidence satisfies the question.

authors.name: Zhibo Zhou
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

authors.name: Fei Du
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification on Simplicial Complexes with Conformalized Simplicial Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Simplicial neural networks (SNNs) are powerful tools for prediction tasks on higher-order relational datasets stored on simplicial complexes (SCs), a higher-order generalization of graphs. However, SNNs usually lack rigorous uncertainty quantification (UQ), limiting their usefulness in high-stakes scenarios. We propose conformalized SNN (CF-SNN), a framework that, given a simplicial-complex entity with m prediction targets, generates prediction sets for all m targets simultaneously. Under mild assumptions, CF-SNN guarantees that, for each target, the prediction set contains the true label with a user-specified nominal coverage probability, and the realized miscoverage proportion across all m targets is guaranteed to remain close to the nominal level with high probability. Extensive experiments across a wide range of SC prediction tasks demonstrate that CF-SNN is a flexible UQ framework that achieves user-specified coverage while producing informative prediction sets of small size.

papers.title: HippocamFLEX: FPGA Prototyping of Hippocampus-Inspired Architecture for Context-Aware Sequence Prediction
papers.abstract: Unlike conventional architectures that treat memory as static pattern storage, the hippocampus organizes experience as ordered sequences and retrieves them through temporally compressed replay spanning prior, current, and anticipated states. This capacity of context-appropriate sequence prediction remains absent from conventional deep learning accelerators and existing neuromorphic fabrics. We present HippocamFLEX, a fully synthesizable digital implementation of these hippocampal computational principles, realized with SystemVerilog RTL on the AMD Zynq UltraScale+,XCZU9EG. The design maps the hippocampal trisynaptic pathway onto three pipeline stages: a Dentate Gyrus / Entorhinal Cortex (DG/EC) stage for hypervector proximity matching, a CA3 stage for context-gated recurrent sequence prediction with multi-phase temporal tagging, and a CA1 stage that integrates past, present, and predicted future events into a theta-sequence inspired output. While much brain-inspired hardware relies on analog mixed-signal design for energy efficiency, this work targets FPGA prototyping as a deliberate architectural choice: FPGAs offer rapid design-space exploration without tape-out cost, bit-exact determinism that simplifies verification. The design supports 64 events across 16 contexts and is verified on physical silicon across context-isolation, temporal-ordering, and mid-sequence sliding-window test cases and is inherently scalable to larger event and context sets.

papers.title: A Neural Network Approach towards Real-Time Knot Point Density Estimates for the Nonlinear Quadrotor
papers.abstract: Spline representations provide a compact way to approximate continuous trajectories using a finite number of parameters. When approximating trajectories generated by dynamical systems, the efficiency of a spline representation depends strongly on the placement of knot points. Uniform knot distributions often lead to inefficient representations, requiring either unnecessary control points or producing poor approximations in regions where the trajectory varies rapidly. In this work we propose a learning-based method for adaptive knot placement in B-spline approximations of trajectories generated by ordinary differential equations. A neural network learns a mapping from the initial condition of the system to quantities that characterize the local variation of the resulting trajectory. These estimates are used to construct nonuniform knot distributions that approximately equidistribute a local error indicator, reducing the number of control points needed to meet a prescribed accuracy.

authors.name: Jasmine Ratchford
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines
papers.abstract: To rigorously establish the value of a novel deep learning method, it must be compared against appropriate baselines. As deep learning has become increasingly common in the physical and life sciences, there have been numerous cases in which apparent progress has turned out to be an artifact of omitted or missing baselines. In this work, we investigate whether this problem can be mitigated by using large language models to automate the construction of baselines. We assemble 36 supervised classification and regression tasks from peer-reviewed studies in Nature, Science, and Cell-family journals that investigate novel deep learning methods for scientific applications. We then use a language model to construct simple baselines for each task. These automatically constructed baselines are strong, recovering a median of 95.5% (mean 85.7%) of the gap between a trivial predictor and the score of the deep learning model. The median simple baseline matches or exceeds the performance of the deep learning model in 12 studies. We further examine the variation across scientific domains and publication venues and we characterize the effects of test-time compute and access to different levels of study context. As human peer review has struggled to keep up with the rapidly increasing volume of research articles in recent years, our results suggest that automated baseline construction is a practical and scalable check on deep learning contributions in the physical and life sciences.

authors.name: Jiaqi Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Model-Agnostic Search for New Physics in the Presence of Imperfect Background by Smearing the Data
papers.abstract: In the search for new particles in high-energy physics, it is necessary to first define the signal region (SR) enriched in signal events, and then compare events in this region with the expected background distribution. While most existing search methods rely on prior domain knowledge of either the signal or the background, there has been less effort to relax both assumptions simultaneously, as methods that weaken one assumption typically rely on strong knowledge of the other. We propose Model-Agnostic Search with Smearing and Imperfect Background (MASSIB), a method that addresses this challenge by learning the density ratio of events relative to a misspecified background distribution using modern tools from machine learning, and defining the SR as the region with high density ratio. Recognizing that a naive application of this idea introduces significant bias in background estimation when interpolating from the control region to the SR, MASSIB mitigates this issue by introducing a "smeared" density ratio, which can be learned efficiently through data-level manipulation and used to define an SR that allows for accurate background estimation. By applying it to various types of simulated Large Hadron Collider (LHC) events with realistic background mismodeling, we demonstrate that MASSIB identifies a data-driven SR that achieves high signal concentration consistently across different types of signals while avoiding bias in background estimation. The method does this without making strong assumptions about either the signal or background distribution. We then show that this robustness extends to the validity and strong statistical power of the resulting hypothesis tests for signal detection, demonstrating the potential of this approach for future model-agnostic searches at the LHC.

papers.title: TAPE: Learning General Audio Effect Representations
papers.abstract: Musicians and mixing engineers often can decipher the signal processing chain they hear on a reference recording, then adapt it to new material. We present TAPE (Transformations of Audio Parameter Embeddings), which estimates this processing from the processed reference audio alone. An encoder trained to identify processors in eight major effect families maps the reference to an embedding. A differentiable digital signal processing (DSP) chain decodes the embedding into editable parameters in one forward pass and applies them to a different unprocessed recording. Its modules are equalization, compression, waveshaping, a small residual network, and reverberation. TAPE achieves lower spectral error than DeepAFx-ST, the previous state of the art for single-step regression, and lower spectral error than per-example search over a chain approximating ST-ITO's, while running 275$\times$ faster than that search. Because the decoder outputs DSP parameters, its chain can also run causally: a C++ implementation with the trained weights processed 128-sample buffers 1.8$\times$ faster than real time, with no missed deadlines.

authors.name: Qihui Yang
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

authors.name: Junfei Liu
authors.institution: Institute of Soil and Water Conservation

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Probability Estimation of Data-Dependent Events
papers.abstract:
We study the general problem of estimating $D(\dde(S))$, the probability that an unknown distribution $D$ assigns to an event determined by a sample $S$ of $n$ i.i.d.\ draws from $D$ through a known mapping $\dde$. The estimation algorithm knows $\dde$ and $S$ but does not have access to any additional samples from $D$. This formulation captures classical missing mass, the data-dependent targets of adaptive data analysis and post-selection inference, and the test error of a data-trained predictor, whose estimation was recently studied by \new{Gastpar et al.\ (2024a,b)}. Within this framework we examine the two classical approaches to estimation. The error of the empirical plug-in estimator is exactly a generalization gap, so generalization bounds transfer to it directly. The leave-one-out estimator, which recovers the Good--Turing estimator, is accurate for every mapping that is stable under the deletion of one sample point, including new structured examples such as neighborhoods of the sample and pierced sets.
  The main application of our framework is to error estimation for a predictor that combines a base classifier with memorized exceptions, a structure common in theory and in practice. For it, the test error is exactly the missing mass restricted to the error region of the base classifier, a region selected by the same sample. We formulate the general problem of \emph{adaptive missing mass estimation} to address such dependence and propose a natural hybrid estimator, the Good--Turing estimator restricted to the selected region. We show that the generalization of the base classifier alone does not guarantee the accuracy of this estimator, and derive two bounds on its error: the first one based on the VC dimension of possible error regions and another based on the mutual information of the selected region with the sample.

papers.title: Truthful and Admissible Principal--Agent Testing with Nuisance Parameters
papers.abstract: Statistical contracts reward experimenters according to the evidence produced by a costly study, so the reward rule influences both who participates and what they report. Principal--agent testing theory explains how to prevent ineffective proposals from being profitable. We ask when such contracts can also elicit honest parameter reports if the decision concerns a mean effect but the variance or distributional shape is unknown. Under risk neutrality and a fixed participation cost, we construct menus of e-values --- nonnegative normalized rewards with expected value at most one under every null --- such that (i) agents who know they are null have no incentive to participate, (ii) every alternative type earns positive expected profit and is thus incentivized to participate, (iii) truthful reporting uniquely maximizes expected their reward, (iv) and each contract is admissible: its payouts cannot be pointwise improved while retaining null validity. For Gaussian observations, we treat separately agents who know both mean and variance and agents who know only their mean; in the latter case, truthfulness holds at every variance without requiring a nuisance prior. Multi-sample extensions preserve these incentives and can reward accumulating evidence. Beyond Gaussian models, we show that two independent nonnegative observations suffice to elicit any finite mean above a positive null threshold, without any further distributional knowledge, but one observation cannot combine strict mean elicitation with individual admissibility on this class. Finally, we distinguish the existence of useful tests from the identification needed for truthful contracts. Boundedness is not required, and finitely many null constraints do not by themselves guarantee admissible elicitation.

papers.title: Direct Action-Manifold Modeling for Efficient and Robust Bimanual Manipulation
papers.abstract: Diffusion and flow matching visuomotor policies require iterative denoising or numerical integration for multimodal action generation, introducing latency and execution mismatch. We instead consider a different formulation: conditioned on vision and proprioception, demonstrated bimanual action chunks concentrate in a structured observation-dependent region of joint-action space, making the action target more direct to model than the generative process. Based on this view, we propose the Direct Manifold Action Transformer (DMAT), which reformulates action generation as the direct modeling of clean, observation-conditioned joint-space action chunks from stochastic interpolants, thereby enabling single-step inference without relying on iterative generative inference or auxiliary trajectory-straightening procedures. Within DMAT, local 3D geometry anchors predictions to spatial structure, while State-Consistent Spectral-Time Refinement (STR) reconciles predicted chunks with proprioception and suppresses high-frequency residuals. Across 567 standard and out-of-distribution (OOD) trials per method, DMAT outperformed Improved 3D Diffusion Policy (IDP3) and DiTFlow3D in aggregate success rate, achieving relative improvements of 129.1% and 95.7%, respectively, while generating action chunks 2.06x and 1.34x faster and remaining robust under repeated 50 N interventions. These results pave the way for a novel generative paradigm for efficient and robust bimanual manipulation.

authors.name: Shuo Jiang
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention
papers.abstract: Linear attention scales linearly with sequence length, but its finite-state memory can limit long-context retrieval. In gated linear recurrences, memory retention depends on state decay, which is shaped jointly by gate parameters A_log and dt_bias and by input activations. In controlled Gated DeltaNet (GDN) experiments, both parameters remain highly correlated with their initial values after training, highlighting the importance of initialization. Therefore, we introduce Dual-Axis Memory Initialization (DAMI), which jointly configures these parameters before training. DAMI assigns geometric timescales across heads for varied retrieval distances and a low-high-low input-sensitivity profile across layers. A small activation sample calibrates the GDN-family implementation to match both behavioral targets without adding trainable parameters. Across GDN, KDA, GDN2, Mamba-2, and RWKV-7, DAMI improves average RULER-style retrieval accuracy by 5.29 to 16.71 percentage points over the corresponding random-initialization baselines. Performance on language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and 2K real-world retrieval remains broadly comparable to those baselines. Our code is available at https://speedai.com/research/dami.

papers.title: Extremal character spectra of finite projective systems
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal M$ be a finite spanning multiset of points in ${\rm PG}(k-1,q)$, and let ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ be its character function. For $1\le r\le k$, we study the maximum number of distinct values attained by ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ on the codimension-$r$ flats under a total-multiplicity budget. The spectrum is subject to two natural upper bounds, whose extremal cases lead respectively to $r$-maximum character spectrum ($r$-MCS) and $r$-full character spectrum ($r$-FCS) systems. We establish the existence of $r$-FCS systems in a broad parameter range, and solve the size-constrained extremal problem completely when $r=k-1$, including the minimum-cost multiplicity profiles. For $1\le r<k$, put $M_r=\qbinom{k}{r}$ and $B_r=\qbinom{k-1}{r}$. The minimum size $\nu_r(k,q)$ of an $r$-MCS system satisfies \[\left\lceil\frac{\binom{M_r}{2}}{B_r}\right\rceil\le \nu_r(k,q)\le \binom{M_r-1}{2}+\frac{q^k-q^{k-r}}{q-1}.\] The upper bound is at most $\binom{M_r}{2}$, strictly less when $r\le k-2$, and exact when $r=k-1$. Its proof applies positive additive labelings to the complement of one flat, whose trace is empty while all remaining traces are distinct. For $r=1$, we improve the known upper bounds on the minimum length of such systems. We also develop global moment identities and local flat-incidence bounds that impose strong structural constraints on large character spectra. Under the projective-system correspondence, complementary character spectra are the support-weight spectra of $r$-dimensional subcodes.

authors.name: Gaojun Luo
authors.institution: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

papers.title: Variance-adaptive Chernoff bounds: nonasymptotically valid, asymptotically sharp confidence sets for unbounded means
papers.abstract: Consider the classical statistical problem of sub-Gaussian mean estimation under martingale dependence: given $n$ observations with conditional mean $\mu$ and a known conditional sub-Gaussian proxy $s>0$, we seek a nonasymptotically valid confidence interval for $\mu$. The usual Chernoff interval has half-width $s\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)/n}$; it neither adapts to the actual standard deviation $\sigma\le s$ nor attains the Gaussian quantile $z_{1-\alpha/2}$. We construct an analytically closed-form nonasymptotically-valid interval under martingale dependence whose endpoints, at every iid law with $\sigma > 0$, agree almost surely to first order with $\bar X_n\pm\sigma z_{1-\alpha/2}/\sqrt n$. The two new building blocks are a sub-Gaussian exponential supermartingale with an \emph{empirical} quadratic variance and a cubic correction term, and a sub-Gaussian continuation supermartingale, the former delivering variance adaptivity ("Empirical-Bernstein'' for unbounded data), the latter also providing the Gaussian quantile ("Empirical-Berry-Esseen'' for unbounded data). The same constructions yield a closed-form time-uniform confidence sequence with asymptotically unimprovable half-width $\sigma\sqrt{2\log\log n/n}$. We also give closed-form multivariate ellipsoids with the true-covariance chi-square limit, and extend the scalar Gaussian and LIL constructions to handle heavy-tailed settings where one only knows a bound on any absolute central moment of order greater than two. Experiments show substantial width reductions when the true variance is smaller than the implied variance bound, at small loss in the boundary cases. The surprising (to us) takeaway message is: given any more than two moments, one can construct fully data dependent nonasymptotic confidence sets for the mean that are asymptotically efficient.

papers.title: A Better Critic Matters for Distribution Matching Distillation
papers.abstract: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) trains a few-step student using the difference between a teacher's score and an online critic's estimate of the student distribution's score. We investigate what the critic needs, in capacity and in information, to provide a reliable training signal. On the capacity side, controlled experiments across seven SiT model sizes on ImageNet show that increasing teacher size while keeping a small critic fixed can degrade student quality and cause training collapse. Scaling the critic alongside the teacher, a strategy we call joint scaling, prevents collapse in our experiments and allows the student to benefit from larger teachers. On the information side, rather than forcing the critic to model a step-agnostic mixture of student outputs, we introduce a step-aware critic (STAC) that conditions on the student's generation step to estimate step-specific scores. Together, joint scaling and STAC consistently improve few-step distillation across class-conditional ImageNet generation, text-to-image generation with SDXL and FLUX.2, and text-to-video generation with Wan2.1.

papers.title: A Counterexample to the Alon-Krivelevich Conjecture and a New Lower Bound for Choosability of Bipartite Graphs
papers.abstract: For an integer $k\ge 2$ and $r^2>2(2k-1)\ln (2k-1)$, we construct a bipartite graph $G$ whose two vertex classes are disjoint copies of the family of all $k$-subsets of a $(2k-1)$-element set, two vertices being adjacent when their sets intersect in at most $r$ elements. Assigning each vertex its corresponding subset as its color list, $G$ is not colorable, and thus its choice number $\ch(G)\ge k+1$. This implies that there are graphs with maximum degree $\Delta$ and $$\ch(G)\ge\Bigl(\frac1{32}-o(1)\Bigr)\frac{(\ln\Delta)^2}{(\ln\ln\Delta)^3}.$$ When $k\to\infty$, consequently $\ch(G)/\ln\Delta$ tends to infinity, which disproves the Alon--Krivelevich conjecture. In order to show the uncolorability, we use tools from probability (conditional product measure, nested coupling, and Doob martingale), which we write in an elementary language of weighted counting, and topology (Brouwer fixed-point theorem).

papers.title: Curvature and confinement: robustness of dryland vegetation patterns on sloped, undulating terrain
papers.abstract: We consider a topographic extension to the well known Klausmeier model describing vegetation on sloped undulating terrain with a primary uphill direction and perpendicular small amplitude undulation forming ridges and valleys. Previous studies of this system have shown that, like 1-dimensional sloped terrain, as rainfall levels decrease through a threshold, vegetation forms into patterned states consisting of bands or stripes which are transverse to the primary upslope direction and move slowly uphill. In this paper we investigate the links between undulation amplitude and pattern dynamics, with the goal of understanding how the terrain impacts the resilience of the vegetation. To do this we take advantage of features of the domain, the ridge and valley, to reduce the analysis to two related 1-dimensional problems. Using a combination of analysis and numerical simulations, we argue that a combination of the ridge and valley equations provide insight to the full 2-dimensional dynamics. In particular, we find that at small undulation, the ridge plays a critical role in determining the existence and stability of patterns. For undulation amplitudes smaller than a well-defined threshold, the added sensitivity of vegetation on the ridge to aridity stress causes vegetation to be less resilient than indicated by uniformly sloped models. For undulation amplitudes above this threshold, vegetation is able to survive longer by becoming localized in the valleys, but the amplitude must be increased further to mitigate the original detrimental effects.

papers.title: Segment Anything Pancreas: A Unified MRI Segmentation Model for Pancreatic Cancer Radiotherapy
papers.abstract: Background: Limited tumor annotations and incomplete labels across MRI datasets hinder unified segmentation of pancreatic tumors and organs at risk (OARs) for MRI-guided radiotherapy. Purpose: We propose Pancreas-MedNeXt, a unified model that segments the whole pancreas, its subregions, tumors, and surrounding OARs from one MRI volume. Methods: The model uses a shared MedNeXt encoder-decoder with supervised whole-pancreas and subregion pretraining, followed by multitask fine-tuning. Three output heads predict the pancreatic subregions, tumor, and OARs (stomach, duodenum, kidneys). An annotation-aware loss allows training on partially labeled data without treating unannotated structures as background. Pancreas and tumor were evaluated by three-fold cross-validation on 142 PANTHER patients (92 diagnostic, 50 MR-Linac), subregions and OARs on Cyst-X and AMOS test sets, and pancreas and OARs on 33 external T1-weighted TotalSegmentator scans. Comparisons with nnU-Net, MedNeXt, VISTA3D, and Swin UNETR used the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) with paired bootstrap 95% CIs. Results: Pancreas-MedNeXt achieved the highest mean pancreas and tumor DSC on diagnostic and MR-Linac MRI. Tumor DSC was 58.41% and 42.55%, exceeding task-specific MedNeXt by 4.94 (95% CI: 0.28-9.45) and 5.89 (95% CI: 2.37-9.72) percentage points, respectively. Whole-pancreas DSC was 85.73% and 70.66%. Pretraining improved head, body, and tail DSC by 2.01, 3.00, and 3.78 percentage points over training from scratch. It also achieved the highest DSC for the pancreas, duodenum, and right kidney on AMOS, and for all five organs on external MRI, exceeding the next-best method by 4.92-8.85 percentage points.Conclusion: A single Pancreas-MedNeXt model segments tumors, pancreatic subregions, and OARs on diagnostic and MR-Linac MRI, which could streamline contouring for pancreatic cancer radiotherapy.

authors.name: Xiaofeng Yang
authors.institution: The Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering

papers.title: On the Tur\'an number for the Cartesian product of an odd cycle and a tree
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a fixed tree on at least two vertices. We determine the Tur\'an number and all extremal graphs for the Cartesian product of an odd cycle $C_{2m+1}$ and $T$, for every fixed integer $m\ge1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, in terms of its decomposition family. Every extremal graph is the join of an independent set and an extremal graph for that family. The proof combines the Erd\H{o}s--S\'os theorem with weak stability and progressive induction.

authors.name: Ya-Hong Chen
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Cognitive Inclusivity in AI Coding Assistants: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
papers.abstract: AI coding assistants are commonly used for daily software development tasks. While prior research has examined their impact on productivity and code quality, less is understood about how these tools support diverse ways of thinking. Evidence from non-AI software engineering tools suggests that mismatches between tool design and users' cognitive styles can introduce inclusivity barriers, but it remains unclear whether similar issues arise in AI coding assistants. We investigate how developers with different cognitive styles experience and interact with these tools and whether they exhibit cognitive inclusivity challenges. We conducted a controlled laboratory study with 20 student participants using GitHub Copilot to complete code generation, debugging, and refactoring tasks. Using think-aloud protocols, semi-structured interviews, and inductive thematic analysis, we identify patterns in user interaction. We then apply the GenderMag framework to examine how these patterns differ across cognitive styles. We identify five inclusivity issues concerning how Copilot explains suggestions, supports validation, facilitates learning, exposes its features, and influences the problem-solving process. Our findings suggest that common interaction paradigms in AI coding assistants can privilege certain cognitive styles while introducing additional cognitive effort for others. We derive design implications for more inclusive AI coding assistants.

papers.title: Modulo k-orientations of highly edge-connected signed graphs
papers.abstract: A modulo $k$-orientation of a signed graph is an orientation in which the outdegree and indegree are congruent modulo $k$ at every vertex. We show that, for every odd integer $k\ge3$, every essentially $k$-unbalanced $(6k-10)$-edge-connected signed graph admits a modulo $k$-orientation. This improves the edge-connectivity bound of Zhu [JCTB, 112 (2015)] from $6k-7$ to $6k-10$.

papers.title: Robust-by-Design Distributional Learning from Contaminated Samples
papers.abstract: Modern data analysis pipelines increasingly rely on large datasets assembled through retrieval, scraping, automated filtering, and post-hoc curation, where the observed sample is often a contaminated mixture rather than the target population. Standard distributional objectives either ignore contamination and converge to the wrong target, or retain only a small trusted subset and discard most of the data. We study supervised and unsupervised learning when a clean reference sample is compared with a pooled sample from $r=(1-\epsilon)q+\epsilon z$, where $q$ is the latent target distribution and $z$ is an unknown contaminant. Motivated by settings with noisy membership scores for all observations and exact labels for a small audited subset, we propose contamination-corrected maximum mean discrepancy (CC-MMD), a design-based estimator that combines proxy scores with audited residual corrections to recover the oracle MMD that would have been computed from the latent clean sample. CC-MMD requires no calibration assumption on the proxy scores and no structural assumptions on the contaminant beyond standard kernel regularity. We prove finite-population design-unbiasedness of the corrected kernel sums, establish asymptotic normality of the audit correction, and show consistency for the target discrepancy $\mathrm{MMD}^2(p,q;k)$. Empirically, CC-MMD tracks the oracle under increasing contamination, improves parameter recovery and prediction in contaminated regression, and enables generative models trained on heavily corrupted mixtures to recover the clean target distribution. These results show that contaminated data need not be discarded or treated as the estimand. With sparse trusted labels and abundant noisy supervision, distributional objectives can be made robust by design.

authors.name: Nevena Gligic
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: Machine Learning Sensor Fusion for Water Vapor Radiometry based Tropospheric Delay Calibration
papers.abstract: The next-generation Very Large Array (ngVLA) intends to use 22 GHz water vapor radiometry (WVR) to correct for tropospheric phase fluctuations in its high-frequency bands. However, current delay-retrieval methods do not reach the required accuracy and reliability. As a remedy, we propose a machine-learning based retrieval concept and a preliminary architecture, framed as heterogeneous, multi-rate sensor fusion. Atmospheric reanalysis profiles and surface weather set the context in which per-antenna WVR spectra are used to estimate excess path by a Kalman filter whose parameters are learned from high-cadence calibrator phases. The method is being developed, with planned first validation on the 183 GHz WVR system of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).

papers.title: An Assessment of Water Vapor Radiometry Landscape in ngVLA Context
papers.abstract: The ngVLA intends to utilize Water Vapor Radiometry (WVR) as an approach to lower calibration overheads for tropospheric phase fluctuation correction in its high frequency bands (5 \& 6; 30.5-116 GHz) to levels below those feasible with fast switched reference gain calibration. As a stepping stone to an eventual ngVLA WVR system, the JVLA/ngVLA teams pursued an effort to develop and install a set of MMIC based compact water vapor radiometers (CWVR) and carry out on-sky testing. Most recent tests found that the CWVRs installed on the VLA antennas under this effort were non-functional in tracking visibility phases. As part of the program to develop a WVR system for the ngVLA, this memo summarizes the current landscape of water vapor radiometry experience, the situation with the CWVRs, how they relate to the ngVLA WVR requirements, and the work needed to operationalize the CWVRs as useful test systems and to make broader progress. We currently lack statistically relevant WVR correction data to understand their expected performance for the ngVLA sites. We also discuss parallel additional approaches alternative and/or complementary to the CWVRs. A path involving tests to establish the functionality, stability, sensitivity, and switched power cal/data synchronism of the CWVR system in the lab and on antenna, followed by on-sky tests, and a parallel effort to assess the utility of autocorrelation outputs of the VLA K-band receivers for delay estimation is recommended. Potential paths going beyond traditional excess path estimation methods which may be necessary to meet ngVLA requirements and goals are touched upon.

papers.title: Simple Features Beat Most AI Control Monitors
papers.abstract: AI control relies on monitors to catch a capable model that sabotages its work. These monitors are evaluated on their ability to differentiate honest from backdoored code. We show that on a standard evaluation dataset, simple features beat most monitors without ever running the code, outranking 20 of 24 open-weight models prompted as monitors. The dataset gives its labels away in two ways. People wrote the honest solutions and older language models the backdoors, so the style of the code reveals the class. Additionally, problems that LLMs can backdoor have different characteristics, so basic facts about the problem reveal it too. Swapping one class at a time for code by Claude Sonnet 5 shows that these features reward a contrast between authors, since human code against Sonnet 5's backdoors is easier to separate than the original pairs, 0.95 against 0.79. One in seven backdoors in the standard test set fails our validity checks, which distorts comparisons between attackers. A Sonnet 5 monitor appears to catch 77% of the older models' backdoors but 37% of Sonnet 5's, and 78% against 61% once both are verified. We do not show that published monitors rely on these shortcuts, but our findings suggest that a high score on such a dataset is not by itself evidence of sabotage detection. We release the rebuilt dataset and checks.

papers.title: Benchmarking One-Dimensional Quantum Lattice Boltzmann Methods on Quantum Hardware
papers.abstract: Classical computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods encounter significant computational bottlenecks in large systems and at high Reynolds number flows due to the rapid increase in degrees of freedom, even on flagship supercomputers. As quantum computers emerge, the Quantum Lattice Boltzmann Method (QLBM) has been proposed as a quantum-native alternative for solving fluid dynamics problems. However, until recently, nearly all studies have relied on classical quantum simulators rather than real quantum hardware. This study presents a benchmark of a one-dimensional QLBM implementation executed on three different IBM Quantum hardware. We design and test a quantum circuit for the advection-diffusion equation using amplitude encoding, a Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK)-type collision operator, and a streaming step with periodic boundary conditions. Our numerical experiments evaluate transpiled two-qubit gate count, total circuit depth, runtime, and accuracy metrics including maximum absolute error ($L_\infty$ norm) and root-mean-square error (RMSE). We find that the present collision and streaming operators dominate the overall cost and become the primary scalability bottleneck on current hardware. To mitigate the prohibitive cost of full quantum state tomography on hardware-based benchmarking exercises, we introduce a sampler-based measurement strategy that reconstructs macroscopic density fields directly from computational-basis measurements. This approach substantially reduces measurement overhead while preserving the expected advection-diffusion dynamics on hardware. These results provide a quantitative assessment of QLBM performance in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) regime and identify the principal algorithmic and experimental limitations that must be addressed for QLBM to become viable for fluid dynamics.

papers.title: Stochastic Linesearch Methods for Stochastic Variational Inequality Problems: Parameter-Free Schemes and Non-Monotone Variants
papers.abstract: Much of the existing convergence guarantees and rate statements for stochastic variational inequality (SVI) problems are limited to stochastic approximation schemes that employ constant or diminishing steplength sequences bounded by some reciprocal of the Lipschitz constant $L$ of the map. This requires both knowing such constants and may lead to debilitatingly small steplengths, afflicting the scheme with potentially poor performance. We propose a parameter-free stochastic extragradient method with periodically restarted linesearch (\textbf{SEG-LS}) for solving pseudomonotone and monotone SVI problems. The resulting stepsize sequence is neither monotone nor requires prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant $L$. We show that the iteration and sample complexities for computing a point whose residual has norm at most $\epsilon$ in expectation are $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-4})$, respectively. These results improve to $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-1})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ in the monotone setting. In addition, we propose a periodically restarted biased stochastic linesearch method (\textbf{B-SLAM}) for solving non-monotone SVIs under strict copositivity. The resulting iteration and sample complexities are $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-4})$, respectively. Preliminary numerics support these findings and display promise.

papers.title: Stochastic and Noisy Oracles in Smooth Continuous Optimization
papers.abstract: We review models of inexact computational oracles in smooth continuous optimization and their implications for the convergence, computational complexity, and attainable accuracy of optimization algorithms. We adopt a framework in which zeroth-,first-, and second-order oracles are characterized by quantitative error bounds and may accept additional control parameters that influence both their accuracy and computational cost. We introduce deterministic and stochastic oracle models and illustrate their properties through a variety of examples, including finite-difference approximations, stochastic gradients, and randomized derivative estimators. Particular attention is given to the distinction between absolute and relative errors, bias and variance, and stochastic function evaluations with independent or coupled randomness. A central theme of the review is the use of common analytical tools to recover and compare convergence and complexity guarantees under different oracle models. For deterministic and stochastic first-order methods, we show how a general descent inequality leads to complexity bounds under various assumptions on the objective function and all proposed oracle models. In the stochastic setting, we develop bounds on expected stopping times and the accuracy that can be guaranteed under different oracle conditions. We also examine the total computational complexity of algorithms relying on specific oracle constructions and briefly review models of inexact second- order information and their use in optimization algorithms.

papers.title: A Capability-Aware Backup-Recoverability Filter for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Navigation
papers.abstract: Safe navigation in heterogeneous multi-robot teams faces two coupled challenges: differences in robots' braking and turning capabilities limit how each robot can respond to an approaching neighbor, while simultaneous interactions require a single control action to satisfy multiple collision-avoidance constraints. Together, these challenges can make local safety constraints incompatible with a robot's admissible controls, leaving a decentralized safety controller without a feasible action. We propose a Capability-Aware Backup-Recoverability Filter (CA-BRF), based on the insight that navigation actions should preserve access to a certified recovery maneuver. First, we construct a backup-recoverable set in a shared Cartesian operational space by evaluating whether prescribed backup maneuvers maintain pairwise safety until the robots come to rest. Each maneuver respects the corresponding robot's kinematic and actuation constraints, making the recovery certificate capability-dependent. Second, CA-BRF filters candidate controls by selecting admissible interpolations between candidate and backup actions while coordinating the selection across simultaneous interactions. This preserves backup recoverability while retaining as much of the candidate action as possible and ensures that all pairwise recovery conditions are satisfied by a single executable control for each robot. Together, we establish recursive feasibility and safety for the discrete-time closed-loop system even when the nominal safety-constrained optimization becomes infeasible. The validity and effectiveness of the proposed CA-BRF are validated in simulations with up to 30 heterogeneous robots and experiments of robots with five different kinematic classes.

authors.name: Wenhao Luo
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Filtration theorems, Hilbert functions, and generic freeness
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a finitely generated module over a ring $R$ that is a finitely generated algebra over a Noetherian ring $A$ by $r$ elements. We prove that there are finitely many primes $P_1, \ldots, P_k$ of $A$ such that $M$ has a countable ascending filtration by finitely generated $A$-modules with the property that every factor $F_n$ has a filtration by cyclic modules of the form $A/P_i$, $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that the number of copies $H_i(n)$ of $A/P_i$ that occur in the filtration of $F_n$ is an eventually polynomial function of $n$. We prove a number of bounds on the degrees of these eventually polynomial functions: $r-1$ is always a bound, and the dimension of $\dim(M_P)-1$ is a bound under mild hypotheses. One application is an immediate proof Grothedieck's classic theorem on generic freeness. Several other applications are given.

papers.title: Capability-Conditioned Graph Control Barrier Functions for Zero-Shot Safe Navigation of Heterogeneous Mobile Robot Teams
papers.abstract: Multi-robot systems are increasingly deployed as heterogeneous fleets with diverse kinematic and actuation capabilities. While graph control barrier function (GCBF) methods provide a scalable framework for decentralized safe control, existing approaches typically assume homogeneous robot dynamics. Methods that directly encode robot classes can distinguish known types, but do not represent state-dependent motion capabilities or naturally transfer to unseen robot models. To address this challenge, we propose the Capability-Conditioned Heterogeneous Graph Control Barrier Function (CC-HGCBF), defined in a shared second-order reference-point operational space. This formulation provides a common geometric representation of safety across heterogeneous robots while retaining their model-specific dynamics and admissible control constraints. To enable zero-shot transfer, we introduce the Radial Capability Field (RCF), a compact, fixed-dimensional representation of each robot's state-dependent finite-horizon reachable velocity set. Conditioning the shared graph barrier and decentralized policy on the RCF enables them to adapt to changes in robot state, kinematic constraints, and control limits without relying on predefined robot identities. We jointly train the barrier and policy using proactive safety labeling and neural CBF-QP supervision, and evaluate them on mixed teams containing both seen and unseen robot models. Experiments demonstrate scalable safe coordination and zero-shot transfer to robot models and capability variations withheld during training. Physical-robot experiments further demonstrate zero-shot deployment to unseen kinematic models without retraining.

papers.title: On unitary representations of $p$-adic $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}$ and $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ of purely bad parity
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be $\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$ or split $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$ over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. We classify the irreducible unitary representations of $G$ of purely bad parity: such a representation is unitary if and only if it is of Arthur type, except for one additional family when $G=\textrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)$. In particular, we confirm the remaining case of Ciubotaru's conjecture for $\textrm{SO}_{2n+1}(F)$, namely that every unitary unipotent representation with integral infinitesimal parameter is of Arthur type.

papers.title: On the generic case of Jiang's conjecture
papers.abstract: Jiang's conjecture predicts that if $\pi$ is a generic representation of a quasi-split $p$-adic group, then the $L$-parameter of the Aubert-Zelevinsky involution of $\pi$ must be trivial on $\mathrm{SL}_2$. In this paper, we prove this statement for a general quasi-split group under certain assumptions on the conjectural local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: GhostPrefix: Synchronization-Free Universal Prefix Attacks for ASR Manipulation
papers.abstract: We present GhostPrefix, the first synchronization-free universal adversarial prefix attack against automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems. Unlike prior audio attacks, which are typically crafted per utterance, require synchronization with the victim waveform, or target narrow objectives, GhostPrefix learns a short, reusable audio segment prepended to arbitrary live speech to exert real-time control over ASR outputs without knowledge of the future utterance or temporal alignment. A key challenge is maintaining stable adversarial effects across unknown, evolving speech contexts. GhostPrefix combines token-level losses with a novel representation-level objective for stable, input-agnostic effects. GhostPrefix supports three attack modes: (i) prompted prefix attacks for semantic steering, (ii) targeted prefix attacks for transcript hijacking, and (iii) untargeted prefix attacks for transcription degradation. To remain perceptually inconspicuous, we regularize prefixes toward benign environmental-sound distributions and improve robustness against over-the-air distortions. We evaluate GhostPrefix across 13 open-source ASR models from four families. In digital settings, it achieves average attack success rates of 97.6% for prompted steering and 93.4% for targeted hijacking, while driving word error rate to 1.18 under untargeted attacks. Over the air, it achieves success rates of 91.5% and 89.5% for prompted and targeted modes, respectively. These manipulations propagate into downstream AI-assisted pipelines, including voice assistants and AI note-taking tools, causing systematic semantic misinterpretations. GhostPrefix exposes synchronization-free universal prefixes as a practical, under-explored threat to real-world ASR and downstream applications. Artifacts and demos are available at https://ghostprefix.github.io/.

papers.title: Only constant mean curvature surfaces in $E(\kappa,\tau)$, $\tau\ne0$, have a holomorphic original Abresch-Rosenberg differential
papers.abstract:
For immersed surfaces in the homogeneous spaces $E(\kappa,	au)$ with $	au
e0$, we prove that the original Abresch--Rosenberg differential $[2(H+i	au)p-(\kappa-4	au^2)A^2]\,d\zeta^2$ is holomorphic if and only if the mean curvature $H$ is constant; here $p\,d\zeta^2$ is the Hopf differential and $A=\langle\xi,\partial_\zetaangle$.
