authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Attention Maps Know When to Think: Training-Free Difficulty-Aware Chain-of-Thought for Reasoning Segmentation
papers.abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting has become a standard reasoning strategy in Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), showing strong performance in complex vision-language tasks such as reasoning segmentation. However, our analysis reveals that indiscriminate CoT usage can lead to degraded performance by inducing unnecessary reasoning, a phenomenon we term overthinking. In reasoning segmentation, overthinking often leads to misalignment between the query's intent and visual grounding. To address this, we propose Difficulty-Aware Chain-of-Thought (DA-CoT), a training-free adaptive framework that selectively triggers CoT based on the input's intrinsic difficulty. We find that the entropy of the model's attention maps reliably reflects task difficulty: low entropy indicates confident, localized grounding, while high entropy suggests uncertainty and potential benefit from CoT. DA-CoT uses this entropy signal to determine whether to apply CoT prompting. Additionally, we introduce a Bidirectional Rethinking mechanism that enables the model to automatically flip its reasoning decision when the initial output fails, enhancing robustness by recovering from failures induced by overthinking and underthinking. DA-CoT demonstrates its effectiveness by achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Reasoning Segmentation benchmarks while significantly improving inference efficiency.

papers.title: GRIT: Gradient Masking for Visually Misgrounded Tokens in Text-Rich Reasoning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has recently been extended to vision-language models (VLMs), yet its effectiveness remains limited for text-rich reasoning tasks. We highlight a key factor contributing to this limitation: models frequently arrive at correct final answers despite misperceiving visual information during intermediate steps. We define this phenomenon as Correct-but-Visually-Misgrounded Reasoning (CVMR). Because standard RLVR rewards only final-answer correctness, it fails to differentiate between properly grounded and misgrounded reasoning, reinforcing both equally. Through token-level analysis, we reveal that CVMR tokens exhibit distinct attention patterns that differ systematically from well-grounded ones. Based on this observation, we propose GRIT, a training framework that incorporates visual grounding into RLVR to mitigate the impact of CVMR. Furthermore, to address the lack of text-rich reasoning benchmarks that allow for systematic evaluation across text length and reasoning depth, we introduce GRIT-Bench. Experiments demonstrate that GRIT significantly improves both reasoning accuracy and grounding fidelity over existing RLVR methods.

papers.title: OpenVIO: A Versatile Open-Source Visual-Inertial Odometry System
papers.abstract: Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) is a fundamental topic in robotics research. Beyond research, VIO has been adopted in a wide range of products. In this manuscript, we present OpenVIO, an open-source VIO system for research and practical applications. It is released under the MIT license. OpenVIO supports pinhole and fisheye cameras and extends this support to stitched 360{\deg} images. We describe each part of the system together with its design considerations. We also report benchmark results with other open-source VIO systems on public datasets. OpenVIO is available as open source at https://github.com/93won/openvio.

papers.title: Privacy-Constrained Function Computation in Distributed Databases
papers.abstract: Consider distributed databases that contain both sensitive (private) and non-sensitive (public) attributes. A user seeks to compute a function of public attributes and side information by interacting with the databases and downloading their responses. In this paper, we study the trade-offs among download cost, information leakage about the private attributes, and distortion between the computed function and its reconstruction, referred to as the capacity region. Our main contributions are as follows. For a single database, we provide a complete characterization of the capacity region for general discrete sources and characterize the capacity region of two different setups for Gaussian sources when the computed function is defined as the sum of the public attribute and side information. For distributed databases, we establish inner and outer bounds on the capacity region of discrete sources and we characterize the capacity region when the databases and the side information are mutually independent. As a special instance, we study lossless function computation, and results analogous to the lossy case are obtained.

authors.name: Vamoua Yachongka
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Arlington

authors.name: Remi A. Chou
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Arlington

papers.title: Intersections of fractal sets with rectifiable curves
papers.abstract: Let $K \subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, be a connected compact set and $\phi(t)=tL(t)$ be a gauge function with $L$ non-increasing. We study intersections of $K$ with rectifiable curves and chord-arc curves. We show that if $\int_0^1\frac{dt}{\phi(t)}<\infty$, then there exists a rectifiable curve $\gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $\mathcal H^\phi(K \cap\gamma)>0$. Moreover, for every $0<s<1$, there exists a chord-arc curve $\gamma$ such that $\textrm{H.dim }(K \cap\gamma)\ge s$. Conversely, we show that if $K$ is uniformly porous on lines and $\int_0^1\frac{dt}{\phi(t)}=\infty$, then $\mathcal H^\phi(K \cap\gamma)=0$ for every rectifiable curve $\gamma$ and $\textrm{H.dim }(K \cap\gamma)<1$ for every chord-arc curve $\gamma$.

papers.title: Joint Estimation and Network Configuration in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Distributed consensus-based sensing enables a multi-agent system to collaboratively estimate an unknown state by combining local measurements with information received from neighboring agents. In practice, however, the communication network, transmission delays, and finite-rate communication directly affect the disagreement among agents. On the other hand, agreement among agents does not ensure accuracy, particularly when sensors have different measurement uncertainties. We develop a sampled consensus-plus-innovations framework under realistic wireless network constraints that jointly accounts for inter-agent disagreement and estimation inaccuracy. We derive a computable upper bound on the worst-case steady-state estimation error that captures consensus disagreement due to the communication graph, quantization error, and transmission delay, together with estimation inaccuracy, which accounts for measurement uncertainty against the true state. We then use this bound as a network design objective and propose a semi-distributed auction-based algorithm that jointly modifies the communication graph and link-rate allocation. The proposed method preserves connectivity, converges in finite time to a locally auction-stable network configuration, and reduces the bound on the estimation error at every accepted change. The proposed method has been evaluated on various test cases, and the results show that it reduces the estimation error while maintaining fewer links and allocating moderate link rates in a short time.

papers.title: Simple Cuts, Simple Landscape: Dimension-Free Rank Bounds for Burer-Monteiro Factorizations via Rank-Width
papers.abstract: In this work, we study Burer-Monteiro factorizations of semidefinite programs with unit diagonal constraints. For a real symmetric cost matrix whose rank-width over $\mathbb{R}$ is at most $k$, we prove that every non-flat second-order stationary point of the factorized problem is globally optimal whenever the factorization rank is at least $2k$, independently of the matrix size.

papers.title: Bounds on the maximum denominator of fractional chromatic numbers
papers.abstract: For a positive rational number $x=p/q$, where $p$ and $q$ are coprime positive integers, let $\operatorname{den}(x)=q$. For a positive integer $n$, let $\operatorname{sd}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{den}(\chi_f(G)): |V(G)|=n\}$. Let $D(n)=2^{-n}(n+1)^{(n+1)/2}$. It was proved by Alon, Tuza and Voigt that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)$. In this paper, we prove that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)n^{-\frac12\log_2 n+\frac14\log_2\log_2 n+O(1)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For the lower bound on $\operatorname{sd}(n)$, it was recently proved by Bonamy, Hylasov\'a, Kaiser and Sereni that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge\sqrt{2}$. We prove that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge 3^{1/3}>\sqrt{2}$.

papers.title: The Alon-Tarsi number of 4-regular circulant graphs
papers.abstract: This paper studies the Alon-Tarsi number of connected $4$-regular circulant graphs $C_n(s,t)$, where $1\le s<t<n/2$. We prove that if $n=\ell p^r$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $r\ge 1$, and $t\equiv\pm s\pmod{\ell}$, then $\operatorname{AT}(C_n(s,t))=3$ if $\ell$ is even, or if $\ell\ge 3$ is odd and $p\nmid 2^\ell-2$. We also prove that $\operatorname{AT}(C_{6m}(2,3))=3$ for $m\ge 2$, and $\operatorname{AT}(C_n(1,3))=3$ for $n\ge 8$.

papers.title: Dynamic Persuasion: Managing Reputation under Censored Feedback
papers.abstract: We study a long-run sender who repeatedly communicates about a state to a sequence of myopic receivers and whose credibility is a public score updated from past interactions. Receivers face a lemon loss and an opportunity loss, and their behavior depends on these only through a single index, the tolerance. Because the score records only detected misrepresentations, it rests above the sender's true honesty rate; we characterize this credibility premium in closed form. In a fluid limit in which the score adjusts slowly, no policy earns more than operating at a single credibility level, and the sender's gain from managing credibility equals the value of the premium: against receivers who correct for imperfect detection, that gain vanishes. At a fixed adjustment speed, every policy is bounded by the fluid value plus a term linear in the speed. We then study three policy classes, linear, (s,S), and threshold, obtain the optimal parameters of the linear and threshold classes in closed form, show how receiver losses shape them, and show that, under an approximation, the optimal (s,S) band collapses to a threshold. Simulations of the dynamics agree with the closed forms and indicate where the single-level conclusion stops: bands pay when switching modes is costly, and cycles pay when demand is seasonal.

papers.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
papers.abstract: Although nonconservative forces and extended phase space are individually common topics in Hamiltonian dynamics, their combination is seldom developed explicitly. This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion for nonconservative and nonautonomous dynamical systems formulated on extended phase space. Particular attention is given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. The classic analytical dynamics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates (i.e., canonical coordinates) or functions thereof.

papers.title: Understanding the Energy Cost of Quantized Agents on Shared GPUs
papers.abstract: Quantization can lower the energy of language-model calls and free memory for serving more agents, but its benefit per completed task remains unclear when agents share a GPU. Measurements of fixed requests or isolated agents leave open how the agents' generated work interact with competition for compute and cache. We present a systematic study of precision and admission limits for two agent models on A100 deployments with 40 or 80 GB of memory, using coding and data-analysis tasks with independently verified outcomes. We replay recorded calls across precisions to isolate execution energy and cap the cache to test the value of freed memory. For both models with four admitted agents where requests fit in the cache, 4-bit weights with 16-bit activations execute the same calls with 10-25% less energy than 8-bit weights and activations. Despite this saving, extra work and fewer completions in live runs raise their energy per verified completion by 49%. Where requests compete for cache on the 40 GB deployment, 4-bit weights cost less, and capping their cache raises energy per verified completion by 34% with 16 agents. These results show how generated work and cache demand change the energy benefit of quantization, providing a practical basis for choosing precision and admission limits together.

papers.title: A Robust High-order Approximation of the Gray Thermal Radiative Transfer Equations
papers.abstract: We present a high-order, positivity preserving, and asymptotic preserving approximation of the gray radiative transfer equations. The time and space approximation is done using a diagonally-implicit Runge-Kutta method with stabilized, continuous finite elements, and the angular approximation uses the method of discrete ordinates. We detail a simple and robust inner/outer iteration strategy to solve these equations and prove that the proposed scheme is exactly conservative, independent of iterative tolerances. A maximum and minimum principle is enforced using a conservative redistribution limiting technique, and the method is demonstrated to be robust in the thick diffusion limit.

papers.title: Learning to Interact and Direct: Co-Evolving Video Director Agents
papers.abstract: Video director agents orchestrate multistage production to realize users' creative visions. Emerging research on their self-evolution advances screenplay planning effectively. However, the mutual reinforcement between directing and user interaction remains largely overlooked. Improved interaction clarifies user intent and informs workflow refinement, while more reliable execution shifts collaboration from troubleshooting to creative decisions. To this end, we introduce LIT (Learning to Interact and DirecT), a framework comprises a director agent, a simulated user, and a meta engineer. Simulated user assigns creative tasks to probe the director's weaknesses, while the meta engineer uses the task traces to revise the director's interaction and production strategy. Although this approach can address discovered interaction and production issues, it still relies on passive attribution by the meta agent. This limits its ability to adapt to broader user interaction patterns and production techniques. To solve this problem, we equip LIT with a co-evolution paradigm. The meta agent proactively learns external knowledge, thereby improving its ability to discover problems and propose solutions. The meta agent, simulated user, and director together form an evolutionary closed loop, collaboratively enhances the system's directing and interaction capabilities. Across the Test and OOD Test splits, LIT improves production and Interaction scores by 19.1% and 32.0%, respectively, relative to the initial pipeline. Controlled ablations reveal the correlation between improvements in production and interaction, where the co-evolution mechanism further encourage directing skill and interaction mode exploration.

papers.title: Improving the Optimization Landscape of Matrix Completion with $\epsilon$-close Surrogates
papers.abstract: Non-convex optimization is central to machine learning and AI, yet unlike its convex counterpart, it still lacks a general and principled framework. In this work, we try to highlight the importance of combining noisy perturbations with over-parametrization mathematically under the classic setting of matrix completion (MC). Matrix completion is an important non-convex recovery problem in which only a subset of a matrix's entries is observed, and the remaining entries must be recovered using low-rank constraints. This problem is notoriously difficult because observations are limited. However, we show that by injecting $\epsilon$-level perturbations into the nullspace of the observation mask, we can construct noisy matrix sensing surrogates whose solutions remain $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon)$-close to the ground truth with valid restricted isometry property (RIP) constants. The existence of RIP further enables powerful tensor frameworks to be applied with theoretical guarantees. This approach reflects a broader empirical trend in which stochasticity or noise improves the curvature of the optimization landscape, allowing over-parameterized (a.k.a large) models to better separate signal from noise. Assuming each matrix entry is observed independently, we establish quantitative recovery guarantees without explicit requirements on sampling rate or incoherence, and discuss how such assumptions can further strengthen our results.

authors.name: Ziye Ma
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: Stability of ideal Nash equilibrium points in generalized multi-criteria games, interval-valued games, and existence in single-leader--multi-follower problems
papers.abstract: We study the stability of ideal Nash equilibria in generalized multi-criteria games, in which each player's vector-valued payoff is ordered by a closed cone and the feasible strategy sets depend on the other players' strategies. Under compactness and continuity assumptions, the ideal Nash equilibrium correspondence is upper semicontinuous on the class of games admitting an ideal equilibrium. Our main result does not require the ordering cones to be convex or pointed. In fact, the ideal equilibria are exactly the common equilibria of associated scalar games when all the cones are convex. As consequences of our results, the stability of interval-valued games is derived and existence theorems for single-leader-multi-follower problems are proved for both optimistic and pessimistic sense.

authors.name: Poom Kumam
authors.institution: Center of Excellence in Theoretical and Computational Science

authors.name: Parin Chaipunya
authors.institution: Center of Excellence in Theoretical and Computational Science

papers.title: Observable-Specific Validity Tests for Scientific AI: Controlled Approximations and Intervention Response
papers.abstract: An approximation can reproduce an energy while missing its response, or satisfy an error tolerance without being certified by a given bound. We formulate observable-specific validity records for scientific artificial intelligence (AI) that link a reduction to its reference model, error measure, tolerance, parameter domain, and transformations or interventions. Explicit displacement and velocity certificates for a singularly perturbed oscillator recover distinct convergence orders and provide sufficient validity guarantees. Exact Hubbard dimer relations resolve the different coupling domains accepted by energy and response criteria. Across 16 repeated neural fits, imposing dimensional homogeneity reduces energy scale transfer error from 52.3% to 0.0768% and raises the median fraction jointly satisfying gap and response tolerances from zero to 100%. Paired transformations verify the protected scaling relation, while a coupling crossover identifies the additional information needed for response transfer. A causal model recovers a positive intervention response beneath a strong negative observational association. For two mechanisms observed with Gaussian noise whose responses first differ at order $x^k$, we derive an exact fixed control query requirement scaling as $x^{-2k}$ and verify its full success curve numerically. Together with a 256-task evaluation interface, these results provide independently checkable tests of controlled approximation, physical transfer, and mechanism discrimination in scientific AI.

papers.title: $W^{1,p}$ error estimates of an IPDG and a class of HDG methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) method, a hybrid mixed DG method, and two representative hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains. For any fixed $\epsilon\in (0,\frac{1}{2})$, we first derive optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates for $2\leq p<\frac{1}{\epsilon}$ by combining the interface Green's functions developed in \cite{lq2026} with the Fubini-type weighted estimates established in this paper. These error estimates lead to discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability for $2\leq q<\frac{1}{\epsilon}$, where $q$ is the conjugate number of $p$ such that $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$. Using this stability result and a suitably constructed dual problem, we extend the optimal error estimates to $\frac{1}{1-\epsilon}<p<2$ and subsequently establish the corresponding inf-sup stability for $\frac{1}{1-\epsilon}< q<2$. Thus, both optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates and discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability hold throughout the range $\frac{1}{1-\epsilon}<p<\frac{1}{\epsilon}$, with $q=p/(p-1)$. Note that all of the aforementioned results are free of logarithmic factors and also hold on polyhedral meshes (except for the hybrid mixed DG method). Compared with the conforming finite element method (FEM), establishing such error estimates and inf-sup stability results for DG methods on convex polyhedral domains is more delicate because their analysis involves mesh-dependent norms. Consequently, the operator interpolation theory employed for conforming FEMs cannot be directly applied to DG methods. Finally, a numerical example is presented to illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: What It Costs to Trust a Source: A Reproducible Method for Institutional Assessment of Author Disambiguation
papers.abstract: Records of research outputs are curated with care by universities, and the effort is shaped by the external sources from which candidate records are drawn. The curation required before the author identities in such sources can be trusted is examined, and a reproducible method for estimating its cost is set out. Four tests are described; two can be run on public data alone, and two are conducted against an institution's own curated record, taken from Symplectic Elements Discovery portals. The method is demonstrated on OpenAlex and Dimensions across 30 institutions. Of the publications attributed to matched researchers, 50.4\% were confirmed by the institutional record for OpenAlex and 69.6\% for Dimensions, and fewer trusted researcher profiles were retained from OpenAlex at a matched confidence threshold in each of the 30 institutions. Carried through to effort, integrating OpenAlex requires 1.5 times the person-days of review and entry of Dimensions even when each feed is filtered at the threshold that minimises the amount of review required.

papers.title: The generalized core-EP inverse of operator matrices with generalized Schur complements
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the generalized core-EP inverse of block operator matrices over a Banach algebra. As a result, novel representations and explicit formulae for the core and core-EP inverses of the $2\times 2$ block operator matrices are established.

authors.name: Huanyin Chen
authors.institution: Fuzhou University of International Studies and Trade

papers.title: Twisted second moments of Dirichlet $L$-functions with applications to weighted one-level density
papers.abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function in the $t$-aspect. This is a generalization of Selberg's asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of the Riemann zeta function. As an application, we observe the change and the stability of the weighted one-level density of zeros of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function.

papers.title: The regular set of Ricci limit spaces
papers.abstract:
Let $(X,d,p)$ be a nontrivial pointed Gromov--Hausdorff limit of complete connected Riemannian $n$-manifolds satisfying $\operatorname{Ric}\geq-(n-1)g$. For $1\leq j\leq n$, set
  \[ \mathcal{R}_j(X) = \bigl\{x\in X:\text{ every tangent cone at } x \text{ is isometric to } \mathbb{R}^j\bigr\}, \qquad \mathcal{R}(X)=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^n\mathcal{R}_j(X). \]
  We prove that there is a unique $k$ such that $\mathcal{R}(X)=\mathcal{R}_k(X)$, answering the pointwise regular-dimension question originating in Cheeger and Colding's work~\cite[p408]{CC97}. We construct a volume-corrected heat entropy on RCD space and identify the distributional logarithmic-density defect $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Hess} f)-\Delta f$ by Green-volume regularization.

papers.title: Prevented is Not Protected: What Attack Success Rate Hides about RAG
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is vulnerable to knowledge poisoning, where adversaries manipulate retrieved evidence to influence model outputs. Existing defenses are primarily evaluated using attack success rate (ASR), which obscures defense-induced failures and the mechanisms behind apparent attack prevention. To address this issue, this work introduces \textbf{Aligned RAG Evaluation}, a matched-query protocol that jointly examines clean and poisoned responses, with and without defense. By combining matched conditions analysis, LLM-judge endorsement, and retrieval dependence controls, the proposed framework distinguishes prevented from introduced failures, target mentions from LLM endorsement, and single-passage influence from evidence composition. Experiments on HotpotQA and Natural Questions reveal that existing defenses can introduce unexpected target-positive answers, although they can prevent some attacks, while evaluation criteria can also change defense rankings. Our findings expose critical blind spots in ASR-based evaluation and motivate a more comprehensive assessment of RAG poisoning defenses. The code and the evaluation artifact are available at https://github.com/chxhana/aligned-rag-eval.

papers.title: HWP-synchronous signal induced by misalignment of the sapphire crystal axis
papers.abstract: We investigate the optical response of a rotating sapphire half-wave plate (HWP) with optic axis misalignment, defined as a deviation of the optic axis from the ideal a-cut orientation. We extend the transfer-matrix formalism for calculating the modulated transmittance of multi-layer wave plates with optic axis misalignment and oblique incidence. Using this formalism, we compute the modulated response of a rotating HWP with an optic axis misalignment to linearly polarized incident light. We experimentally validate the model at 90 GHz using sapphire wave plates with intentionally introduced optic axis misalignments of up to 30 degrees. Additional even harmonics are observed for oblique incidence and optic axis misalignment, with odd harmonics appearing when both effects are present. The measured modulation signals are in good agreement with the model predictions. We also evaluate the potential impact of a illustrative small optic axis misalignment of 3 degrees on precision polarimetry. For the configuration considered, the model predicts odd-harmonic amplitudes at the percent level for a single-layer HWP and up to 8% at individual frequencies for a five-layer achromatic HWP.

authors.name: Tomotake Matsumura
authors.institution: Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe

authors.name: Yuki Sakurai
authors.institution: Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe

authors.name: Nobuhiko Katayama
authors.institution: Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe

papers.title: Arithmetical Characterizations of Two Intuitionistic Logical Principles
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the role of negation in arithmetic by analyzing subsystems based on subminimal logic. We introduce NA^PR, a system of subminimal arithmetic equipped with all primitive recursive functions, and answer the following four questions: (1) Can we develop reasonable arithmetic within NA^PR? (2) Can we characterize logical rules Absorption of Negation (An) and Ex Falso Quodlibet (ECQ) by arithmetical principles? (3) Are there strict differences in deductive power among NA^PR, MA^PR, and HA? (4) Do MA^PR and MA, and NA^PR and NA have a similar mutual interpretability relationship as HA? We show the following: First, Heyting Arithmetic (HA) is shown to be a conservative extension of NA^PR for positive formulas. Based on NA^PR, we prove that (ECQ) is equivalent to the definability of disjunction, and that (An) is equivalent to a variant of the least number principle. Furthermore, using the constant domain neighbourhood semantics, we show that the systems NA^PR, MA^PR (written as NA^PR+(An)) and HA (written as NA^PR+(An)+(ECQ)) form a strictly increasing hierarchy of strength. Finally, we demonstrate the essential role of primitive recursive functions in weak arithmetic using classical countermodels.

papers.title: Optic flow in the visual system determines interaction force and collective motion
papers.abstract: Collective motion in animal groups relies on visual cues, yet how individual sensory inputs translate into group-level dynamics remains unclear. Traditional models often assume pre-defined ``3A" rules - avoidance, attraction, and alignment - which require agents to directly access the exact positions and velocities of their neighbors. Here, we propose a minimal model based on fundamental visual processing shared across species: detection of image size and optic flow. We show that the collective patterns, such as vortex and polarized school, emerge spontaneously from the competition between image-size-driven avoidance and optic-flow-driven approach. We find that alignment does not require a pre-assumed velocity-matching rule; instead, it arises from the acceleration of an agent toward regions of strong optic flow. The model shows scale-free velocity correlations and topological visual features observed in animal groups. Our results indicate that the phenomenological 3A forces are not irreducible physical rules, but rather emergent outcomes of basic sensorimotor feedback. This framework provides a physical perspective for linking sensory inputs to macroscopic collective behaviors.

papers.title: On $t$-designs supported by self-orthogonal codes
papers.abstract: We study self-orthogonal $t$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ designs satisfying the condition that the codes generated by the designs are self-orthogonal codes whose codewords of minimum weight $k$ correspond to the blocks. A classification of such designs is given under the conditions that $t\geq \lfloor k/4\rfloor+1\geq2$ and $t \le 11$. This yields a classification of self-orthogonal codes of minimum weight $k$ whose codewords of minimum weight form a $t$-design under the same conditions.

papers.title: Task Vectors Can Be Linearly Decomposed into Interpretable and Controllable Components
papers.abstract: Task Vectors (TVs) provide a compact way to steer large language models, but they are typically treated as atomized directions merely extracted from hidden states, leaving their internal functional structure poorly understood. Motivated by prior work that decomposes in-context learning into Task Recognition (TR) and Task Learning (TL), we ask whether a single TV can likewise be decomposed into functionally meaningful components. We formulate a TR/TL-based decomposition from candidate-label unembeddings, separating each TV into TR, TL, and residual components, and try to optimize the TR and TL coefficients using Bayesian optimization for more effective intervention. We evaluate this formulation across multiple model families, classification tasks, and both instruction- and demonstration-based TVs. Across these settings, TR/TL-based optimization identifies intervention directions that outperform the original TVs. Although optimization over random directions can also improve performance, TR/TL-based search yields more reliable gains, particularly for instruction-based TVs. Moreover, isolated interventions on the decomposed components produce distinct logit-level effects that are consistent with their intended functional roles. Together, these results suggest that TVs are not monolithic steering directions, but can be decomposed into functionally meaningful components that support both interpretation and control.

papers.title: PBSR: Pseudo-Burst Super-Resolution via Zero-Shot Novel View Synthesis
papers.abstract: Burst super-resolution (BSR) achieves higher reconstruction fidelity than single-image super-resolution (SISR) by aggregating sub-pixel information from multiple frames. However, it requires a burst of frames captured under near-static conditions, and such frames are unavailable for single photographs or archival images. We propose Pseudo-Burst Super-Resolution (PBSR), which brings BSR-style reconstruction to the single-image input setting by synthesizing pseudo-burst frames via zero-shot novel view synthesis (NVS). PBSR first generates pseudo-burst frames with realistic parallax using a viewpoint sampling strategy calibrated to the pixel-shift distribution of real burst datasets. The frames are then processed by a BSR backbone equipped with a geometry-aware alignment module that reuses the NVS camera parameters and estimated depth. While the NVS stage is zero-shot, the backbone is fine-tuned with an artifact-aware adaptation so that it can exploit the synthesized frames despite their generative artifacts. Experiments on the BurstSR dataset show that PBSR consistently improves in PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS over the single-frame baseline with the same reconstruction backbone.

papers.title: Memory and Recall of Color Images Using Neural Networks-1 - The Cue-Ball Model based on the Associative Memory Mechanism -
papers.abstract: This paper presents a neural network model for storing and recalling color images of different sizes using the Cue BallRecall Net systems [1,2,3,4,5]. The Cue Ball system consists of a Recall Net composed of multiple memory neurons each responsible for memorizing a single, distinct memory and a large number of neurons that represent image patterns. The images used in this study [6] consist of ten images(see Appendix). The pixel values of these images were converted into digital values and used for subsequent processing. Accordingly, the Cue Ball contains ten Cue neurons, corresponding to the ten images stored in memory. The number of pixels varies among the images, and therefore, the number of Recall neurons comprising the Recall Net also varies accordingly. In this study, the number of Recall neurons was prepared between 106,134 and 360,000, depending on the number of pixels in each image. In this simulation, after the connection weights (wjip, vijp) had been learned, we have used the learning and recall algorithms to investigate whether the Cue neuron which had memorized a specific image could be identified by the Recall Net when that a memorized image has been presented. Therefore, the most important simulation result is which Cue neuron responds when a memorized image is presented to the Recall Net. If the Cue neuron that memorizes the presented image responds, its output can be used to obtain the corresponding image data. By adding a BMP header to the resulting image data, the original memorized image can be accurately recalled.

papers.title: Plasmoid Instability in Inhomogeneous Current Sheets
papers.abstract: Plasmoid instability in inhomogeneous current sheets is investigated using electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulations of collisionless magnetic reconnection. Simulations with and without small random perturbations are compared to examine the effects of symmetry breaking and spatial inhomogeneity. The current-sheet width immediately before disruption remains close to the electron skin depth, whereas the disruption aspect ratio varies significantly between primary and later current sheets. Random perturbations also produce asymmetric plasmoid topologies in which neighboring X points no longer share a common separatrix. These results suggest that spatial inhomogeneity is an important factor in the disruption of dynamically evolving current sheets.

papers.title: Equivariant Ehrhart series for rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes
papers.abstract:
Equivariant Ehrhart theory was introduced by Stapledon (2011) and has since been extensively studied. A central question is whether the numerator in a certain rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series is both a polynomial and effective.
  In this paper, we propose a modification of the denominator in the rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series of rational polytopes. For rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes whose vertices have coordinates that are reciprocals of integers, we show that the resulting numerator is a polynomial and is effective. As an application of our results, we compute the equivariant series of the characteristic quasi-polynomials of root systems.

papers.title: Which Adiabatic Cycles Alter an Action Variable?
papers.abstract: Action variables are adiabatic invariants: their values are preserved during adiabatic time evolutions in completely integrable classical Hamiltonian systems. Nevertheless, an adiabatic cycle can alter how an action variable depends on phase-space variables that are independent of adiabatic parameters. Such a change, which we call action variable holonomy, induces adiabatic torus pumping in phase space. For a family of completely integrable kicked-top systems, a homotopy classification of adiabatic cycles identifies which adiabatic cycles induce action variable holonomy and adiabatic torus pumping. A physical example is also provided.

papers.title: A solution to Haagerup's Problem on decomposable maps
papers.abstract: We prove that a von Neumann algebra $N$ is injective if and only if $\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$ for every linear map $T:\ell^\infty_3to N$, answering a problem of Haagerup (1985).

papers.title: Anomalies of TQFTs coupled to parameter spaces and constraints on ground-state degeneracies
papers.abstract: Anomalies of global symmetries can arise in long-range entangled quantum many-body systems and provide useful constraints on their dynamics. In this paper, we study anomalies of $d$-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) coupled to parameter spaces and their implications for ground-state degeneracies. Specifically, we formulate anomalies as obstructions to constructing parametrized families of TQFTs. We discuss how the classification of these anomalies depends on the choice of topology on the universal $\mathrm{U}(1)$ $(d-1)$-form symmetry. In this framework, we use the projective ground-state bundle obtained by compactifying the TQFT on a spatial manifold to derive a general constraint relating its ground-state degeneracy $N$ to its torsion anomaly $\omega$, expressed as $N\int_W\omega\in\mathbb{Z}$ for bundles $W$ of spatial manifolds over closed surfaces. We apply this constraint to ground-state degeneracies of (2+1)-dimensional TQFTs with framing and 1-form symmetry anomalies and to obstructions to symmetry-preserving TQFTs. We also discuss implications for bordism generators and propose a conjecture on anomaly detection by manifolds fibered over surfaces.

papers.title: Stellar Kinematics and Molecular Gas toward NGC 6357: An Overlooked Earlier Stellar Generation
papers.abstract: We investigate past star formation in NGC 6357 using Gaia DR3 astrometry and Three-mm Ultimate Mopra Milky Way Survey (ThrUMMS) $^{12}$CO($J=1$--0) data. A Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (HDBSCAN) search independently recovers the previously cataloged cluster G352.8+0.6 in addition to Pismis 24, G353.1+0.6, and G353.2+0.6. Isochrone fitting yields an age of $7.9^{+1.5}_{-1.4}$ Myr for G352.8+0.6, compared with approximately 1--3 Myr for the three young clusters. Assuming constant relative plane-of-sky motion, a linear traceback places G352.8+0.6 closest to their reference center approximately 1.8 Myr ago, comparable to their inferred ages. The $+2$ km s$^{-1}$ CO component overlaps G352.8+0.6 in projection and shows localized depressions in integrated intensity around three spectroscopically identified massive stars belonging to G352.8+0.6. The $-4$ and $+2$ km s$^{-1}$ components show complementary projected distributions and intermediate-velocity CO emission in position--velocity space. Assuming that the $+2$ km s$^{-1}$ component was physically associated with G352.8+0.6 and shared its transverse motion, our principal interpretation is that the two molecular structures interacted around the epoch indicated by the stellar traceback, approximately 1.8 Myr ago. The resulting gas compression may have contributed to the recent episode of clustered and high-mass star formation in NGC 6357 and to the formation of Shell A, which subsequent stellar feedback may have reshaped.

papers.title: Shaping and Finite-Blocklength Analysis of Quaternionic Alamouti-Type Codes
papers.abstract: We study finite $2\times2$ Alamouti-type space--time codes associated with classical maximal orders in definite quaternion algebras over $\mathbb Q$. For the family indexed by primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, we prove that the Eisenstein case $q=3$ uniquely minimises the finite quotient-alphabet energy at fixed minimum lattice distance and alphabet size. This ordering holds for every integer $p\geq2$, including when the representatives and their common translation are jointly optimised, with an explicit positive gap for every $q>3$. For uniform finite inputs, we derive a controlled high-SNR expansion of the information variance and determine its limiting ratio to the mutual information deficit. The mutual information expansion specialises arbitrary input fading results and gives an explicit remainder. Standard random-coding and second-order achievability tools relate these quantities to reliability over independently faded Alamouti blocks. All alphabets preserve symbol-wise maximum-likelihood detection at the Alamouti level. Numerical energy, mutual information, and error-rate comparisons support the analysis. Centred comparisons with classical Alamouti, Golden, and Silver codes illustrate the trade-off between reliability, symbol rate, and decoding effort.

authors.name: Yu-Chih Huang
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

papers.title: Solyanik Estimates for Ergodic Flows
papers.abstract: Let $\{T_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a measure-preserving flow on a probability space $(\Omega,\Sigma,\mu)$ and let $T^*$ be the associated one-sided ergodic maximal operator. We show that the sharp Tauberian constant $C(\alpha)=\sup_{\mu(E)>0}\frac{\mu(\{T^*\chi_E>\alpha\})}{\mu(E)}$,$0<\alpha<1$, equals $1/\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$, unless every measurable set is invariant modulo null sets, in which case $C(\alpha)=1$ for every $\alpha$. In particular the Solyanik estimate $\lim_{\alpha\to1^-}C(\alpha)=1$ holds for every measure-preserving flow, and for ergodic flows on nonatomic spaces the estimate $C(\alpha)-1\le 1/\alpha-1$ holds with equality. This answers the one-parameter case of a question of Hagelstein and Parissis. The main point is the lower bound, which is obtained from a lacunary cross-section built out of the upcrossings of a probe function along the orbits of the flow.

papers.title: Sharp Solyanik Estimates for Discrete and Ergodic Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operators
papers.abstract: Let $U_1,\dots,U_n$ be commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations of a probability space, and let $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(\alpha)$ denote the sharp Tauberian constant of the associated ergodic uncentered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator. Hagelstein and Parissis showed that $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(\alpha)-1\lesssim_n(1/\alpha-1)^{1/(n(n+1))}$ as $\alpha\to1^-$ and asked whether this exponent is sharp. We prove that $C^{*}_{\mathrm{HL}}(\alpha)-1\lesssim_n(1/\alpha-1)^{1/n}$ for all such transformations, and that this is sharp: equality of the ergodic and discrete Tauberian constants holds for every action admitting arbitrarily large Rokhlin towers (in particular for every free action, ergodic or not), and the discrete constant satisfies $\widetilde{C}_{\mathrm{HL}}(\alpha)-1\asymp_n(1/\alpha-1)^{1/n}$. For $n\ge2$ the sharp ergodic exponent $1/n$ is strictly smaller than the sharp Euclidean exponent $2/(n+1)$ recently obtained by Mukherjee; the discrepancy is caused by a lattice ``first layer'' effect. We also show that the discrete Tauberian constants of the Hardy--Littlewood and strong maximal operators dominate their Euclidean counterparts; for the strong maximal operator this yields $C^{*}_{\mathrm{S}}=C_{\mathrm{S}}$ for every free action.

papers.title: Some properties of completely convex functions
papers.abstract: We study the class $CC_\alpha$ of completely convex functions of order $\alpha$, defined through a two-point analogous of the classical convexity condition. We give several equivalent characterizations of $CC_\alpha$, together with representation formulas in terms of two auxiliary Schwarz functions linked by a compatibility equation. From these representations, we derive coefficient bounds, a subordination result $zf'/f$, and a two-point Taylor expansion in which the Schwarzian derivative $S_f$ arises naturally as the coefficient of the linear term. This yields a pointwise bound for $S_f$ and a bound for the pre-Schwarzian norm $\|P_f\|_{CC_\alpha}$, improving the classical Yamashita bound when $\alpha\leq 1-1/\sqrt2 $. We also show that, unlike the class $C_\alpha$ of convex functions of order $\alpha$, every $f\in CC_\alpha$ is bounded when $\alpha>0$.

papers.title: Query-Efficient Quantum Multi-Objective Optimization for Materials Configuration Search via Bayesian Weight Selection
papers.abstract: Materials design is a multi-objective problem, and recent advances in quantum optimization make it possible to bring quantum solvers to bear on such problems. The realistic near-term win, though, is not raw quantum advantage but making an expensive, noisy quantum solver usable by spending its calls wisely. Quantum Approximate Multi-Objective Optimization (QAMOO) traces a Pareto front by solving a family of scalarized Ising problems, one per objective-weight vector, with QAOA --- but chooses those weights \emph{non-adaptively}, sampling them at random, blind to what it has already found. We recast weight selection as \emph{multi-objective Bayesian optimization}: our method, BW-QAMOO (Bayes-Weighted QAMOO), picks each next weight by expected hypervolume improvement (EHVI) under a Gaussian-process (GP) surrogate over the weight-to-objective map. On a frustrated alloy-configuration benchmark across $m\in\{3,4\}$ objectives and $n\in\{10,11,12\}$ sites, BW-QAMOO reaches the same Pareto hypervolume as QAMOO's random sampling with a median 33% fewer scalarized solves across the 90/95\% targets and 60--74\% fewer than a uniform-grid baseline), on a genuine (simulated) QAOA solver; a paired Wilcoxon test confirms the saving is significant, and the advantage grows with the objective count m as the weight simplex expands and blind sampling wastes more of the budget. This is a \emph{query-efficiency} result, and we close with the open challenges on the path to real alloy data and hardware.

papers.title: Bar likelihood in local galaxies: the joint role of stellar mass, morphology and environment
papers.abstract:
We investigate how the likelihood of hosting a stellar bar depends on both intrinsic galaxy properties and environment, using a volume-limited sample of central and satellite galaxies from the NASA-Sloan Atlas, spanning isolated systems, low- and high-richness groups, and massive haloes, complemented with halo-based environmental information and probabilistic morphology.
  Using probabilistic bar identification, we quantify the bar likelihood as a function of stellar mass, colour, morphology, halo mass, and cluster-centric distance. We find that stellar mass and morphology are the galaxy properties most associated with the bar likelihood. At fixed morphology, the probability of hosting a bar increases with stellar mass, particularly for late-type galaxies. At the same time, morphology strongly modulates the overall incidence of bars, with early-type galaxies displaying systematically lower probabilities than late-type systems across the stellar mass range. Environmental trends are observed, including halo mass and cluster-centric distance, but these trends largely reflect the morphological composition of the galaxy population. In particular, the decrease in bar likelihood towards the centres of massive haloes reflects the increasing fraction of early-type galaxies, consistent with the morphology-density relation, rather than a direct environmental suppression of bars.
  Our residual analysis finds no statistically significant residual dependence on halo mass or normalized cluster-centric distance after accounting for stellar mass and morphology, within the sensitivity of this sample. Overall, our results show that stellar mass and morphology are the main factors associated with bar likelihood.

papers.title: RC Prediction: A Python Package for Parameter-Aware Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: A nonlinear dynamical system can be characterized by the autonomous evolution of its state in time and its dependence on system parameters. As a parameter varies, the dynamics can change quantitatively and, at bifurcation points, qualitatively. When the governing equations are unknown, a data-driven model should therefore capture both elements from observational data, rather than reproduce the dynamics at a single operating condition only. Parameter-aware reservoir computing (PARC) is a model-free framework for this purpose, where the parameter is supplied to a reservoir computer through an additional input channel. PARC is trained on time series recorded at several parameter values, and the trained reservoir, run in closed loop as an autonomous dynamical system, generates trajectories at parameter values that were never observed. rc_prediction is an open-source Python package that implements this workflow. It provides multi-parameter training of a reservoir, autonomous closed-loop prediction at user-specified parameter values, parameter scans, and a standard echo state network for forecasting at a fixed parameter. Hyperparameter optimization and optional GPU acceleration through PyTorch are also provided. We use three benchmark dynamical systems as examples to demonstrate its usage. As one of the featured applications, here we illustrate the prediction of critical transitions and system collapse: trained only on pre-critical data, the model is queried beyond the training range to predict whether the system collapses, to estimate the critical parameter $p_c^{*}$, and to characterize transient lifetimes.

papers.title: Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties
papers.abstract:
Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$.
  The algebraic input is a numerical characterization of complete flags: a positive-dimensional smooth Fano variety $X$ is a complete flag variety if and only if its pseudoindex $\iota_X$ is at least two and ${\rm ker}({\rm Sym}^2N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}\to N^2(X)_{\mathbb R})$ contains a positive-definite quadratic form. The pseudoindex condition can equivalently be replaced by the divisibility of $-K_X$ by two in ${\rm Pic}(X)$. The key observation is that a single definite quadratic relation excludes surfaces in every fiber of any elementary contraction; standard contraction theorems then yield smooth ${\mathbb P}^1$-fibrations and the characterization of complete flags applies. For the odd-degree theorem, Poincar\'e duality and a mod-two Wu-class argument show that the anticanonical class is divisible by two; comparison of the integral coroot lattices then identifies the flag. Most proofs were developed through extensive discussions with OpenAI's ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6), based on mathematical directions supplied by the author and arguments suggested by ChatGPT; see the AI Disclosure.

papers.title: Faster-than-power-law decay of order parameter correlations in the two-dimensional RP$^2$ model: a rigorous result by vibe-proving
papers.abstract: We consider the RP$^2$ model on the two-dimensional square lattice with nearest-neighbor interactions. It is obtained by replacing the spin in the standard classical Heisenberg model with a director, which does not distinguish two opposite directions. Unlike the standard classical Heisenberg model or the O(3) nonlinear sigma model, the RP$^2$ (and its cousin RP$^3$) model allows point vortex defects classified by $\pi_1(RP^2)= Z_2$ in two dimensions. It is tempting to expect the $Z_2$ vortices to induce a phase transition analogous to the well-established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the O(2) model (XY model) in two dimensions. Indeed, the possibilities of a critical phase or a critical point with power-law correlations of the order parameter in the RP$^2$ and RP$^3$ models have been discussed in the literature. However, the challenging nature of the problem has prevented a definitive conclusion on the phase diagram so far. In this paper, we report a rigorous mathematical proof by Artificial Intelligence (ChatGPT 6 Astra) that the absolute value of the two-point correlation function of order parameters at distance $r$ in the RP$^2$ and RP$^3$ models on the two-dimensional square lattice is bounded above by $C_\beta \exp{(-c_\beta[\log(2+r)]^2)}$ for any finite inverse temperature $\beta\ge0$, with positive constants $C_\beta$ and $c_\beta$ depending only on $\beta$. Namely, the correlation function decays faster than any power of $r$. The proof is formalized and verified in Lean; the formalization is publicly available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.23548847 . A heuristic argument based on a one-parameter effective theory ansatz at large distances combined with the rigorous correlation bound suggests (but does not prove) that the $Z_2$ vortices are always unbound at any nonzero temperature.

authors.name: Masaki Oshikawa
authors.institution: Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe

papers.title: Asymmetric Decline Rather Than Backfire: A Repost-Network Analysis of Japanese Vaccine-Shedding Misinformation on X
papers.abstract: This study investigates the diffusion of vaccine-shedding discourse on X in 2024, focusing on polarization in repost networks and reactions to corrective information. Here, "shedding" refers to the scientifically unsupported claim that harmful substances are released from individuals vaccinated against COVID-19 and cause adverse health effects in nearby unvaccinated people. Using 109,170 posts containing the Japanese term for "shedding" and 478,089 reposts collected from January 1 to December 31, 2024, we constructed a post-level repost network, identified discourse clusters, and examined changes in repost participation before and after major events. The results show that shedding discourse formed a two-pole structure consisting of pro-vaccine and anti-vaccine clusters. After news coverage denying shedding, we found no evidence of diffusion-level backfire in anti-vaccine repost activity. Instead, although the overall topic declined, repost participation in the anti-vaccine cluster decreased more sharply than that in the pro-vaccine cluster. User transition analysis further suggests that this change was not driven by the conversion of strongly anti-vaccine users, but by the entry of previously non-expressive users into pro-vaccine diffusion and the withdrawal of anti-vaccine supporters from repost activity. These findings suggest that corrective information may reshape the composition of misinformation diffusion participants without necessarily converting core opponents.

papers.title: On the Reconstruction of Orthomodular Logic via Restricted Negation
papers.abstract: Orthomodular logic has long been studied as a fundamental logical framework within quantum logic. In addition to its lattice-theoretic foundations, various formulations have been proposed that incorporate specialized implication connectives and more complex logical connectives. In this study, we reconstruct orthomodular logic by introducing a connective referred to as restricted negation, which has received comparatively little attention in the existing literature. We demonstrate that this connective provides a natural and expressive basis for formulating the core principles of orthomodular logic. Furthermore, as a main result, we construct a new proof system for orthomodular logic founded on this connective.

papers.title: Flash Word : ESL Listening Support with Subtitle Skimming
papers.abstract: Listening to English audio with English subtitles is thought to be effective for ESL students to improve listening comprehension skills. However, for those who learn English as a second language it can be hard to finish English subtitles. Also they are unlikely to focus on listening while being busy reading subtitles. We propose Flash Word, a subtitling system which generates and presents shortened intralingual subtitles for English audio by detecting keywords from the script. Flash Word extracts keywords from scripts using an existing algorithm, and shows them one at a time like a flashcard. The system calculates when the keywords are being pronounced and aligns them correctly. Flash Word aims to enable ESL students to focus better on listening by minimising the cost of reading subtitles.

papers.title: Model Sharing Bayesian Optimization for Mechanical Wi-Fi Antenna Control in Multi-Station Environments
papers.abstract: Some commercial Wi-Fi access points used in homes and offices have antennas whose orientations can be adjusted manually. However, selecting suitable orientations is difficult for non-expert users, particularly in indoor multipath environments where reflections and polarization effects complicate the relationship between antenna orientation and link quality. We investigate automatic mechanical antenna orientation control for uplink Wi-Fi communication when the set of active stations changes over time. Building on our previously developed antenna-control system, we propose a model-sharing Bayesian optimization (BO) framework that learns the log-capacity of each link using a separate Gaussian process regression (GPR) model. The framework reuses these models across active-station (STA) combinations and optimizes proportional fairness, equivalently maximizing the geometric mean of the active links' capacities. Exploiting the linearity of this objective in log-capacity, we also derive a upper confidence bound (UCB) acquisition function and its gradient. We evaluate the framework through simulations driven by measured channel capacities and experiments with a mechanical Wi-Fi antenna prototype. The results demonstrate that the proposed model-sharing BO achieves better optimization performance than independent state-specific optimization by reusing the models trained on previously observed links.

papers.title: Reduction numbers under flat extensions
papers.abstract:
The reduction number of the maximal ideal of a localization (or even faithfully flat extension) need not
  increase under specialization. Nevertheless, for
  each fixed local ring the reduction numbers of the maximal
  ideals of all its localization have a finite common bound.

papers.title: Unidentified prediction-risk rankings under spatial sampling with fixed inclusion probabilities
papers.abstract: For Gaussian spatial prediction, we construct positive sampling mechanisms with identical observation laws and conditional site inclusion probabilities, yet opposite risk rankings for two fixed predictors. The construction selects two of four sites and allows independent Gaussian measurement error.

papers.title: Functional-Specific Information Borrowing under Limited Overlap
papers.abstract: Source observations can improve a target average without estimating the entire shared response accurately. We study this distinction in two independent observational samples whose treatment effects share a rough component and differ by a smoother discrepancy. For power-law treatment overlap known for the analysis, known design density, fixed positive Sobolev radii, and Gaussian noise, we derive matching minimax mean squared error bounds with three regimes. Two explicit source-information thresholds determine the onset of rate improvement and attainment of the source-known rate. A signed local correction explains the thresholds: source observations estimate only the part of the integration functional poorly recovered from the target sample. Direct likelihood lower bounds apply to all estimators. Existing joint reproducing-kernel recovery, which does not require propensity inputs, attains these rates, and standard bias-aware intervals are conditionally honest under the specified class. A supplementary zero-overlap result separates estimation error from residual identification uncertainty. Numerical results illustrate both gains and losses when the total number of participants is fixed. The intermediate rate depends on overlap geometry, while smoothness determines its two endpoints.

papers.title: Region-Preserving Accelerated Gradient Methods for Geodesically Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: Accelerated Riemannian optimization methods often require a priori assumptions that their iterates remain in a region where geometric bounds hold. We develop a parameterized inertial dynamical system and an explicit accelerated gradient method for smooth geodesically convex optimization on Riemannian manifolds with locally bounded sectional curvature. Our setting allows both positive and negative curvature without requiring completeness of the ambient manifold. Starting from a curvature-corrected continuous model, we construct the discrete updates by eliminating indefinite cross terms in the Lyapunov energy difference and derive verifiable conditions for a fixed step size. The resulting energy analysis establishes preservation of the initial geodesic ball without assuming iterate containment in advance. We further establish accelerated convergence rates for both geodesically convex and strongly geodesically convex objectives, without requiring restarts.

papers.title: Ullman--Stahl--Totik regularity for conjugacy measures
papers.abstract: We consider probability measures whose distribution functions solve conjugate equations between two compatible systems of increasing maps on the unit interval. We give sufficient conditions for Ullman--Stahl--Totik regularity in terms of finite compositions of the source maps and a lower mass estimate which holds at Lebesgue almost every point. Our result substantially extends a regularity theorem of Mantica and Totik by allowing nonlinear target maps and replacing their assumptions on convexity, concavity, and displacement near fixed points. The proof uses the mass criterion of Stahl and Totik from logarithmic potential theory. We give further sufficient conditions involving uniform mesh bounds, sets where derivatives equal one, and endpoint drift. Examples distinguish these conditions and show that the uniform version of the lower mass estimate can fail for regular conjugacy measures.

papers.title: Root-of-unity limit of the $A_{n-1}$ lens elliptic gamma function solution of the star-star relation
papers.abstract: We study the root-of-unity limit of the multi-component spin solution of the star-star relation whose Boltzmann weights are products of lens elliptic gamma functions, and whose spins take values in $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\times(\mathbb{Z}_r)^{n-1}$. When one of the elliptic nomes tends to a primitive $2rN$-th root of unity, the quasi-classical expansion gives at leading order the classical star-star relation of the Bazhanov-Sergeev multi-spin model; at the next order, under the standard assumptions on the saddle points, a $(\mathbb{Z}_{rN})^{n-1}$-state solution of the star-star relation, which depends on $r$ and $N$ only through $rN$. Real $\mathbb{Z}_n$-symmetric configurations of the continuous spins give elliptic $\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ Kashiwara-Miwa type models labeled by $n$-torsion points. Extended to general primitive torsion points, these include the broken $\mathbb{Z}_{rN}$ model of Quano and Fujii, for which the star-star relation follows from their Yang-Baxter equation when $\gcd(n,rN)=1$. In the trigonometric limit the saddle point equations single out the spectral curve of the $\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ chiral Potts model of Bazhanov, Kashaev, Mangazeev and Stroganov, and the Boltzmann weights become those of that model.

papers.title: A Basic Modal Logic for the Abstract Treatment of Quantum Mixed States
papers.abstract: Quantum logic has developed in various directions since its inception. However, many existing logical approaches either focus only on pure states, or use Hilbert-space models in which the abstract relationship between pure states, mixed states, and probabilities is not made explicit. In this work, we introduce a model designed to handle quantum mixed states abstractly. Furthermore, we construct a proof system for the proposed logic and establish its completeness with respect to the intended semantics.

papers.title: Tropicalization and Polyhedral Completions of Weyl Algebras
papers.abstract: We construct weighted and polyhedral completions of the Weyl algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field and organize them into a structure sheaf on a polyhedral $G$-site. For discretely valued fields, we prove two-sided flatness for $\Gamma$-rational polyhedral completions, yielding exact base change for finitely generated $D$-modules. For compact integral polyhedra, we also construct finite-type integral models whose special fibers are toric face rings and describe the reduction of Gauss points in terms of toric strata.

papers.title: Extended Tropical Characteristic Fibers and Slopes of Binomial D-Modules
papers.abstract: For a holonomic $D$-module, we consider the extended tropicalization of the reduced $L$-characteristic fiber along the family $L_s=F+(s-1)V_Y$. For $A$-hypergeometric systems, this tropical fiber determines the complete $(A,L)$-umbrella and hence recovers the classical slopes. We extend this result to holonomic binomial $D$-modules, for which the tropical jump parameters are exactly the classical slopes at the origin. As an application, a holonomic binomial $D$-module is regular holonomic if and only if there are no tropical jumps along any coordinate subspace.

papers.title: A reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and its extensions
papers.abstract: We study reciprocal moments of the critical points of a polynomial with a simple zero at the origin. A positive similarity transforms a reciprocal derivative companion into a complex symmetric matrix. This gives a short proof of the reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and a refinement for every elementary symmetric function. We determine the optimal constants in the corresponding inequalities for every positive exponent, including the sublinear range, and extend the results to arbitrary positive charges. We also characterize the normal powers of the companion and of its symmetric representative. The resulting criterion gives the complete equality cases in two quartic inequalities and explains the appearance of noncollinear equality configurations at higher orders. We also obtain a closed generating determinant and a quantitative collinearity estimate.

papers.title: P-ContextBench: From Personal Fact Recall to Personalized Agent Behavior
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for personal tasks, yet evaluating their safe use of personal context remains difficult because such contexts are private, fragmented, dynamic, and socially situated. We introduce P-ContextBench, a realistic, verifiable, and scalable benchmark for evaluating personal-context understanding. P-ContextBench constructs population-structured, life-story-grounded digital humans from demographic seeds reflecting the U.S. population. Rather than using explicit, static profiles, P-ContextBench embeds traits, routines, goals, and constraints as implicit evidence across fragmented, evolving synthetic mobile-app records. It evaluates five capabilities: single-source fact recovery, multi-source fact recovery, temporal state tracking, inference of higher-level personal patterns from routine behavior, and safe handling of requests conflicting with persona-specific constraints through compliance, warning, clarification, or refusal. A multi-stage validation pipeline checks persona plausibility, context recoverability, information leakage, evidence preservation, test-case grounding, and human-judge agreement. We instantiate P-ContextBench with 100 personas, 10,088 hidden facts, 18,261 app-trace fragments, and 4,810 verified test cases. The pipeline supports configurable generation across scales and demographic groups. Cost-effective state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs relevant to personal agents achieve below 60% accuracy on temporal tracking, higher-level pattern inference, and constraint-aware action-boundary decisions, with fewer than 10% of test cases answered correctly across all three repeated runs. Even a high-performing SOTA model remains inconsistent on these capabilities. P-ContextBench provides measurable targets for improving the accuracy, reliability, and safety of LLM-based personal agents.
papers.intro:
In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have increasingly been deployed to assist users with personal, everyday tasks, such as shopping, scheduling appointments, and making daily decisions. In these consumer-oriented settings, personalization is a critical requirement. LLMs must adapt to a user’s specific context, including preferences, past events, personal traits, goals, and constraints. Effective personalization requires more than fact recovery or following an immediate user request; it requires applying personal context to produce useful, appropriate, and safe responses. This capability becomes increasingly important as LLMs are embedded deeply in everyday life.

In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have increasingly been deployed to assist users with personal, everyday tasks, such as shopping, scheduling appointments, and making daily decisions. In these consumer-oriented settings, personalization is a critical requirement. LLMs must adapt to a user’s specific context, including preferences, past events, personal traits, goals, and constraints. Effective personalization requires more than fact recovery or following an immediate user request; it requires applying personal context to produce useful, appropriate, and safe responses. This capability becomes increasingly important as LLMs are embedded deeply in everyday life.

Personal-context benchmarking introduces challenges not captured by traditional LLM evaluations. Personal context is rarely available as a consolidated, static profile; instead, it is fragmented across multiple sensitive digital traces such as app logs, which are difficult to access, collect, or share ethically because of privacy concerns. Personal context is often revealed implicitly through behavior rather than direct statements, and it changes over time as preferences, constraints, routines, relationships, and goals evolve. As LLMs are increasingly used for a growing range of everyday tasks, personalization must move beyond the simple fact recall emphasized in existing benchmarks. It requires interpreting how multiple facts jointly shape a person’s needs, constraints, and appropriate actions. Hence, models need to synthesize low-level details into higher-level personal patterns, such as motives, tradeoffs, constraints, and decision rules, and determine how to act when user requests involve conflicting goals, ambiguity, or exceptions. Since personal task patterns vary across individuals and demographic groups, and app usage trends evolve rapidly, personal-context benchmarks should also be extensible across populations and different app sources.

Hence, models need to synthesize low-level details into higher-level personal patterns, such as motives, tradeoffs, constraints, and decision rules, and determine how to act when user requests involve conflicting goals, ambiguity, or exceptions. Since personal task patterns vary across individuals and demographic groups, and app usage trends evolve rapidly, personal-context benchmarks should also be extensible across populations and different app sources.

To address these challenges, we propose P-ContextBench, a realistic, verifiable, and scalable benchmark framework. Unlike existing benchmarks that assign predefined traits to a persona, P-ContextBench first constructs a population-structured life-story-grounded digital human. It starts from demographic seeds reflecting the U.S. population and enriches each seed through a comprehensive interview of over 100 questions covering personal history, family and social relationships, work, health, finances, values, daily routines, and views on social issues, thereby forming a coherent representation of an individual. P-ContextBench then extracts hidden facts—personal traits, routines, goals, and constraints used as benchmark ground truth—from this digital human, rather than assigning them as isolated attributes, thereby grounding downstream app traces in plausible personal context. Building on these facts, P-ContextBench synthesizes each persona’s social circle and longitudinal app traces, which implicitly represent personal context as fragmented, socially situated, and temporally distributed over time without using real user data. The benchmark construction pipeline is scalable: demographic seed selection can target specific populations, and app-agnostic hidden facts and social circles can be instantiated as different app-log formats. Each applicable construction stage is checked by a separate LLM for consistency, recoverability, leakage control, and grounding.

Unlike existing benchmarks that assign predefined traits to a persona, P-ContextBench first constructs a population-structured life-story-grounded digital human. It starts from demographic seeds reflecting the U.S. population and enriches each seed through a comprehensive interview of over 100 questions covering personal history, family and social relationships, work, health, finances, values, daily routines, and views on social issues, thereby forming a coherent representation of an individual. P-ContextBench then extracts hidden facts—personal traits, routines, goals, and constraints used as benchmark ground truth—from this digital human, rather than assigning them as isolated attributes, thereby grounding downstream app traces in plausible personal context. Building on these facts, P-ContextBench synthesizes each persona’s social circle and longitudinal app traces, which implicitly represent personal context as fragmented, socially situated, and temporally distributed over time without using real user data. The benchmark construction pipeline is scalable: demographic seed selection can target specific populations, and app-agnostic hidden facts and social circles can be instantiated as different app-log formats. Each applicable construction stage is checked by a separate LLM for consistency, recoverability, leakage control, and grounding.

To evaluate LLMs’ personal intelligence in an everyday setting, P-ContextBench includes five task types: single-source fact recovery (T1), multi-source fact recovery (T2), temporal state tracking (T3), higher-level personal-pattern inference (T4), and constraint-aware agent behavior (T5). T1–T4 test whether models can recover, connect, update, and reason over fragmented personal context. T5 tests whether models can set appropriate action boundaries when user requests conflict with persona-specific constraints, such as complying, warning, clarifying, suggesting alternatives, or refusing. For example, if a user with diabetes requests to buy chocolate, the model must recognize the health constraint and decide whether to warn, clarify, or suggest an alternative rather than simply comply.

To evaluate LLMs’ personal intelligence in an everyday setting, P-ContextBench includes five task types: single-source fact recovery (T1), multi-source fact recovery (T2), temporal state tracking (T3), higher-level personal-pattern inference (T4), and constraint-aware agent behavior (T5). T1–T4 test whether models can recover, connect, update, and reason over fragmented personal context. T5 tests whether models can set appropriate action boundaries when user requests conflict with persona-specific constraints, such as complying, warning, clarifying, suggesting alternatives, or refusing. For example, if a user with diabetes requests to buy chocolate, the model must recognize the health constraint and decide whether to warn, clarify, or suggest an alternative rather than simply comply.

We provide an implementation that supports configurable benchmark generation at different scales and for different demographic groups. For evaluation, we instantiate P-ContextBench with 100 personas, 500 social-circle contacts, 10,088 hidden facts, and 4,810 test cases. Personas are verified for demographic plausibility, behavioral consistency, psychological coherence and political consistency. App logs are checked to ensure that hidden facts are implicitly encoded and recoverable from the supporting evidence. Test cases are verified to ensure that their answer keys are grounded in the hidden facts, supported by the app logs, and valid for their intended task types. The scoring protocol is cross-checked by human annotators.

On P-ContextBench, we evaluate cost-effective state-of-the-art (SOTA) models relevant to personal-task settings, along with a high-performing reference model. We report overall, worst-run and Pass3 accuracy (Shi et al. 2026), where Pass3 counts a test case as correct only when the model receives full credit in all three independent runs. The cost-effective models achieve 48–62% overall accuracy, but less than 20% Pass3, with Pass3 below 6% on each of T3, T4 and T5. This gap shows that models often succeed inconsistently across repeated runs. Even the high-performing reference model exhibits a persistent reliability gap, achieving 75.49% overall accuracy but only 34.58% Pass3 on average, underscoring the challenge posed by P-ContextBench.
