Failure analysis shows a common pattern: models often find relevant evidence but fail to use it completely. In T3, 81.01% of non-correct cases omit a required current-state hidden fact. In T4, 64.78% omit hidden facts needed to support the reasoning conclusion. In T5, failures center on decision quality, led by constraint-recognition errors (37.53%) and over-refusal (13.62%). Together, these findings reveal concrete targets for improving the reasoning, reliability, and safety of LLM-based personal agents.

papers.title: Rigidity in sharp eigenvalue estimates for differential forms
papers.abstract: For $1\leq p\leq n/2$, we derive sharp eigenvalue estimates for the Hodge Laplacian on differential $p$-forms under the curvature condition introduced by Petersen and Wink, and study their equality cases. Equality recovers the stronger curvature operator lower bound and, in the closed case, leaves only round or Sasakian metrics on the universal cover. For manifolds with boundary, weak $p$-convexity of the boundary makes the unit hemisphere the only equality case for the absolute boundary problem.

papers.title: Numerical Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for rank-three matroids
papers.abstract: We prove the numerical Kawamata--Viehweg conjecture for every matroid of rank three: the Euler characteristic of the inverse of an integral big and nef line bundle class is nonnegative. The proof reduces the conjecture to an inequality for a stone game.

papers.title: Counting on Dummies: Privacy Amplification with Observable Counts and Truncated Batches
papers.abstract: In many practical deployments of Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD), the server processes data in batches. Randomly sampling these batches allows for better privacy bounds via privacy amplification results. Most sampling schemes with provable privacy amplification, including Poisson sampling and random allocation, result in variable batch sizes. The privacy guarantee of these schemes requires that the batch sizes are not revealed. In distributed settings, the server performing the aggregation or any party observing the communication traffic may learn these batch sizes. Furthermore, in both centralized and distributed settings, memory and computation constraints may require each batch to be of some maximum size $s$, necessitating truncation of the batch when it exceeds this limit. It is known that this truncation can result in a significant increase in privacy loss. In this work, we address both of these challenges via a simple mechanism that uses a random number of \emph{dummy points} to privatize the batch size and maintain the privacy guarantee even under truncation. We demonstrate that our mechanism is easy to implement in a distributed setting, and provide a general analysis of this mechanism for both Poisson sampling and random allocation. Our analysis is designed to support efficient and relatively tight privacy accounting. It also effectively amplifies the privacy of the count releases by subsampling, making the expected number of dummy points asymptotically smaller than what is needed to directly privatize the (sensitivity-one) batch sizes with non-negative noise. For Poisson sampling with truncated batches, we demonstrate empirically that our mechanism achieves better privacy--efficiency tradeoffs than the direct accounting for truncation recently given by (Ganesh, 2025).

papers.title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed. Our proof relies on first order expansions for Weil-Petersson moduli space volumes in the $n(g)/g\to 0$ regime. We also obtain some new existence results for small Laplacian eigenvalues.

papers.title: Missing Mergers: On the Unexpected Delay-Time Distribution of Binary Neutron Star Mergers
papers.abstract: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration has detected two binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, GW170817 and GW190425. While no clear electromagnetic counterpart was discovered for GW190425, a coincident counterpart to GW170817 (GRB170817A, AT 2017gfo) was discovered in an early-type galaxy, NGC 4993. Using broad-band photometry and an integrated optical spectrum, we measure a mass-weighted age of $12.4^{+0.5}_{-0.7}$ Gyr (90% credible) for NGC 4993, which is an estimate of the delay time between star formation and merger for the GW170817 progenitor. BNS systems are expected to have a power-law delay-time distribution (DTD) with a minimum delay time, $t_{\rm min}$, of ~10 Myr and index $\alpha \approx -1$. This canonical DTD, convolved with the cosmic star-formation history, predicts ~16 BNS mergers at delay times of ~100 Myr for every BNS merger at 10 Gyr; under it, the chance of detecting even one merger as old as GW170817 is ~1.8%. The long delay time of GW170817 therefore implies many "missing" shorter-delay mergers if the canonical DTD holds. A DTD with $t_{\rm min} = 12.6$ Gyr and $\alpha = -1$ is favored over the canonical DTD by a factor of 40-140, and over short gamma-ray burst and Galactic double-NS DTDs by factors of 80-280. These results are in tension with current population synthesis models, the Milky Way double NS population, and the SGRB population. Explaining the LVK population requires either a dramatically different separation distribution than commonly assumed, an additional channel with a long delay time and comparable rate to an isolated-binary formation scenario, or a large population of BNS mergers missed in the LVK analysis. This result has wide-ranging implications for binary-population synthesis, chemical enrichment models, connections between BNS mergers and SGRBs, and future gravitational wave observations.

papers.title: Integrating of Attack Patterns and Threat Modeling to Support Security Analysis in the Automotive Domain
papers.abstract: The increasing connectivity of cyber-physical systems in the automotive domain demands systematic approaches for identifying and mitigating cybersecurity threats. While ISO 21434 defines a structured workflow for Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA), it does not prescribe a specific method for identifying attack paths or evaluating risks. This paper proposes a conceptual model grounded in ISO 21434 that integrates the STRIDE threat classification with the CAPEC attack pattern database, focusing on the identification of attack scenarios and risk assessment. Its applicability is demonstrated through a case study involving Bluetooth-based threats to an automotive headlamp system.

papers.title: Completeness and Cost of Retrieval Structures for Multi-Tool Requests in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: An agent that must call several tools to fulfill a request fails when the tool retriever omits any one of them, yet tool retrievers are mostly built and evaluated on queries requiring a single tool. We compare representatives of six retrieval structures (flat lexical and dense retrieval, LLM query decomposition, LLM-navigated hierarchies, server-then-tool matching, dependency graphs, and trained set-level retrievers) across two multi-tool testbeds: 345 AppWorld queries with expert dependency labels and 103 MCP-Bench tasks over 257 MCP tools. We measure completeness@k, the share of queries whose entire required tool set appears in the top k, alongside the LLM calls, tokens, and latency that each structure incurs at retrieval time. A motivating analysis on all 7,961 ToolRet queries shows that aggregate completeness mixes two regimes: completeness at 10 is .58 to .67 on single-target queries and .08 to .17 on queries with four or more targets, and the ordering of retrievers on single-target queries reverses on multi-target ones. Across the two testbeds, none of the compared structures that is untrained on the testbed and makes at most one LLM call per query completes more than 10% of AppWorld queries at k = 16. The two structures that do better incur different costs: a set-level retriever trained on 75 to 90 in-domain queries reaches .33 on AppWorld and .58 on MCP-Bench with no LLM calls, while an LLM-navigated hierarchy reaches .30 and .40 with a median of 31 to 38 LLM calls and about five minutes per query. Their failure modes also differ: the trained retriever mostly ranks the missing tools just below the cutoff, whereas the hierarchy finds the target API and stops before collecting its prerequisites. In a downstream check with the official AppWorld agent, tasks with a complete retrieved set succeeded 21 of 21 times, whereas incomplete ones succeeded 2 of 39 times.

papers.title: Foatic Homomesy
papers.abstract: Using a unified method of identifying a telescoping function for each statistic-action pair, we prove conjectures of La Croix and Roby, and of Sheridan-Rossi that various permutation statistics, such as the number of fixed points, are homomesic under Foatic actions: compositions of the Foata bijection and dihedral symmetries of one-line notation. Underlying these results is a family of bijective identities relating permutation statistics across the Foata bijection; one of them --- an unexpected invariance of the number of right-to-left minima under reverse-complement, proved by an explicit bijection --- may be of independent interest. The telescoping functions also turn out to be shared among some Foatic actions, implying that mixing certain actions still yields a constant average on closed walks.

papers.title: CompoSET: A Controlled Single-Edit Benchmark for Vision-Language Compositionality
papers.abstract: Vision-language compositionality is the ability to identify which properties, relations, quantities, and states bind to which entities in both an image and a caption, and to match those bindings across modalities. Existing benchmarks evaluate this ability through image-text matching: a model ranks candidate image-caption match similarities and succeeds when the correct match comes on top. In such datasets, paired images differ by more than a single binding: scene, layout, and content all differ, with 97% of pixels changing on average. Such pairs do not isolate compositionality: results are confounded by global image differences. We introduce Compositional Single-EdiT (CompoSET), a benchmark dataset in which each base image-caption pair has an edited counterpart, or foil, that preserves the scene but differs by a single controlled edit, such as color, count, spatial relation, or object state. Base and foil images preserve naturalistic scene complexity yet are visually near-identical: only 8% of pixels change on average. Our dataset has many foils per base scene (~22) in order to separate scene difficulty from edit difficulty, a distinction one-foil-per-base benchmarks cannot make. CompoSET contains 1,776 instances across 80 naturalistic scenes, spanning 16 edit types in 4 semantic categories, with captions at 3 verbosity levels. We test 22 dual-encoder VLMs and find that all models perform at or below chance level on CompoSET, despite scoring well on prior benchmarks. This suggests that apparent progress under prior image-text matching protocols may be an artifact arising from confounds in benchmark design, and that compositional understanding in dual-encoder VLMs is far from solved. CompoSET addresses the confounds and offers a better controlled benchmark to measure future progress.

papers.title: Mpemba effect as an entropy-production race:Finite-amplitude bounds on crossing times in Markovian relaxation
papers.abstract: Two canonical preparations evolving under a common final Markov generator can exhibit the Mpemba effect because they excite different relaxation modes. We bound the first crossing of their relative entropies by treating relaxation as an entropy-production race. The exact balance $-\dot D=\dot e_p$ implies that a meeting occurs when the accumulated \emph{difference} of normalized entropy-production rates, $\int_0^t(r_H-r_C)\,\mathrm ds$ with $r_\alpha=\dot e_p^{\alpha}/D_\alpha$, equals the initial logarithmic deficit $\ln[D_H(0)/D_C(0)]$. Global entropy-decay inequalities yield a lower crossing-time bound when the entropy-decay constant is bounded from below and the hot rate from above; we supply both certificates. A nonzero cubic moment of a slowest eigenfunction is sufficient for the modified logarithmic Sobolev constant to lie strictly below the spectral gap. Combining established relative-entropy comparison inequalities with Markov contraction and the actual mode amplitudes gives finite-amplitude crossing bounds without a small-deviation expansion. For an exactly strong, reversible three-state preparation these give $0.1659\le t_M\le0.1674$ in model time units, independently certified by outward-rounded interval arithmetic. This interval is narrower than $1\%$ and contains $t_M=0.1662209$. The conservative global-rate comparison used here gives only $t_M\ge0.042$. The hotter preparation starts $6.12$ times farther from equilibrium, yet it reaches $D=10^{-5}$ at $t=0.233$, compared with $t=0.844$ for the colder one. Mean energy crosses later than relative entropy. For a fixed driven generator, nonadiabatic entropy production governs the same balance. These results concern finite-state relaxation in a specified distance and do not predict water-freezing times.

papers.title: Finite-time Mpemba crossings with imperfect preparation
papers.abstract: Two preparations evolving under the same thermal Markov generator can reverse their ordering in relative entropy even when the hotter state retains a nonzero slow-mode component. We derive a sufficient finite-time crossing condition for arbitrary finite irreducible reversible systems. The condition compares the preparations' weights in the entire slowest eigenspace, including degeneracies, and gives an explicit upper bound using the separation from the next distinct decay rate. Exact finite-amplitude entropy comparisons also yield all-mode enclosures and bounds based on a retained spectrum with a controlled omitted tail. A preparation-error inequality converts finite-time sign margins into explicit probability tolerances; extensions account for temperature, generator, and stationary-reference uncertainty. We test the bounds on 2000 predefined network draws with four graph families and 4--64 states. There are 86 numerically located crossings, of which 45 satisfy the simple sufficient condition. In a selected eight-state example, retaining two nonstationary modes certifies a crossing before 1.55163, improving a certified slow-sector endpoint of 2.53951; the located crossing is near 1.26943. A reflecting diffusion in an asymmetric potential supplies a separate physical example, with systematic mesh refinement. Independent interval arithmetic certifies selected spectral bounds, finite-grid first crossings, and an entire preparation-temperature rectangle in a three-state benchmark. The theorem does not require exact slow-mode cancellation, while its numerical sharpness and detection coverage remain model dependent. These results concern relative-entropy relaxation and do not predict water-freezing times.

papers.title: Generative SDEs with Trainable Diffusion and Density-Based Losses
papers.abstract: We develop a divergence-kernel method for jointly optimizing neural SDE drift and diffusion fields and the initial Gaussian distribution, using losses that depend directly on the terminal density. In two- and eight-dimensional Gaussian-mixture experiments, we learn time-independent fields and obtain far fewer off-mode samples than score-based generators with similar parameter counts. The drift attracts samples toward the modes, while the diffusion helps disperse excess probability between them.

papers.title: Hyperbolic Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) seeks to infer the reward function underlying observed behavior, but its predictive accuracy and interpretability depend on how that reward is computed from the underlying features. While prior IRL reward functions have been implemented through a variety of techniques including linear weights, neural networks, or other function approximators, none make assumptions about the geometry of the underlying feature space. Inspired by geometric organization observed in neural circuits, we introduce Hyperbolic inverse reinforcement learning (Hyperbolic IRL), which parameterizes reward as a function of Hyperbolic distance between the feature vector and a learned parameter vector, as well as its Euclidean distance variant. We tested our methods against a range of linear and nonlinear IRL baselines under both deterministic and stochastic policies. Our Hyperbolic approach achieved comparable performance to state-of-the-art models on established benchmarks and excelled in the low data limit and across dense environments. Applied to human navigation among multiple exhibits in a museum room, Hyperbolic IRL reveals reward structure that depends not only on individual exhibit-distance features, but also on non-separable conjunctions between them. Together, these results demonstrate that a Hyperbolic reward parameterization can improve both the predictive accuracy and interpretability of IRL, providing a framework for studying how non-separable, conjunctive structure can begin to explain behavior.

papers.title: Contribution of chromosome-na\"ive transposon-seeded network of DNA templates to intracellular pools of protein dimers of liquid-liquid phase-separated condensate-forming proteins
papers.abstract: Molecular mechanisms governing protein-protein interactions (PPI) contributing to the biogenesis of membraneless condensates remain poorly understood. Observations reported in this contribution demonstrate that liquid-liquid phase-separated (LLPS) condensate-forming proteins and their variants harboring condensate-disrupting human pathogenic mutations are significantly enriched among PPI cascade constituents of the Hybrid Assembly Pathway (HAP) of endogenous multiprotein complexes (EMC). In contrast, no structured or disordered proteins defined as condensate-negative molecules were detected among PPI cascade constituents. Cumulative evidence derived from different lines of analytical inquiries support the concept of the significant contributions of PPI cascade constituents of HAP to the biogenesis of intracellular pools of cell type-specific protein heterodimers assembled with the engagement of at least one protein monomer selected from condensate-forming protein molecules. Analytical evidence documented in this study support the concept that genome-wide chromosome-na\"ive networks of transposon-seeded DNA-templates nucleate the initiation of PPI cascade chain reactions with the capacity to facilitate the concurrent iterative assembly in human cells of both the membraneless biomolecular condensates and the structured multiprotein complexes. AlphaFold 3D modelling of mutation patterns and analysis of partner-bound experimental structures identified variants located at a measured protein dimerization interface. This contribution nominates numerous protein heterodimers of potential relevance to human pathophysiology for follow-up mechanistic studies of potential fundamental and translational impacts.

papers.title: Opening the Box Changes the Cat: LLMs Detect Chain-of-Thought Monitoring - What now?
papers.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning allows large language models (LLMs) to generate intermediate reasoning traces in natural language while solving complex tasks. These traces can support safety monitoring by exposing potentially harmful plans before actions are executed. In this work, we investigate the conditions under which LLMs infer the presence of CoT monitoring from direct and indirect environmental cues and examine how this inference affects their subsequent behavior. Our observations suggest that oversight is an interactive process: while a monitor inspects a model's reasoning, traces left by monitoring interventions can allow the model to infer that its thoughts are being observed and to adapt its behavior accordingly. We show that even subtle environmental cues, such as timing-related signals from timeouts and operation durations, can reveal the presence of monitoring and trigger models to adapt their behavior. Across repeated episodes and interaction loops, we further observe that models can form statistical estimates of the monitor's effectiveness and use these estimates to guide attempts to evade detection. These findings highlight the need to evaluate CoT-based oversight under adaptive conditions, where the monitoring process itself may influence the behavior it seeks to observe.

papers.title: Motivic invariants of birational hyper-K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that birational projective irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds have equivalent integral cohomological motives as commutative algebra objects in $\mathrm{SH}(\mathbb C)$. Consequently, their algebraic K-theory spectra are equivalent as $E_\infty$-algebras, and their integral graded K-theory rings are isomorphic.

papers.title: Short Jennings series and the modular isomorphism problem
papers.abstract:
Let $p$ be an odd prime and $G$ a finite $p$-group whose Jennings series has length at most $p$, that is, $D_{p+1}(G)=1$; when $D_p(G)
e1$ assume also that $G/D_p(G)$ has nilpotency class at most $p-2$. We prove that $G$ is determined up to isomorphism by its modular group algebra $\mathbb{F}_p G$, and indeed by the quotient $\mathbb{F}_p G/\mathrm{I}^{\,
u+1}$, where $\mathrm{I}$ is the augmentation ideal and $
u$ the length of the Jennings series; for an arbitrary finite $p$-group $G$, the quotient $\mathbb{F}_p G/\mathrm{I}^{\,p}$ determines $G/D_p(G)$; and that every automorphism of $\mathbb{F}_p G$ is the product of an automorphism of $G$ and an automorphism inducing the identity on $\mathrm{I}/\mathrm{I}^2$. In particular the modular isomorphism problem has a positive answer for all $p$-groups of exponent $p$ and class less than $p$, and for all $p$-groups of class at most $p-2$ and exponent dividing $p^2$ whose derived subgroup has exponent $p$. Consequently every counterexample in odd characteristic has class at least $p-1$, or a derived subgroup of exponent at least $p^2$, or an element of order $p^3$. The proof combines a descent theorem in the truncated group algebra of a free group, valid for every prime, with a relative rigidity theorem for the unipotent automorphisms of truncated group algebras of groups of exponent $p$, proved through the Lazard correspondence. The bound $p$ is the range in which the logarithm of the group algebra exists.

papers.title: Estimating Irving-Kirkwood pressure profiles from per-atom virial and density profiles: a closure for the contour-dependent term in planar liquid films
papers.abstract: The local pressure tensor of an inhomogeneous fluid is not unique. Two tangential profiles are in common use in planar simulations: the Irving-Kirkwood (IK) profile, which requires a dedicated pass over every pair of atoms for every slab, and the per-atom virial (PAV) profile, which molecular-dynamics codes produce at negligible cost and coincides with the Harasima contour. The two differ by the derivative of a pair quantity, P_T^IK - P_T^PAV = dQ/dz. We show that, for Lennard-Jones free-standing films, Q(z) can be predicted from the density profile and the bulk radial distribution function of the coexisting liquid: under the closure rho2(r1,r2) ~ rho(z1) rho(z2) g(r12), with a pair-local interpolation of g between its liquid and dilute limits, Q is a double integral of rho(z) against a kernel built from u'(r) g(r). The estimator P_T^IK,est = P_T^PAV + dQ/dz is tested against IK profiles measured on the same trajectories for 20 films (thicknesses 7-25 sigma, three cutoff radii, two temperatures): the root-mean-square residual is 0.001-0.002 epsilon/sigma^3, against 0.010-0.021 for the uncorrected profile, and Q, the amount that the contour choice transfers between the two interfaces of a film with non-equivalent surfaces, is recovered to within 0.6% of the surface tension. Applied to the normal component, the same closure removes 83-92% of the spurious structure of the per-atom zz profile, a test that needs no IK run. Its mixture form is validated on three two-component films with an adsorbate unequally distributed between their faces, where it resolves the tension of each face; a clean face recovers the tension of the pure film.

papers.title: Language Non-Invariance in the Ideological Evaluation of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent multilingual studies show that political evaluations of large language models (LLMs) can vary across languages. This paper examines how robust this non-invariance is to questionnaire translation, surface wording, stochastic model variation, and instrument choice, and how much it matters for cross-model comparison. Using the Political Compass, the analysis compares the positions of five LLMs, GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, GPT-5.2, Qwen-2.5, and Mistral Large, on its economic and social axes in English, Spanish, and French, with repeated stochastic draws. Additional exercises use independent Spanish and French translations, paraphrased versions in all three languages, and an alternative ideological instrument. Measured ideological positions are not language-invariant: relative to English, between four and five of the ten pairwise model rankings reverse in Spanish or French, depending on the language and axis. The broad cross-language pattern persists under independent translations, indicating that it is not solely an artifact of the official questionnaire versions. Yet the magnitude of particular shifts, and in some cases their sign, remains sensitive to wording and instrument choice. The evidence therefore supports a measurement interpretation: ideological audits recover language- and instrument-conditioned outcomes rather than a language-free political attribute. Because a single provider serves distinct linguistic constituencies through a common product, without users observing what other constituencies receive, this lack of comparability also bears on political accountability and cross-model comparisons.

papers.title: A model for the dimension of the inertial manifold of the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation
papers.abstract:
We propose a model, based on a spectral energy balance argument, that provides an estimate of the dimension of the inertial manifold of the one-dimensional Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation (KSE). By identifying the wavenumber at which energy injection and dissipation balance out, we obtain a cutoff scale $k_d=\sqrt{5/(3
u)}$ that we use to calculate the number of dynamically active Fourier modes. This leads to an explicit expression $d_M(L,
u)$ for the dimension of an effective manifold spanned by these modes, which we take as our estimate of the inertial manifold dimension and which scales extensively with domain size. Direct numerical simulations are consistent with the estimated spectral cutoff and its scaling with viscosity. Using convolutional autoencoders as well as Lyapunov-based estimates, we show that the minimal latent dimension required for accurate reconstruction coincides with $d_M$ across a range of $(L,
u)$.

papers.title: GNSS Receiver Operating Point Comparison Between Vector and Scalar Tracking Under High-Dynamics
papers.abstract: This paper presents a measurement noise adaptation mechanism for Kalman filter-based carrier tracking in a navigation-aided GNSS receiver designed for launch-vehicle applications. The tracking loop is tuned for 20\,g acceleration steps, which requires a wide bandwidth that makes the loop vulnerable to noise-driven pull-out at low carrier-to-noise density ratios. To resolve this tradeoff, the measurement noise covariance, $R$, is inflated via a two-layer gate: a sigmoid envelope keyed to the signal $C/N_0$, modulated by a dynamics indicator derived from the discriminator output statistics of the Loop Bandwidth Control Algorithm. During noise-dominated periods the gate inflates~$R$, reducing the Kalman gain so the filter coasts on the navigation-aided prediction; when dynamics are detected the gate opens within one epoch, restoring the high-bandwidth tuning. The navigation aiding is formulated as a stochastic control input whose uncertainty is propagated from the navigation EKF covariance. Simulation results on a 20\,g acceleration step scenario show that the adapted vector architecture doubles the lock-retention rate relative to the standalone scalar filter at $C/N_0 = 31$\,dB-Hz. The receiver is implemented in MSGR, an open-source MATLAB GNSS software-defined receiver.

papers.title: Thermal conductivity of Lennard-Jones fluids from equilibrium thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We derive a general expression for the thermal conductivity of simple fluids within a thermodynamic transport theory (TTT) in which the Onsager coefficients of an interacting system are related to those of an ideal reference system through the ratio of the determinants of the Hessians of the relevant thermodynamic potential. The transported quantity is identified with an effective energy density proportional to the rms energy fluctuations of a small fluid cell. The result expresses the thermal conductivity as the product of its dilute-gas value and a function of equilibrium thermodynamic properties, namely the specific heats at constant density and at constant $\rho T$ and the temperature derivative of the latter, with no adjustable parameters. For hard spheres, it reduces to a previously verified expression in terms of the thermodynamic factor. The theory is tested against molecular dynamics results for the Lennard-Jones (LJ) and the truncated and shifted Lennard-Jones (LJTS) fluids in the supercritical region, for densities up to $\rho^*=0.8$, using equations of state based on perturbation theory. For the LJTS fluid, the mean absolute percentage error is below 8\% for all the temperatures considered. For the LJ fluid, the predictions are compared with those of the revised Enskog theory for Mie fluids, using the same equation of state: TTT gives smaller errors at almost all temperatures, with a significant improvement at low temperatures, where the errors are reduced approximately by a factor between two and three.

papers.title: Simple proofs of a Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality and their extensions
papers.abstract: We revisit the one-dimensional Gagliardo-Nirenberg interpolation inequality $$\|u'\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R})}\leq C\|u\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R})}^{1-a}\|u''\|_{L^r(\mathbb{R})}^{a},\qquad u\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}),\quad \tfrac12\leq a\leq 1,$$ and recall how its general form follows from the case $a=\frac12$ by interpolation with an endpoint estimate. For $a=\frac12$ and $p=q=r$, we give four alternative proofs, based on integration by parts (two proofs), on an ODE, and on the $L^p$ theory of singular integrals. The two proofs by integration by parts also cover most of the other admissible exponents. In $\mathbb{R}^N$, the integration by parts arguments give the inequality with explicit constants and, for $p\leq 2$, with the Laplacian in place of the Hessian and a constant independent of the dimension. For weighted measures $w(x)\,dx$, a pointwise version of the ODE argument gives the pointwise inequality $|\nabla u|^2\leq C_N\,Mu\,M(\Delta u)$, where $M$ is the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function, and hence the inequality for Muckenhoupt weights, with the Laplacian and an explicit constant. The integration by parts arguments give it for homogeneous weights of large degree and for superharmonic weights. These results apply, in particular, to power weights and to monomial weights.

papers.title: Spectral Information Content of Diffraction-Limited Images
papers.abstract: High-resolution optical imaging is fundamentally limited by diffraction, which imprints wavelength-dependent structure onto the point spread function (PSF) of the optical system. This intrinsic chromaticity implies that in addition to spatial structure, images encode spectral information. We develop the theory of this spectral information content and provide strategies for its optimal extraction with calculations of Fisher information. We show that polychromatic PSF formation can be expressed as a convolution in logarithmic coordinates and define the corresponding spectral transfer function. We derive this function for the Airy disk and find algebraic decay in spectral log-frequency, implying the existence of arbitrarily fine spectral structure in the ideal, noiseless PSF. We use a differentiable forward model to numerically construct the spectral information eigenbasis and quantify the spectroscopic capability of diffraction-limited imaging across a range of noise and detector systematics. We demonstrate injection and recovery of the constrained spectral modes in a realistic simulated example and compare these results with previously reported methods. Our information-theoretic framework provides a generalisable method for spectral characterisation of PSFs spanning a variety of imaging contexts.

papers.title: Nonlinear Maps Between Irreducible Representations in Graph Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Equivariant linear maps cannot mix non-isomorphic irreducible representations, whereas nonlinear activations can. We develop a degree-resolved version of this nonlinear interaction picture and use the resulting block inventory to construct Specht Triple, a residual on unordered graph triples. On a synthetic structural benchmark with a frozen GIN backbone, Specht Triple reduces aggregate standardised test MSE by 11.05% relative to a parameter-matched Projector Control using the same irreducible projectors and complete linear equivariant space. The results support irreducible decomposition as an inductive bias for nonlinear higher-order equivariant processing.

papers.title: Resource Locks and Fast Unlock for Shared Balances in Certificate-Based Payment Systems
papers.abstract:
Certificate-based payment systems such as FastPay settle a payment with one round of signatures from a quorum of validators and avoid global ordering. The client collects the signatures, and validators never talk to each other. We observe that this client-driven design is complete only as long as no lock is ever undone. Each account has a single writer, a conflict can only come from that writer's own misbehavior, and the account stays locked as the penalty. Stablecoin payments routinely need balances that several accounts debit: treasuries, merchant pools, allowances and subscriptions. There, honest accounts race, locks must be undone, and a quorum certificate held privately by a client can be silently overridden. We prove that no unlock rule is safe in this setting unless certificate formation is visible to validators.
  We present a hybrid protocol. Personal accounts keep the client-driven FastPay path unchanged. A shared resource is a balance with its own version number and a set of authorized accounts. Transactions on shared resources are submitted to any validator and certified by a two-phase broadcast, ECHO then READY. The admission check requires both the sender's nonce and the resource's nonce to be free. Without contention, this path needs no consensus. When concurrent debits split the votes in any proportion, validators detect the split themselves, freeze the affected resource version, and resolve it with one agreement instance scoped to that version. Losing transactions return their sender nonce. We prove consistency, no overdraft, validity, finality and liveness. The protocol composes with the PDCC reconfiguration protocol.

papers.title: Identification through Heteroskedasticity in One Lemma: Partial Identification, an Eigenvalue Construction, and a Caution on Rank Tests
papers.abstract: This teaching note unifies known results on identification through heteroskedasticity, under volatility regimes, GARCH, stochastic volatility and covariate-driven variances, in one lemma with a short linear-algebra proof. A shock is identified up to sign and labelling if and only if no other shock shares its variance path, and shocks that share a path are identified up to a rotation. The rows of the structural coefficient matrix solve one generalised eigenvalue problem that nests Rigobon's (2003) two-regime solution. Rank tests on second moments of the errors count at most linearly independent centred variance paths, not identified shocks. A simulation illustrates each point.

papers.title: Point-to-ellipse series -- Part II Expansion about the center
papers.abstract: Power series expansions in the polar distance about the center are derived for the normal direction and signed distance from an ellipse to points near its center. After extracting constant terms and common factors, the series coefficients are polynomials in the axis ratio and the absolute value of the sine of the polar angle, with rational coefficients. The region of convergence is shown to be the region bounded by the ellipse evolute. The expansions complement previously derived expansions valid for points far from the center.

papers.title: On the estimation of the Gromov-Hausdorff distance
papers.abstract: The paper investigates the Gromov--Hausdorff distance using a new tool, the so-called $\varkappa$-traces of metric spaces. A general lower bound for the Gromov--Hausdorff distance is obtained in terms of $\varkappa$-traces. Using this bound, exact estimates for the distance between an arbitrary metric space and its Hausdorff hyperspace are derived, and the behavior of the metric on transfinite towers (inductive limits) of hyperspaces is studied. In the final part of the paper, the trace machinery is applied to $l^p$-products of metric spaces. A connection is established between computing the Gromov--Hausdorff distance for infinite $l^\infty$-products and partition calculus. Using methods from Ramsey theory (in particular, the Erdos--Rado theorem), $\varkappa$-traces for $l^\infty$-products are computed, and sufficient conditions are obtained under which the Gromov--Hausdorff distance between infinite Cartesian products can be computed exactly. The final section also provides a general estimate for the Gromov--Hausdorff distance between $l^\infty$-products of metric spaces using the Erdos--Rado theorem.
papers.intro:
The concept of distance between metric spaces, introduced by F. Hausdorff [2] and generalized in the papers of D. Edwards [3] and M. Gromov [4], is one of the fundamental tools of modern metric geometry. This theory was developed further in studies that take into account additional structures on metric spaces and also examine properties of the Gromov–Hausdorff distance itself (see, for example, [5, 6, 7]). An important stage in this area was the work of S. A. Bogatyy and A. A. Tuzhilin [8], as well as A. O. Ivanov and A. A. Tuzhilin [9, 10, 11], devoted to computing the Gromov–Hausdorff distance to simplices and to studying its fundamental properties.

The computation and estimation of the Gromov–Hausdorff distance for various classes of metric spaces have been studied in detail in many papers. For instance, in [13, 14] bounds for spheres were obtained, and in [9, 10] methods were developed that made it possible to compute the distances for a wide class of objects, including simplices and ultrametric spaces. In [11] sufficient conditions for the attainability of the upper bound are given by means of the Borsuk number (that is, in the case where the Gromov–Hausdorff distance between two metric spaces equals half the maximum of their diameters). Further examples are the computations of the Gromov–Hausdorff distance between a segment and a circle [15] and between ℤ2\mathbb{Z}^{2} and ℝ2\mathbb{R}^{2} with the Euclidean metric [16]. In [17] two-sided bounds were obtained for the Gromov–Hausdorff distance between lpl^{p}-products of metric spaces.

In classical metric geometry, packing numbers and metric entropy are widely used to describe the capacity of spaces. In the present paper we propose an approach dual to packing numbers, namely the concept of ϰ\varkappa-traces of a metric space. In Section 2 we formalize this notion and prove a general lower bound for the Gromov–Hausdorff distance in terms of the difference of ϰ\varkappa-traces (Theorem 2.11). This tool enables us to prove the strict positivity of the distance between a wide class of spaces and their Hausdorff hyperspaces. In Section 3 this technique is extended to transfinite towers of hyperspaces, where we prove that at some (quite specific) level the Gromov–Hausdorff distance inevitably accumulates up to the diameter of the original space (Theorem 3.10). Finally, in Section 4 the trace machinery is applied to the problem of estimating the Gromov–Hausdorff distance between lpl^{p}-products of metric spaces. We show that the exact computation of traces for Cartesian products with the l∞l^{\infty}-metric runs into set-theoretic obstructions related to colorings of complete graphs. Using classical results of Ramsey theory and the Erdős–Rado theorem on the partition calculus, we obtain exact values of the ϰ\varkappa-traces for infinite products and derive sufficient conditions for the exact computation of the Gromov–Hausdorff distance between them (Theorem 4.11). In the very last subsection (4.3) we obtain a general lower bound for the Gromov–Hausdorff distance between l∞l^{\infty}-products of metric spaces, using only the Erdős–Rado theorem (without using the ϰ\varkappa-trace machinery).

In dimension 11, the celebrated Poincaré–Koebe uniformization theorem states that the universal cover precisely prescribes the size of the canonical bundle of a curve, the trichotomy being whether it is anti-ample, trivial, or ample. This is captured by Kodaira dimension: two curves XX and YY have biholomorphic universal covers if and only if their Kodaira dimensions satisfy κ⁡(X)=κ⁡(Y)\kappa(X)=\kappa(Y). In dimension 22 and more, such an equivalence does not exist, a counterexample being a K3 surface and an abelian surface, whose Kodaira dimension is the same but whose universal covers are very different.

papers.title: On lens spaces which may embed in the complex projective plane
papers.abstract: Using an obstruction derived by Owens and relying on Donaldson's Diagonalisation Theorem, we obtain a complete classification of lens spaces of Lisca type $(2)$ or $(3)$ that are unobstructed from embedding in a homology complex projective plane. This classification is further refined for lens spaces $L(p,q)$ with $p$ even, using an obstruction due to Lidman--Moore--Vazquez based on work of Lin. This article is extracted from the author's PhD thesis.

papers.title: Optimal design problems for the fractional $g$-Laplacian at prescribed energy level
papers.abstract: In this work we study two optimal design problems, of hard and soft obstacle type, in fractional Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. We also establish the connection between these problems, and finally we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the quotients $\Lambda_{s,\mu}(\alpha)/\mu$ with respect to the energy level $\mu$ at the endpoints $0$ and $+\infty$.

papers.intro:
Optimal design problems for eigenvalue-type constants have been studied in several settings. In the local one, the question is how to place an obstacle, or a hole, of prescribed measure inside a given domain so as to optimize an eigenvalue of the associated operator. The first Steklov eigenvalue of domains with holes is optimized in [7] by means of a shape derivative approach, a constrained shape optimization problem in Orlicz–Sobolev spaces is studied in [6], and the local counterpart of the soft obstacle problem considered below — an eigenvalue of the gg–Laplacian penalized on a set of prescribed measure, together with the limit of large penalization — is treated in [25].

In the local one, the question is how to place an obstacle, or a hole, of prescribed measure inside a given domain so as to optimize an eigenvalue of the associated operator. The first Steklov eigenvalue of domains with holes is optimized in [7] by means of a shape derivative approach, a constrained shape optimization problem in Orlicz–Sobolev spaces is studied in [6], and the local counterpart of the soft obstacle problem considered below — an eigenvalue of the gg–Laplacian penalized on a set of prescribed measure, together with the limit of large penalization — is treated in [25].

In the nonlocal setting, optimal design problems for the eigenvalues of the fractional pp–Laplacian were studied in [13], where the hard and the soft obstacle problems are introduced, the optimal obstacle is identified with the set where an extremal vanishes, the two problems are connected by letting the penalization parameter tend to infinity, and the behavior as s↑1s\uparrow 1 is analyzed; see also [8] for the first pp–fractional eigenvalue with mixed boundary conditions. The present work extends the results of [13] to the fractional Orlicz–Sobolev setting.

The present work extends the results of [13] to the fractional Orlicz–Sobolev setting.

The functional framework for that extension was developed in [10], where fractional Orlicz–Sobolev spaces are introduced and their basic properties are obtained; see [1] for the corresponding embeddings and [3] for Neumann and Robin boundary conditions. Eigenvalue problems for the fractional gg–Laplacian were considered in [24] and, in the case without a set constraint, in [11], while regularity properties of the eigenfunctions and of the solutions can be found in [9] and [17]. The essential new feature of this setting is the lack of homogeneity of the modular, which prevents normalizing the admissible functions and forces the problems to be posed at a prescribed energy level; as a consequence, the constants depend on that level in a nontrivial way, and this dependence is one of the subjects of the present paper.

papers.title: Erd\H{o}s--Straus Conjecture: Modular Inversion in Mordell Classes
papers.abstract: We examine modular inversion of strict Grid certificates in a ceiling continued-fraction construction for the Erd\H{o}s--Straus equation. The six Mordell classes modulo $840$ form four inversion orbits. Prime-input pattern frequencies in the pairs $121 \leftrightarrow361 $ and $289 \leftrightarrow 529$ have equal asymptotic limits for every fixed cutoff.
papers.intro:
The Erdős–Straus conjecture asks whether every integer n≥2n\geq 2 admits positive integers x,y,zx,y,z satisfying 4n=1x+1y+1z.\frac{4}{n}=\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{z}. A solution for each prime input suffices for the general conjecture. The six classical Mordell classes [2] are 𝒜={1,121,169,289,361,529}(mod840).\mathcal{A}=\{1,121,169,289,361,529\}\pmod{840}.

The ceiling continued-fraction approach to this equation is described by Ventas in [1]. We study here the strict Grid subfamily, for which inversion has an explicit divisor-complement form. The main statements concern finite certificates, their modular symmetry, and the limiting behavior of their frequencies on primes.

The main statements concern finite certificates, their modular symmetry, and the limiting behavior of their frequencies on primes.

The six Mordell classes modulo 840840 form four inversion orbits. Inversion preserves every Grid-hit indicator below a fixed cutoff, including the first-hit index and the full finite hit pattern. We prove that the inverse representative of a Mordell prime, taken at its maximum Grid cutoff, cannot be a perfect square. For each fixed cutoff, the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions transfers the modular symmetry to equality of limiting prime-pattern frequencies in inverse classes. Finite CRT counts and prime data illustrate the result. The identities do not establish universal Grid coverage or a reduction of that question to four ordinary prime classes.

papers.title: Rational curves of submaximal quantum index
papers.abstract: On a complex toric surface, oriented real rational curves tangent to the toric boundary at real points are distinguished by their value of quantum index. Using variants of usual Welschinger multiplicities, G. Mikhalkin defined enumerative invariants $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ that are provided by a signed count of oriented real rational curves with given quantum index $\kappa$ and fixed tangency points on the boundary of the positive quadrant (the tangency orders being encoded by $\tilde{\Delta}$). We prove that, for most toric surfaces and tangency orders, the invariant $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ is zero in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$. This is done by enumerating tropical curves with Block--G\"ottsche multiplicities. Additionally, we prove that, in many situations, the lower bound, given by the absolute value $|W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}|$ of $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$, for the number of oriented real rational curves is not sharp close to the tropical limit in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$.

papers.title: The complexity of tilting
papers.abstract: Many explicit constructions in algebra are not first-order definable in classical finitary logic, but are, however, definable in infinitary logic. The aim of this paper is to show how infinitary logic can be used to lift model-theoretic results in arithmetic to a quantifier-sensitive form. We apply this idea to a deep result of Jahnke and Kartas on the model theory of perfectoid fields. Our main result is that a first-order sentence $\phi$ holds in the tilt $k^{\flat}$ of a perfectoid field $k$ if and only if a certain sentence $\phi^{\natural}$ holds in a non-principal ultrapower of $k$, where $\phi^{\natural}$ does not depend on $k$ and is only slightly more complicated than $\phi$ itself. In particular, tilting preserves the L\'evy hierarchy in a precise sense. To this end, we prove that the Standard Decomposition of a valued field at a constant $t$ is infinitarily interpretable by formulas of rank at most 1.

papers.title: Positive Values of Inhomogeneous Quadratic Forms of Type (1, 4): The Constant \Gamma_{1,4} = 8
papers.abstract: Let Q be a real indefinite quadratic form of type (1, 4) with determinant D \neq 0. We prove that for every c \in \mathbb{R}^5 there exists x \in \mathbb{Z}^5 such that 0 < Q(x + c) \le (8|D|)^{1/5}, and that the constant 8 is optimal. This establishes a conjecture of Bambah, Dumir and Hans-Gill and, together with earlier work, completes the determination of the sharp constants \Gamma_{r,s} for positive inhomogeneous values of nondegenerate indefinite quadratic forms. The proof combines classical reduction and gap theorems with uniform bounds for circular gaps of quadratic residues. A central step identifies the exceptional parameters in certain resonant reduced families: an explicit ladder of integer witnesses resolves their punctured neighbourhoods, leaving only three rational parameter points, subject to stated coefficient conditions. These are treated by retaining the coupling in a preceding, less reduced form. The remaining covering statements are verified by finite certificates in exact rational arithmetic.

The problem is not merely to find a small value of QQ, but a positive value below the sharp threshold, uniformly over all translates x+cx+c. Classical reduction and one-variable gap theorems settle most parameter ranges. At certain rational resonances, however, the reduced inequalities have genuine exceptional configurations, so repeating the same one-variable argument cannot finish the proof. papers.title: Semipositivity and complete subvarieties of projectivised strata of holomorphic differentials
papers.abstract: We show that if the projectivised stratum $\mathbb{P}{H}_g(\mu)$ associated to a partition $\mu=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ of $2g-2$ contains a complete curve, then \[ \kappa_\mu:=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{m_i(m_i+2)}{m_i+1}>12. \] The weak inequality follows from semipositivity applied to a quotient of the Hodge bundle, while equality is excluded using the second Fujita decomposition and the geometry of fibred surfaces with maximal unitary rank. Consequently, no projectivised holomorphic stratum in genus $g\leq5$ contains a positive-dimensional complete subvariety. In genus $g=6$ the same conclusion holds for \[ (10),\ (9,1),\ (8,2),\ (8,1,1),\ (7,3),\ (6,4),\ (5,5). \]

papers.title: Strong law of large numbers for random semigroups in norm topology
papers.abstract: This paper studies the strong law of large numbers for products of random uniformly continuous semigroups in Banach spaces. We propose a novel approach by treating the product of semigroups as a solution to an integral equation and establish a version of the SLLN in norm topology for arbitrary Banach spaces.
papers.intro:
The theory of compositions of random linear operators can nowadays be considered classical [19, 11, 28, 26]. Besides the purely theoretical interest, it has applications in random quantum dynamics, where either compositions of random linear operators in Hilbert spaces [15, 21] or compositions of random quantum channels [1, 16, 13, 23, 6] are considered.

The theory of compositions of random linear operators can nowadays be considered classical [19, 11, 28, 26]. Besides the purely theoretical interest, it has applications in random quantum dynamics, where either compositions of random linear operators in Hilbert spaces [15, 21] or compositions of random quantum channels [1, 16, 13, 23, 6] are considered.

The strong law of large numbers (SLLN) for random variables acting in a Banach space is well studied [17, 14]. Distributions of compositions of random linear operators were studied in [22, 28, 26, 23]. In particular, the law of large numbers for compositions of random operators in different operator topologies was studied in [24, 25, 21]. Most of the results of this type follow the classical approach of the Chernoff product formula [4, 9, 12], where the convergence of semigroups is typically described in strong operator topology (SOT) and occasionally in weak operator topology (WOT). For example, in [8], the SLLN in SOT was obtained for uniformly continuous random semigroups in uniformly smooth spaces; and in [DzhenzherSakbaev26-unbound], a generalization was obtained for strongly continuous random semigroups. However, these and earlier papers only consider uniformly bounded random operators and usually rely on some geometric properties of the underlying Banach space (such as uniform smoothness), which limits the applicability of such results.

The strong law of large numbers (SLLN) for random variables acting in a Banach space is well studied [17, 14]. Distributions of compositions of random linear operators were studied in [22, 28, 26, 23]. In particular, the law of large numbers for compositions of random operators in different operator topologies was studied in [24, 25, 21]. Most of the results of this type follow the classical approach of the Chernoff product formula [4, 9, 12], where the convergence of semigroups is typically described in strong operator topology (SOT) and occasionally in weak operator topology (WOT). For example, in [8], the SLLN in SOT was obtained for uniformly continuous random semigroups in uniformly smooth spaces; and in [DzhenzherSakbaev26-unbound], a generalization was obtained for strongly continuous random semigroups. However, these and earlier papers only consider uniformly bounded random operators and usually rely on some geometric properties of the underlying Banach space (such as uniform smoothness), which limits the applicability of such results.

In this paper, we present another viewpoint on the product of semigroups by considering it as the solution of an integral equation. This allows us to derive the SLLN for random semigroups from the SLLN for their generators by employing the standard theorems of calculus for the Bochner integral. In particular, this approach produces the SLLN in norm topology for all independent, identically distributed (i.i.d.) random uniformly continuous semigroups in an arbitrary Banach space. This directly generalizes earlier results obtained in [8].

papers.title: Spectral theory for transmission problems and resonances for transparent balls
papers.abstract: We construct generalized eigenfunctions and a spectral calculus for the transmission problem on Lipschitz domains. Then, focusing on the specific example of the ball, we prove a high-frequency resonance dichotomy for Maxwell's equations for a ball with positive, piecewise constant permittivity and permeability. If the product of these coefficients is no larger inside the ball than outside, the cutoff resolvent extends holomorphically to a strip of fixed width below the real axis, including the case of equal products. If the interior product is larger, we construct whispering-gallery resonances exponentially close to the real axis. The proofs use estimates for the transverse electric and transverse magnetic determinants that are uniform in angular momentum and complex frequency, together with a quasimode construction and Rouch\'e's theorem. Explicit generalized eigenfunctions identify these determinants with the scattering poles and give the spectral resolution and the normalization relating the scattering amplitude to the Mie T-matrix.

papers.title: CRCs in four-dimensional lattice graphs
papers.abstract: We obtain series of new completely regular codes in Cayley graphs of the groups $Z_q^n$ with the Lee metric. Combined with binary linear programming methods, the constructions lead to enumeration of all completely regular codes in such graphs for the groups $Z_q^4$, $q\leq 7$ up to parameter matrices.

papers.title: Deformations of Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms
papers.abstract:
Recent work of Brantner and Taelman shows that derived deformation theory and period maps can recover strong mixed-characteristic lifting results. In this paper, we develop a prismatic version of this method for Calabi--Yau varieties over transversal or crystalline prisms, constructing compatible deformations over $A/I^n$ for every $n$ under suitable hypotheses.
  We also apply our method to $F$-split Calabi--Yau varieties over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$. In particular, we consider an $F$-split smooth proper variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$, with $H^{d-1}(X,O_X)=0$ and trivial canonical bundle. We show that $X$ admits a lift to $W_3(k)$.
papers.intro:
The Bogomolov–Tian–Todorov theorem asserts that smooth proper Calabi–Yau varieties over a field of characteristic zero have unobstructed formal deformations, but in positive characteristics, this statement no longer holds. Nevertheless, recent work shows that deformation-theoretic methods still gives lifting results under suitable hypotheses. In particular, Brantner and Taelman [BT24] prove mixed-characteristic unobstructedness and liftability results for Calabi–Yau varieties in characteristic pp by comparing the deformation functor of XX with a derived period functor. Some related theories also appear in the Serre–Tate theory of Calabi–Yau varieties developed by Achinger and Zdanowicz [AZ18], where the Frobenius splitting and the Hodge filtration gives the smooth deformation space under certain conditions.

papers.title: $K$-tropical curves, Riemann-Roch and Serre duality
papers.abstract: We endow a tropical curve with the structure of a ringed space and establish analogues of Riemann-Roch and Serre duality for these ringed spaces. As a corollary, we give a cohomological proof of the tropical Riemann-Roch theorem.
papers.intro:
The Riemann–Roch theorem for algebraic curves relates the degree of a divisor DD to the dimension of the space of meromorphic functions with zeros and poles constrained by DD. Remarkably, an analogous formula holds for tropical curves, with the dimension of a linear system replaced by tropical divisor rank. Baker and Norine [5] first established the corresponding theorem for finite graphs using chip-firing and reduced divisors; the extension to metric graphs was then obtained independently by Gathmann and Kerber [17] and Mikhalkin and Zharkov [26].

papers.title: Coring morphisms presenting nonaffine noncommutative fibre bundles
papers.abstract: We consider noncommutative analogues of associated fibre bundles where the total space, base space and even the fiber may be nonaffine, that is, not represented by a single algebra, and where the structure group is replaced by a Hopf algebra $H$. We choose to describe gluing of affine pieces by corings. In the role of a principal bundle we take an internal $E$-coring $M$ in the monoidal category of right $H$-comodules where $E$ is a faithfully flat right Hopf-Galois extension. In a role of a fibre we either take a left $H$-comodule algebra $F$, or more generally an internal $F$-coring $N$ in the monoidal category of left $H$-comodules. Cotensor products combining these data is used to obtain an ordinary coring representing the total space of an associated bundle. If the fiber coring $N$ is equipped with a choice of an $H$-coinvariant grouplike element, then we exhibit a canonical morphisms of corings from the $H$-coinvariant coring of $M$ to the associated bundle coring which is viewed as a dual to the projection of an associated bundle.

As for the fibre bundles with typical fibre associated to the noncommutative principal bundle, most literature considers just the space of sections of the bundle and only in the case when the fibre is a vector space; this is somewhat similar to considering locally free sheaves in commutative algebraic geometry rather then total spaces of bundles as varieties. Algebra of functions on an affine space is the symmetric algebra on the dual of the underlying vector space; in noncommutative case especially when one works with Hopf algebras it is often not clear when the entirely noncommutative analogue like the tensor algebra, or rather a quantum algebra like Manin’s quantum plane and analogues, is more natural. Nevertheless, the compatible left (co)action on the fibre enables Steenrod-like construction of an associated bundle to a right principal bundle. papers.title: Decomposing super unitary representations using Berezin integration
papers.abstract: I introduce the notion of a family of super unitary representations depending upon odd parameters as well as the notion of a direct Berezin integral of such representations. I use this to decompose the (left-)regular representation of the super Heisenberg group and of a super Heisenberg-like group into smaller (irreducible) subrepresentations. I compare the obtained subrepresentations to the representations obtained by applying (super) geometric quantization of the coadjoint orbits of the corresponding groups. It turns out that for the super Heisenberg group we need coadjoint orbits with an odd symplectic form in order to describe all subrepresentations found in the decomposition and for the Heisenberg-like super group we even need orbits with a non-homogeneous symplectic form.

papers.title: Loose Inductive Set Theories
papers.abstract: We prove that KP, with Full Set Induction, is neither solid nor tight. More generally, every consistent theory obtained from KPC by adding a quantifier bounded set of sentences has a model with a parameter-free definable class surjection from its natural numbers onto its universe. Using such enumerations to define generic extensions by relative interpretations, we show that theories with the stable definable ground property are not tight. Ground definability over MOST and continuum coding over ZFC^{\Pi_3} yield applications to weak inductive set theories with large cardinals and forcing axioms. Finally, solidity for quantifier bounded extensions of MOST with Full Set Induction implies a Ground Axiom formulated using a fixed finite level of genericity; under the same solidity hypothesis, the corresponding extension of full ZFC proves the ordinary Ground Axiom.

papers.title: Evaluating Maternity Leave Reforms When RD Fails
papers.abstract: This paper documents that expansions of UK maternity pay in the 2000s improved children's test scores while reducing maternal employment. Extending job protection alone generated similar employment effects but no detectable impact on children. None of these effects are recoverable with a conventional regression discontinuity (RD) design because eligibility is only imperfectly captured by the available data. We explain why existing corrections for measurement error in RD are not well suited and propose a simple imputation-based solution. The approach preserves RD's main advantages, nonparametric identification and transparency, and remains valid even when measurement error has economic content.
papers.intro:
Although economic gender inequalities are largely driven by motherhood (Kleven et al., 2019b; Kleven et al., 2019a) and the early years are decisive for child development (Heckman, 2006), the consensus is that policy—even when targeted at early maternity—can do little to change either. This view rests on evaluations of family-policy reforms in Scandinavia and continental Europe, which struggle to document any effects (Dahl et al., 2016; Schönberg and Ludsteck, 2014; Kleven et al., 2024), and on evidence pointing to strong cultural determinants of maternal behaviour (Boelmann et al., 2025).

Despite this consensus, there are two arguments for another reform evaluation. The first comes from the observation that most of the reforms considered in the literature are expansions of already generous benefits in strong welfare states, from which it may not be appropriate to draw general conclusions. The reforms in the United Kingdom considered in this paper are evaluated against a weaker benchmark, both in terms of the benefits themselves and the surrounding welfare environment. They also expanded job protection and pay sequentially, which allows for the effects of the two components to be distinguished. In three steps between 2000 and 2007, minimum job protection rose from 14 to 52 weeks and minimum paid leave from 18 weeks (six at 90% of earnings, then 12 at a flat rate of £60.20 per week) to 39 weeks (six at 90%, then 33 at up to £112.75 per week).

It is tempting to remain within the RD framework, treating the actual date of birth as a mismeasured version of the true running variable and drawing on the methods developed for measurement error in RD. Measurement error smooths both the treatment probability and the conditional mean of the outcome as functions of the observed running variable, attenuating—and, in our setting, effectively eliminating—the discontinuities on which RD relies (Davezies and Le Barbanchon, 2017). Most existing corrections rely on auxiliary information, such as instrumental variables or validation data, and require the measurement error to be non-differential “noise”, conditionally independent of potential outcomes (see, e.g., Hullegie and Klein, 2010; Davezies and Le Barbanchon, 2017; Pei and Shen, 2017; Bartalotti et al., 2021). With age-based running variables, this assumption is hard to justify, because the “measurement error” has economic content of its own. In this case, the gap between the actual and the expected date of birth reflects premature or delayed delivery, which may itself affect children’s outcomes. Another commonly employed, less demanding approach is the donut RD design (e.g., Almond et al., 2011; Barreca et al., 2011). It drops observations near the cutoff to restore correct treatment-status classification among the remaining observations, and then extrapolates the estimated regression functions to the cutoff to construct bias-aware confidence intervals for certain causal parameters (Dong and Kolesár, 2023; Noack and Rothe, 2023). Because the measurement error has wide support in our setting, restoring correct classification would require dropping a large fraction of observations, and the resulting extrapolation makes inference uninformative and sensitive to the assumed smoothness of the regression functions.11 1 See Section 3.1 for a more detailed discussion of the applicability of existing measurement-error methods for RD to our setting.

To address the infeasibility of standard RD and the limitations of existing corrections, we propose a simple imputation-based approach. We use an untreated pre-reform cohort to impute average outcomes absent the reform under a parallel-trends assumption. We then recover the treated share at each actual birth date—the fraction of children whose expected birth date falls on or after the policy cutoff—from validation data on actual and expected birth dates. Finally, we recover the conditional average treatment effect on the treated (CATT) at each birth date with a positive treated share by dividing the difference between observed and imputed average outcomes by that share.

This imputation approach preserves important advantages of both RD and difference-in-differences (DiD) designs. As in RD, it nonparametrically identifies treatment effects conditional on the actual birth date. Moreover, unlike conventional RD, it identifies them at every birth date with a positive treated share rather than at the cutoff alone. As in DiD, it recovers counterfactual outcomes under a transparent parallel-trends assumption, whose observable implications we assess among births too early to be affected by the reform. The method is simple to implement and avoids the ill-posed inverse problems that arise in some nonparametric corrections for measurement error in RD (see, e.g., Davezies and Le Barbanchon, 2017). Crucially for our application, it remains valid even when measurement error is differential.

We draw on three datasets. Children’s outcomes come from the National Pupil Database, which records test scores at ages 5, 7 and 11 for the universe of children attending state schools in England. Mothers’ outcomes come from the Quarterly Labour Force Survey, which records employment and hours worked. The validation data come from the Millennium Cohort Study, which records both the actual and the expected date of birth and from which we recover the treatment probability at each actual birth date.

papers.title: Rationally slice knots that are not biprojectively H-slice
papers.abstract: We show that rationally slice knots need not be biprojectively H-slice (BPH-slice), answering a question in the study of the rational knot concordance group. Our main tool is a lattice embedding obstruction to H-sliceness in $\#^n\mathbb{CP}^2$ for knots with vanishing signature, extending work of Kjuchukova--Miller--Ray--Sakall{\i}. We apply the obstruction to an infinite family of rationally slice knots, beginning with $8_{18}$. As additional applications, we obstruct the BPH-sliceness of a family of 2-bridge knots which is not obstructed by the instanton knot concordance invariant $r_0$, we obstruct a non-alternating family of Montesinos knots, and we give prime alternating knots that are topologically but not smoothly biprojectively H-slice. We discuss why these knots remain plausible candidates for detecting exotic smooth structures on $\#^n\mathbb{CP}^2$ and suggest natural sources of further candidates.

papers.title: An end-to-end CNN search for ultra-short-period planets in TESS: from the blend ceiling to the independent validation of TOI-6662 b
papers.abstract:
We trained a convolutional neural network to detect ultra-short-period planets in TESS photometry, following the procedure now standard in the field: synthetic transits as positives, eclipsing binaries as negatives. Measured that way it reaches an area under the ROC curve of 0.97. Keeping the same model and the same planets, but replacing the negatives with false positives that the TESS Follow-up Observing Program has actually rejected, the area falls to 0.50 -- the value of a random classifier. The conventional benchmark had been measuring a problem that does not exist.
  The reason is physical, and it bounds what is possible. Of 145 such false positives examined at pixel level, 42% are blends: eclipses belonging to a neighbouring star, diluted into the target aperture. Their light curves are indistinguishable from shallow transits, capping the attainable area at 1 - f/2 = 0.79. Retraining on real false positives reaches 0.80 +/- 0.06, confirming the ceiling independently. No classifier reading a single-band light curve can do better.
  A detector alone is the wrong instrument. We built CASCADE-USP, a pipeline chaining the network with difference-image centroid analysis, scene modelling with high-resolution imaging and the Gaia astrometric solution, supplying in sequence what the light curve lacks. Its output is a prioritisation, not a verdict: it records what evidence each candidate still needs. Only the classifier is domain-specific; the other stages apply to any transit candidate. Of 435 unresolved TESS candidates it isolates 20; 19 prove false positives, traced to causes invisible in TESS photometry. The twentieth is TOI-6662 b, an Earth-sized planet (0.94 +/- 0.03 Earth radii) orbiting an M dwarf every 7.05 hours. Our validation, independent of a concurrent one, agrees with it in planetary parameters and classification, closing the CASCADE procedure with an external check.
papers.intro:
The study of ultra-short-period planets opens with CoRoT-7b (Léger et al., 2009), the first transiting super-Earth with a measured radius, on a 0.854 d orbit around a G9 dwarf, and with Kepler-10b (Batalha et al., 2011), the first rocky planet identified by Kepler. Both established the existence of a population of terrestrial planets on orbits of hours, subject to conditions without analogue in the Solar System.

The study of ultra-short-period planets opens with CoRoT-7b (Léger et al., 2009), the first transiting super-Earth with a measured radius, on a 0.854 d orbit around a G9 dwarf, and with Kepler-10b (Batalha et al., 2011), the first rocky planet identified by Kepler. Both established the existence of a population of terrestrial planets on orbits of hours, subject to conditions without analogue in the Solar System.

Ultra-short-period planets (USPs), conventionally defined by an orbital period below one day (Winn et al., 2018), constitute a singular population. They orbit at distances of a few stellar radii, where they receive irradiations of hundreds to thousands of times the terrestrial value and experience temperatures sufficient to melt silicates on their dayside. They are, almost without exception, of terrestrial size or smaller: the radius distribution falls sharply above ∼\sim2 R⊕R_{\oplus}, a consequence of any gaseous envelope being stripped by photoevaporation in this irradiation regime (Lundkvist et al., 2016; Fulton et al., 2017). Their proximity to the host further places them close to the tidal disruption limit, which imposes lower bounds on their density (Rappaport et al., 2013).

Their proximity to the host further places them close to the tidal disruption limit, which imposes lower bounds on their density (Rappaport et al., 2013).

Their interest is twofold. They offer direct access to the composition of planetary cores stripped of atmosphere — GJ 367 b, with 0.72​R⊕0.72\,R_{\oplus} and an iron fraction comparable to that of Mercury, is the paradigmatic example (Lam et al., 2021) — and their high transit frequency makes them favourable targets for characterisation. Their occurrence rate peaks around low-mass stars (Sanchis-Ojeda et al., 2014), so that M dwarfs constitute the natural hunting ground. The population remains small: only around a dozen ultra-short-period rocky planets orbiting M dwarfs have both mass and radius determined (Srivastava et al., 2026).

Identifying transits in photometric surveys is an imbalanced classification problem over data volumes that make exhaustive inspection unfeasible. Since the foundational work of Shallue and Vanderburg (2018), convolutional networks have become the reference tool, with successive developments incorporating domain knowledge (Ansdell et al., 2018), adapting to TESS data (Yu et al., 2019; Osborn et al., 2020; Tey et al., 2023), or attaining statistical validation capability (Armstrong et al., 2021; Valizadegan et al., 2022; Valizadegan et al., 2023). In the ultra-short-period regime, the GPFC method combines hardware-accelerated phase folding with convolutional classification (Wang et al., 2024). Recent developments have diversified both architectures and inputs, with transformer-based models applied to full-frame images (Salinas et al., 2025) and classifiers incorporating background flux and centroid information (Tardugno Poleo et al., 2024).

In the ultra-short-period regime, the GPFC method combines hardware-accelerated phase folding with convolutional classification (Wang et al., 2024). Recent developments have diversified both architectures and inputs, with transformer-based models applied to full-frame images (Salinas et al., 2025) and classifiers incorporating background flux and centroid information (Tardugno Poleo et al., 2024).

The declared performance of these systems is remarkably high: AUC values of 0.988 (Shallue and Vanderburg, 2018), 0.999 (Armstrong et al., 2021) and 1.0 (Valizadegan et al., 2022) punctuate the literature. These figures are obtained, for the most part, by evaluating against negative sets built from simulations or from curated eclipsing-binary catalogues.

We argue that this evaluation practice measures a substantially easier problem than the operational one, and that the resulting figures do not predict performance on real data.

The concern is not new. Osborn et al. In the machine-learning literature the phenomenon is characterised: Geirhos et al. That cause, we anticipate, is the blend: genuine eclipses originating in a star other than the target and diluted within the photometric aperture. With a pixel scale of 21 arcsec (Ricker et al., 2015), TESS apertures routinely contain flux from several sources, so that the contaminating signal is indistinguishable from a shallow transit in the flux time series.
